). So they rejoice at this reward and at what Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has added to them of His bounty, which has no limit. The kinds of martyrdom are many: the one slain in battle is a martyr; and she who dies
— that is, a woman who dies in childbirth — is a martyr; and a woman who dies a virgin maiden; and a woman who dies of jealousy — she who bore jealousy patiently until
Allah [cast] terror into the hearts of the unbelievers, so they failed to keep the appointment. Allah praised them with His words:

(Q. 3:185) — the false, which one enjoys a little and which then passes away. This world is the abode of delusion: a scant enjoyment, and it passes away before long; and the hereafter is better and more lasting. What remains is better than what passes away, and this world passes away while the hereafter remains. One of the righteous used to worship by night and by day, never slackening in worship; he would fast the day and stand the whole night in prayer. He was asked: Will you not rest at some times? He said: How long is the life of this world? He was told: seven thousand years. He said:

How long is the Day of Resurrection? It was said: fifty thousand years. He said: Were I to live out the whole span of this world, it would be my duty to strive through all its days, because they are few beside the Day of Resurrection — so what of what comes after it? A human being must die, whether he is righteous or corrupt, and a man is requited for his deed: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil; and the recompense is not in this world — the recompense is in the hereafter.
«and you shall only be paid your wages in full on the Day of Resurrection»
— through the obligatory dues and through blights —

(Q. 3:186) — among the things resolved upon, which are resolved upon because they are obligatory.

— the compact laid upon them in the Torah —

⟨you have praised your brother, you have slaughtered him⟩, and that holds in the case of one who, when he is praised, forgets the shortcomings he knows in himself and attaches himself to the praise of those who praise him. His likeness is one who is told that what comes out of him as excrement has a pleasant smell, and he is content with what he heard and leaves aside what he knows. Whoever, when he is praised, grows proud through the praise and forgets the base (

) attributes and the shortcomings that are in him — that is the one whom praise slaughters. Among them are an elect who, when they are praised, return to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with asking forgiveness and with humility, as our master ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib used to do, or Abū Bakr; when he was praised he would say: ⟨My Lord, make me above what they suppose, and forgive me what they do not know⟩. Praise does no harm to this one. Among them are the perfected, the elect of the elect: they hear praise from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in every condition. Were the praise not issuing from Allah it would not have occurred, and so the perfected rejoice at every praise given them, because they witness it as from al-Ḥaqq, Blessed and Exalted. Those too are not harmed by praise.
«To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is powerful over all things»
(Q. 3:189). Part of that is the punishment of the unbelievers and the deliverance of the believers.

— with the wonders that are in them —

— by coming and going, and by increase and decrease —
(Q. 3:190). This verse was revealed after the verses of Sūrat

al-Baqara. Those are eight verses, and these are three verses, which he abridged because they had come earlier. Whoever reflects on the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day knows the power of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
«Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides»
(Q. 3:191). Those possessed of understanding are those who remember Allah in all their states, standing and sitting

A company of the Companions came in upon ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, with ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar at their head, and they greeted ʿĀʾisha. She said: Who are these people? They said: A company of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; among us is ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar. She said: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar, why is it that you do not visit us often? He said to her: The Messenger ﷺ says:
⟨Visit at intervals and you will be loved the more⟩

. But spare us all this. We have come to ask you about the most wondrous thing you ever saw in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She let her tears flow and said: All his states were wondrous, but the most wondrous thing I saw of him ﷺ is that he came in upon me one night, on my turn, and when he drew near to me he said to me: ʿĀʾisha, will you give me leave to worship Allah, Blessed and Exalted? I said to him:

By Allah, right now I love nothing but to be near you — but I give you leave. So he performed the ablution and stood weeping, weeping, until his tears reached his breast. Then he sat down, then he lay over on his cheek weeping until his tears reached the ground. Bilāl came in to call him to the dawn prayer and saw the state he was in, and said: Do you do this, Messenger of Allah, when Allah has forgiven you what went before of your sin and what came after? He said:
⟨Shall I not then be a thankful servant?⟩
How should I not do it, when this verse was sent down upon me tonight:
«and they reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth»

(Q. 3:191). The reflection of the common people is that they reflect on the creation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, so as to infer the Creator from it. The reflection of the elect is on the Essence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. As for

reflection on the Essence of Allah, that is forbidden to the common people, because they are not able to conceive a modality for the Essence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, which has no where and no how, no foot and no head and no two hands. When a common man reflects on this he makes our Master into a mere melon, and so he falls into what is not praiseworthy. As for the elect, reflection on the Essence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, belongs to them. For this reason it has come down:
⟨An hour’s reflection is better than a year’s worship⟩
⟨An hour’s reflection is better than seven years’ worship⟩
⟨An hour’s reflection is better than seventy years’ worship⟩
. Each station has its own saying.

— this creation that we see, You created it only to point to the perfection of Your power, not in sport —
— declaring You free of all imperfection —

— they sought forgiveness from Allah, Blessed and Exalted —

— upon the tongues of Your messengers, of mercy and of bounty. Their asking for that — even though His promise, Exalted, is not broken — is a request that He make them of those who deserve it, since they were not certain of their deserving it. And the repetition of
«and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Surely You do not break the promise»

(Q. 3:194). He described those who remember Allah, Blessed and Exalted, as making much supplication and as remembering Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The remembrance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is at the beginning with the tongue, then with the heart, then with the spirit. By the remembrance of the tongue he finds annihilation in the acts; by the remembrance of the heart he finds annihilation in the attributes; by the remembrance of the spirit he finds the total annihilation — he is annihilated, then annihilated, then annihilated, and so his annihilation is the very same thing as subsistence. Remembrance has a husk, and a kernel, and a kernel of the kernel. The common people have the husk, and the elect have
the kernel, and the elect of the elect have the kernel of the kernel. The kernel of the kernel is the oil. In any case, there must be much remembrance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
«I do not let the work of any worker among you go to waste, whether male or female; you are of one another»

(Q. 3:195). The occasion of this verse’s revelation is that Umm Salama complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: Why is it that I hear no mention of the women in the hijra and the jihad at all? And he said:
«I do not let the work of any worker among you go to waste, whether male or female; you are of one another»
. The males are from the females and the females from the males. So everything Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has mentioned concerning the men, He has mentioned concerning the women.
«and were driven out of their homes and were harmed in My way»

— I shall cover them over with forgiveness

(Q. 3:195) — the best of recompense. The people of the Garden are those who emigrated from Mecca to Medina, and they are the Muhājirūn, and who
— the unbelievers harmed them, along with the Messenger ﷺ. And the Messenger says:
⟨No prophet was harmed as I have been harmed⟩
, and the meaning of that is: no prophet was purified as I have been purified.
⟨The severest of people in trial are the prophets, then the most like them, then the next most like them⟩
. Those who have purity with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, must have neighbours who harm them; they must

find the harm from those they know and from those they do not know, because that is what purifies them. Man by his nature loves his own kind and his kin, and so if he finds nothing to unsettle him away from these, he goes on loving them, or he goes on apportioning them an ample share of his heart; and Allah loves to have the servant’s heart to Himself alone. And so harm issues to him from every side: from every relative — from a wife, from a child, from a brother — from everyone he would expect and from everyone he would not expect. Then his heart departs, and he knows that the servant has none but Allah, and he flees to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, by rejecting everything other than Him. And when He has perfected him, until He has taken him wholly for Himself, He returns him to them so that he may benefit them, and he is not harmed by their harming him; he does not feel it. — of this world, by concealing them out of fear for their leadership, as others among the Jews do —

(Q. 3:199) — He reckons with creation in the space of half a day of the days of this world. A

made his way to a bathhouse. He was asked: ‘What do you want?’ He said: ‘I want to enter the bathhouse to wash in it.’ The keeper of the bathhouse said to him: ‘No one enters except for a fee.’ So he turned away weeping. They said: ‘This is an old shaykh who has been barred from the bathhouse, and so he simply weeps.’ He said: ‘No, I did not weep because I was barred from the bathhouse; but if the bathhouse, which is the house of

, is not entered except for a fee, then how shall I enter the presence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, except by works?’ And there was one of the righteous whose garment became soiled and he did not wash it; for the whole of his life he never washed his garment. Someone said to him: ‘Your garment is dirty; there is no harm in your washing it.’ He said: ‘If I wash it, it will get dirty a second time.’ He said: ‘You wash it again.’ He said: ‘Then it gets dirty a third time.’ He said: ‘You wash it again.’ He said: ‘Allah did not create me to busy myself with washing clothes; He created me only to worship Him, Blessed and Exalted.’ And there was one of the righteous, a

called al-Ḥaddād, who would take fire in his hand and it would not harm him. He was asked about that, and he said that he had become attached to a woman and had solicited her, and she refused, and said:

‘I have a husband.’ So he waited a while, and her husband died, and he asked to marry her, and she refused, and said: ‘I will not […] my children; rather I will guard my children.’ After a time the woman became poor and fell into need, and she came to him asking him for something that she and her children might eat. He said to her: ‘I will not give you anything unless you consent to me in what I asked of you before.’ She said: ‘Yes.’

So he was alone with her. He handed her the money, and she implored Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and said to him that he should let her go for the sake of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. He said: ‘I have let you go for the sake of Allah.’ She said to him: ‘May Allah deliver you from the Fire.’ He said: ‘From that day the fire of this world does not burn me, and I hope that the fire of the hereafter likewise will not burn me.’ And there was another youth whom a beautiful woman saw, and she made an attempt on him, and he refused. So she adorned her house with all kinds of ornament and perfumed it, and she sent an old woman to the youth, and she invited him, and he answered the invitation and entered the house and saw the ornaments in it and the kinds of perfume. The woman shut the door and solicited him for himself. The youth said: ‘I am now in need of relieving myself, so let me enter the privy.’ So he entered the privy and relieved himself and smeared himself with the excrement, and when he came out smeared with the excrement the woman said: ‘This one is mad,’ and she merely pushed him, and he went out of her house. Then Jibrīl came to him and said to him: ‘Are you Yūsuf?’ And the excrement turned to perfume, so that the scent of musk wafted from him for the whole of his life, on account of that deed.
— in acts of obedience and in afflictions, and against acts of disobedience —

⟨Shall I not tell you of that by which your evil deeds are effaced for you and your degrees are raised? Medinan. One hundred and seventy-five or one hundred and seventy-six verses (āya).
«By Allah's Name: The Entirely Merciful, The Especially Merciful» «O people»
— Ḥawwāʾ, with the lengthening, from a rib among his left ribs —

— Allah created Ādam with His hand and created Ḥawwāʾ from his left rib, and He spread from the two of them many men and many women likewise, with the adjective omitted, as an indication that women’s right is to be covered.
«and fear Allah, by whom you ask one another»

— fear Allah by whom you ask one another: when you ask your brother, you say to him, ‘Give me, for Allah’s sake,’ ‘I adjure you by Allah,’ ‘by the right of Allah’ — among yourselves, where one of you says to another, ‘I ask you by Allah’ and ‘I adjure you by Allah’ —
— and fear severing them. They used also to adjure one another by kinship.
«Indeed Allah is ever watchful over you»

— preserving your deeds and requiting you for them; that is, He has never ceased to be so described (Q. 4:1). In this verse He guided us to godfearing (al-taqwā) and to maintaining the ties of kinship. Kinship (al-raḥim) is derived from al-Raḥmān. al-Ḥaqq says:
⟨Whoever maintains you, I maintain him, and whoever severs you, I sever him!⟩

And the godfearing of Allah, wherever it is mentioned, is compliance with the command and avoidance of the prohibition. As for maintaining the ties of kinship, people differ in that: among them is the rich man, whose maintaining of his kin is by giving of wealth, a gift according to the measure of his means; and whoever is not able to make a gift of any wealth, then service, and visiting, and keeping up contact,

even correspondence by writing — all of this falls within maintaining the ties of kinship. It has come in the hadith that a man may have three days remaining of his life, and when he maintains his kin Allah leaves him thirty years; and a man may have thirty years remaining of his life, and he severs
what is in the tablets of effacement; but as for what is in Umm al-Kitāb, it does not change.
«Indeed Allah is ever watchful over you»
. This verse was revealed concerning an orphan who asked his guardian for his property and he withheld it from him. So the Exalted said:
— the young who have no fathers —
— the lawful. Do not consume the orphan’s property together with your own property; that is mixing the good with the defective.
— the consuming of the property of orphans
«And if you fear that you will not deal justly»
they shrank from the guardianship of orphans; and among them was one who had under him ten or eight wives and would not deal equitably among them.

There was a man who had eight orphan girls in his charge whom he would marry, because marrying them cost him nothing, and he would not give them their due, neither in property nor in the apportioning of nights; and this is wrongdoing. So the Exalted said:
«And if you fear that you will not deal justly»
— that you will not be equitable —
— and so you shrank from their affair — then fear likewise that you will not deal equitably among the women when you marry them:
«such as are good for you among the women»
. So then do not marry the orphan girls for whom you have no
desire; rather, marry such as are good for you among the women.
— if you wish, marry two at a time —
— four at a time — and do not go beyond that. It is permissible for a man to marry
one, or two, or three, or four.
«But if you fear that you will not be equitable»
— this is on condition of equity; so if you fear [that you will act] otherwise than equitably —
since they do not have the rights that wives have.
«And give the women their bridal gifts»

— a bestowal, a gift, out of a willing heart. They used to marry women and not pay them their dowers; and they would give their daughters in marriage and consume what was brought to them of the dower.
«If they willingly remit to you any part of it»
— of praiseworthy outcome; there is no harm for you in it in the hereafter (Q. 4:4).
— the squanderers among men and women and children —

— that is, their property. The orphan, so long as he has not reached a maturity of judgement fitting him to manage his property, so long as he is foolish, the property is not handed over to him. He attached the orphans’ property to the guardians to confirm the care of it.
«which Allah has made for you a means of support»
«and provide for them out of it»
«and clothe them, and speak to them a kindly word»
— promise them a fair promise that you will give them their property when they reach maturity of judgement (Q. 4:5).
— before puberty or after puberty, as to their religion and their management of their affairs —
«until, when they reach [the age of] marriage»

— they become fit for it, by nocturnal emission or by age, which is the completion of fifteen years; this is the school of al-Shāfiʿī, or eighteen years in the school of Mālik, or they attain puberty —
— soundness in their religion and their property —
«then hand over to them their property, and do not consume it»
— hastening to spend it for fear —
— to maturity of judgement, so that you would be obliged to deliver it to them.
— let him keep from the orphan’s property —
«and whoever is poor, let him consume in a seemly manner»
— to the extent of the wage for his work —
«and when you hand over to them»
«their property, then call witnesses over them»
— that they have taken possession of it —
(Q. 4:6) — a keeper of the deeds of His creation and one who brings them to account. It was revealed to rebut the practice of the Jāhiliyya, which gave no inheritance to women or to minors.
the children and the near kin —
«of what the parents and the near kin leave»
«and for women a share of what the parents and the near kin leave, of what is little of it»
determined, so that it must be handed over to them.
«And when the division is attended by»
— the relatives from among those who do not inherit —
«and the orphans and the poor, then provide for them out of it»

(Q. 4:8) — a fair one, by excusing yourselves to them, that you do not own it and that it belongs to minors. Some have said that this is abrogated and some that it is not; but people have made light of leaving it off, and on that view it is a recommendation (
), while from Ibn ʿAbbās it is obligatory.
— let him be afraid for the orphans —
— that is, were close to leaving —
— destitution. The guardians fear that they will die and their children will be left young.
— in the matter of the orphans, and let them do for them what they would wish to be done for their own offspring after them —
— to one whom death has come upon —
correct, by bidding him give in alms less than a third and leave the rest to his heirs, and not leave them destitute.
«Indeed those who consume the property of orphans wrongfully»
«and they will be made to burn»

(Q. 4:10) — a fierce fire in which they burn. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, of the night he was taken on the night journey, that he ﷺ passed by a company of men, each of them having a lip like the lip of a camel, and they were being fed morsels of live coals from the Fire which came out from their backsides. He said, ⟨Who are these?⟩ He said, ⟨These are the devourers of the property of orphans.⟩
The opening of this sura speaks of the two hollow parts, the belly and the private parts, and these two are what most brings people into the Fire. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ says,
⟨Whoever guarantees to me what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I guarantee him the Garden.⟩
that is, the tongue and the private parts. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says,
⟨Guarantee me six things and I will guarantee you the Garden:⟩

⟨Be truthful when you speak; when you promise, do not break it; when you are entrusted, do not betray; guard your hands, lower your eyes, guard your private parts, and enter the Garden in peace.⟩ ʿUmar came in upon Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was pulling at his tongue and striking it. ʿUmar said to him, ⟨Gently, Abū Bakr — may Allah forgive you.⟩ He said, ⟨This has brought me to grievous straits and has brought me into the Fire.⟩ Then they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a man asked:
⟨Will Allah hold us to account for what we say?⟩
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
⟨May your mother be bereaved of you! And does anything cast⟩

⟨people down on their faces in the Fire other than the harvests of their tongues?⟩ ⟨Whoever is protected from the evil of his laqlaq (tongue), his dhabdhab (private parts) and his qabqab (belly) has been protected from all evil.⟩ Whoever is protected from the evil of what is between his jaws and his legs has been protected from all evil.
Do you see the opening of this sura? The whole of it speaks of the two hollow parts — the belly and the private parts. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
⟨I entered the Garden and found most of its people to be the poor, and I entered the Fire and found most of its people to be women⟩

— because they curse much and show ingratitude to their husbands. If you were good to one of them for a long while and then she saw in you something that displeased her, she would say, ‘By Allah, I have never seen any good from you.’ Says

⟨Two kinds of the people of the Fire I have not seen: men with whips in their hands like the tails of cattle, with which they beat people; and women clothed yet naked, deviating and making others deviate, their heads like the leaning humps of Bactrian camels. They will not enter the Garden, nor will they find its scent, and its scent is found from a distance of five hundred years.⟩
Most of the people of the Fire are women, and what most brings men into the Fire is also women.

«And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them; so let them fear Allah, and let them say a right word. Indeed those who consume the property of orphans wrongfully consume only fire in their bellies, and they will be made to burn in a blaze»

— when the two of them are joined with him, he has half the property and they have the half. Someone dies and leaves three children, a male and two daughters: the property is divided into two halves, half for the male, and the remaining half is divided between the two daughters.
— that is, two and whatever is above them —
«they have two-thirds of what he left»
«one, she has the half, and to his parents»
— the two parents of the deceased, the father and the mother —
«to each one of them a sixth of what he left, if he has a child»
— if the deceased left a child, then the parents have the sixth —
«But if he has no child and his parents inherit him»
— only, or together with a spouse —
«But if he has brothers and sisters»
— that is, two or more, male or female —
goes to the father, and nothing to the brothers and sisters.
«after any bequest he may make, or any debt. Your fathers and your sons — you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit»
— in this world and the hereafter. The son does not exclude the father, and the father does not exclude the son, because the wisdom in the inheritance is that whoever has had a
benefit from his property enters the Garden; and as for the deceased, it is not known which of his heirs are the
, the father or the son. For this reason a share is fixed for the father and a share for the son.
«An ordinance from Allah. Indeed Allah is ever knowing»

(Q. 4:11) — in what He has ordained. The questions of the inheritance shares: Allah entrusted them to no prophet and to no angel. He Himself took the division of the inheritance in hand, and that because of people’s miserliness and their greed for property. Had the Messenger been the one who took the division of the inheritance in hand, he would have been accused and treated with enmity, and whoever hates him is wretched with a wretchedness after which there is no felicity ever. And since the apportionment came from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, every one of the heirs was content.
«An ordinance from Allah. Indeed Allah is ever knowing»

. This is the outward inheritance. As for the real inheritance, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says: ⟨We, the company of the prophets, are not inherited from; what we have left behind is alms.⟩ And he said: ⟨The ulama are the heirs of the prophets.⟩ So whoever is born an outward birth has his share of the outward inheritance, and whoever is born a spiritual (
the spiritual inheritance. To it points the saying of ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace: ⟨He who has not been born twice shall not enter the Presence.⟩ The sensory (
«And yours is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child; but if they have a child, then yours is a fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they may make, or any debt»
. In this, the child of the son is joined to the child by consensus.
— that is, the wives, whether they be several or one —
«is a fourth of what you leave, if you have no child; but if you have a child»
«then theirs is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you may make, or any debt. And if a man is inherited from as kalāla»
— he has no child and no parent; this is the explanation of
— that is, the one inherited from as
— by the mother; and Ibn Masʿūd read it so —
«then to each one of the two a sixth»
— that is, the brothers and sisters by the mother —
«then they are sharers in the third»
— in which their male and their female are equal —
«after any bequest made, or any debt, without causing harm»
— without bringing harm upon the heirs —
Allah enjoins upon you an injunction —
— of what He has ordained for His creation in the inheritance shares —

(Q. 4:12) — in deferring the punishment of whoever opposes Him. The sunna has restricted the inheritance of those mentioned to such as have in them no impediment, of killing, or difference of religion, or slavery.
— the rulings mentioned, from the matter of the orphans and what comes after it —
— His ordinances, which He has set as bounds for His servants that they may act by them and not transgress them —
«And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger»

«We shall admit him into gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding therein; and that is the great triumph. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His bounds, We shall admit him»
«into a Fire, abiding therein; and he shall have»
«from among your women, call four of you to witness against them»

. When a man alleges fornication against his wife, he must produce four upright Muslim men who testify that they witnessed the man’s member enter the woman’s private part as the kohl-stick enters the kohl-jar.
— and keep them from mixing with people. This was the prescribed penalty for fornication at the beginning of Islam: they used to be confined and did not mix with people —
(Q. 4:15) — a path to coming out of it. This was at the beginning of Islam. Then, when Allah prescribed flogging, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
⟨Allah has appointed a way for them: the unmarried with the unmarried, a hundred lashes and banishment for a year; and upon the married woman, stoning.⟩
And in the hadith, when he had made the penalty plain, he said:
⟨Take from me, take from me — Allah has appointed a way for them.⟩
— that is, the indecency: fornication or sodomy —
— with reviling and with beating with sandals —
(Q. 4:16) — to him. And this is abrogated by the prescribed penalty.
— the repentance whose acceptance Allah has written upon Himself, by His bounty —
— that is, being ignorant when they disobey their Lord —
— that is, before they come to the death-rattle —
«And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds»
«until, when death comes to one of them»
— and he has entered upon the death-throes —
— upon witnessing what he is in —
— that does not profit him, and it is not accepted from him —
«nor those who die while they are unbelievers»
— likewise, whoever dies before repentance, his repentance is not accepted —
«O you who believe, it is not lawful for you»

. The occasion of this verse’s revelation is what they used to do in the Jāhiliyya. When one of them died, his kinsman came and inherited his wives alone; if he wished, he married them without a bride-gift, and if he wished, he gave them in marriage and took the bride-gift. And when the father died, the son came into his father’s place and married his father’s wife; otherwise he gave her in marriage and took the dower. So the Exalted said:
«O you who believe, it is not lawful for you»
— the persons of the women; they are not inherited —
— prevent your wives from marrying others by keeping hold of them when you have no desire for them, so as to do them harm —
«so that you may take away part of what you have given them»

— with comeliness in speech, in maintenance and in sharing the night. Whoever marries a woman owes the conditions of marriage: maintenance, clothing, lodging, intercourse and good companionship. Whoever omits one of these five, the wife may divorce herself, and nothing is held against her.
«it may be that you dislike a thing and Allah makes in it much good»
(Q. 4:19). When a man marries a woman and stays with her, and after that comes to dislike her, let him be patient in living with her, for in that steadfast patience (

) he finds much good, which is the reward of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; or Allah provides him a righteous child, and that is much good. There was one of the righteous men who married a bad woman, and she kept on injuring him as long as she lived, until she died. When she died he said,

, and resolved that as long as he lived he would not marry women. When he had stayed some days, he saw in a dream that he was in his mosque and the angels were coming down and passing by him, and whenever an angel passed by him it said: ‘Is this the detested one?’ He said: ‘This is the detested one.’ ‘Is this the one who has lost?’ ‘This is the one who has lost.’ He was alarmed, but he was afraid to ask them, and they went on going back and forth like that. Then he could not restrain himself from asking, and said to them: ‘Who is the loser?’ They said to him:

You. The measure of the deeds of the people of the earth was being raised up for you every day and every night for the whole time of your marriage to the woman and her harming you; and when she died that was cut off, and you came to have no deed. So he awoke, and he married three in one day, and it came about that you would not see him
except that he had three or four with him. This is the meaning of
«But if you dislike them, then perhaps you dislike a thing in which Allah has placed much good»
(Q. 4:19). The harm a man finds from the mistress of the house — in that there is much reward for him with Allah; or the much good may be that Allah grants him a righteous child.
«And if you wish to exchange one wife for another»
— taking her in place of the other by divorcing her —
«and you have given one of them»
— much wealth: if you have resolved to part from the woman and you have already given her much in the way of money and household goods —
— do not take anything from the woman after the divorce —
(Q. 4:20) — plain. Why do you take this money, when the money was given in exchange for something?

, for part of the man has reached part of the woman through the intercourse that makes the dower binding; since she has come to stand in this relation to him, and the cause of that was the money, how can you take this money afterwards?
«and they have taken from you a covenant»

(Q. 4:21) — firm; and that is what the woman sees of the man’s love for her at that time. Or the solemn pledge is the stipulation that is stipulated at the contract. At the contracting of the marriage one says
«then retention in kindness or release with good treatment»
(Q. 2:229) — this is a stipulation, and the husband must observe this stipulation: he either retains in kindness or releases with good treatment.
«And do not marry those women whom your fathers married»

. The occasion of the revelation of this verse was that a man died, and his son rose and came and sat beside his wife, wanting to take her as a wife after his father. The woman swore that this would never come about from her: after I have been with your father, it is not possible that I should ever be with you. The son said that he would certainly marry her by force, by inheritance. So the two of them brought their case to the Prophet ﷺ, and there was revealed
«And do not marry those women whom your fathers married»
— a woman whom the father has married, it is not permitted for the son to marry her —
— of your doing: what came before the revelation of the verse is lawful, and after the revelation of the verse this marriage was forbidden —
— a cause for the detestation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, which is the most intense hatred —
The verse named expressly the women
one of whom it is forbidden for a man to marry. It is forbidden for a man to marry his mothers: his mother, and his mother’s mother, and that one’s mother, and that one’s mother, on up.
— this takes in the daughters of one’s children, however far down: the man’s daughter, and the daughters of his children, and the daughters of those, and the daughters of those, to the end of time.
— from the side of the father or of the mother, likewise: every woman between you and whom there is a sibling bond from the side of the father or of the mother.
— the sisters of your fathers and of your grandfathers.
— the sisters of your mothers and of your grandmothers.
«And the daughters of the brother and the daughters of the sister»
— and their offspring are included among them.
«And your mothers who have suckled you»
— and the mother who suckled the man before the completion of the two years —
— and joined to that, by the sunna, are their daughters.
«And the mothers of your wives, and your stepdaughters»
, and she is the wife’s daughter by a man other than him —

— whom you rear: a description that accords with what is usually the case, so it carries no counter-implication. What is usual is that the stepdaughter is in his care; but even if she is not in his care, the stepdaughter is forbidden.
«of your wives to whom you have gone in»
— the stepdaughter who is forbidden is the stepdaughter whose mother the man has gone in to —
«but if you have not gone in to them»
— if the man has contracted marriage with the woman’s mother and has not gone in to her —
«then there is no blame upon you»
— it is permitted for him to divorce the mother and marry the daughter, if she accepts —
«and the wives of your sons who are of your loins»
— when a son of one’s own loins has married a woman, she is forbidden to the father —
«and that you should join together two sisters»
— whether by lineage or by suckling, in marriage —
— what came before, in the Jāhiliyya, of joining together two sisters: that is lawful —
— of what has passed from you before the prohibition —
(Q. 4:23). Allah has never forbidden anything in the Qurʾan and excepted what had already passed, save in two cases:
«And do not marry those women whom your fathers married»
«and that you should join together two sisters»
(Q. 4:23). The reason for this is that these two cases occurred among certain of the forefathers of

the Prophet ﷺ. Kināna married his father’s wife, and among the forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ there was one who joined together two sisters. Had it been forbidden and what had already passed not been excepted, this would have touched something of the honour of the Prophet ﷺ; but since the Prophet ﷺ is inviolate in his person, what came before the revelation of the verse is lawful, so that nothing should touch any part of the Prophet ﷺ. This is the wisdom (al-ḥikma) in this exception. These women — marrying them is forbidden. O Allah, bless our master Muhammad.
«And married women among women, except those whom your right hands possess»

Allah has forbidden a man to marry the married women — that is, women who have husbands. A woman who is under a man: marrying her is forbidden. That is to guard the Muslim against sharing a woman with another, for this is not manly virtue (
«except those whom your right hands possess»

— except where it so happens that a man has taken captive a woman who has a husband: he has the strength to take possession of her without sharing her, and for this reason she has become lawful to him by ownership after the period of ascertainment (

). These are fourteen or fifteen among the women whom He has forbidden in marriage; and the sunna appended the sister through suckling, and affinity, and the joining of a woman together with her maternal aunt, and of a woman together with her paternal aunt. Those who did not accept this disallowed the abrogation of the Qurʾan by a report of single transmission (

— not committing fornication. When He had mentioned fourteen women, or fifteen, He made clear that He has made lawful what is other than that; and this making-lawful is perpetual in one class and not perpetual in another, just as the forbidden women are of classes. There is the woman whose prohibition is perpetual, and that is what has been mentioned of the women; and it is forbidden to marry the woman irrevocably divorced, and this prohibition is not perpetual — only until after [another] husband; and the woman who has a husband, only until after the divorce; and the woman in her waiting period, until her waiting period expires; and the second sister, until her sister is divorced; and the fifth, until the fourth is divorced. This prohibition is not perpetual.
— of those you have married, by intercourse —
their dowers which you have appointed for them —
«as a prescribed obligation; and there is no blame upon you in what you have mutually agreed»
— by remitting it, or part of it, or adding to it. Additions [to the dower] in marriage: whenever the husband and the wife agree together, there is no harm in that.
«And whoever among you is not able [to afford] means»
«the believing ones, then from those whom your right hands possess»
— then let him marry the slave women —
«And Allah knows best your faith; you are of one another»
. Faith is a condition in marrying slave women, and faith is of the heart; for this reason He, Glorified and Exalted, mentioned

. So be content with its outward signs and commit the inward secrets to Him, for He is the one who knows them in detail. Many a slave woman surpasses the free woman. This is a reassurance concerning the marriage of slave women. Marrying the slave woman — the slave woman of another — is permitted if a person is unable to marry a free woman and fears hardship (

). And patience is better than marrying the slave woman, because you consign your child to slavery. This is the position of Mālik: that whoever is unable to marry a free woman and fears hardship may marry slave women. The position of al-Shāfiʿī is that nothing is stipulated in marrying slave women; he explained marriage as intercourse alone — if you are not able to have intercourse with free women at the time, and you have no free woman whom you may marry, then there is no harm in marrying the slave woman.
«So marry them with the permission of their people»
— intimates who fornicate with them in secret —
«And when they are taken in wedlock»
— they are given in marriage, that is, they marry —
«then upon them is half of what is upon the chaste women»
— the free women, the virgins, when
), so they are given fifty lashes and banished for half a year; and male slaves are reckoned by analogy with them. He did not make being in wedlock (
) a condition for the penalty to be due, but in order to convey that there is no stoning upon them at all.
— the marriage of slave women when the means are lacking —

— unlike the one among the free men who does not fear it, for whom marrying her is not lawful; and likewise one who is able [to afford] the means for a free woman. Al-Shāfiʿī holds this. Excluded by His words
are the unbelieving women: marrying them is not lawful for him even if he lacks [the means] and fears.
«And that you be patient is better for you»
— so that the child does not become a slave —

He, Blessed and Exalted, gave in this verse the ruling of marriage, what is lawful and what is forbidden. People differ over marriage according to the difference of their ranks: it is obligatory for one who is strong and of intense craving for desire — for such a one it is obligatory that he marry; and it is recommended (

) in the case of the moderate man; and it is forbidden in the case of one unable to perform the act, or unable [to provide] maintenance and the dower. And when a person wishes to marry, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says:
⟨Take for yourself the one who has religion.⟩

He is to choose, truly, the women of religion, the daughters of the righteous; and the virgin is to be chosen, because the virgin is more sincere in love. They said: as for the woman married before, if you marry her and she has no child by another, then half her heart is yours and the remaining half is the first husband's; and if she has a child from before you, then you have nothing of her — half her heart is for the first husband and the second half for the child; she consumes your provision and, more often than not, treats you as an enemy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned:
⟨Made beloved to me, of this world of yours, are women and perfume; and the delight of my eye is in the prayer.⟩

Women, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finds in his wives a help toward conveying the message; and every married man finds help from his wife in establishing the religion. Even if it were nothing but that she spares him the grinding and the kneading and the cooking and the washing and the sweeping of the house and the care of the child — all of this, had the man undertaken it himself, would have occupied him away from his religion. So the woman is not of this world; rather she is a help toward religion in the case of the Muslim. For this reason they said that the righteous woman is not of this world. And for this reason the Messenger said:
⟨Made beloved to me, of this world of yours, are women and perfume; and the delight of my eye is in the prayer.⟩
In the woman there is the beautiful face that reminds him of the beauty (

) of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and in perfume there is the sweet scent, and its origin is from the Garden. So all of this was made beloved to him — but the delight of his eye is in the prayer. He did not say that the delight of his eye is by the prayer, but that the delight of his eye is in the prayer. The state (
) that he finds in the prayer is what his eye is delighted by ﷺ, not the prayer itself, the place of intimate converse:
«Allah wishes to make clear to you»
— the laws of your religion and what is in the interest of your affair —
«and to guide you to the ways of those before you»
— the paths of the prophets in what is made lawful and what is made forbidden —
— He brings you back from His disobedience, in which you were, to His obedience —
(Q. 4:26) — in what He has ordained for you.
«And Allah wishes to relent toward you»
— He repeated it in order to build upon it —
«and those who follow the desires wish»
— the Jews, the Christians, the Magians and the fornicators —
«that you should deviate with a great deviation»
«Allah wishes to lighten [the burden] for you»
— He makes the rulings of the shariʿa easy for you —
(Q. 4:28) — he cannot be patient away from women and the desires. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, mentioned in this verse that He wishes four things for us, by His bounty, Blessed and Exalted:
He wishes to make clear to us the shariʿa; and He wishes to guide us to the straight path; and He wishes to relent toward us; and He wishes to
«And those who follow the desires wish»

— a faction of Quraysh who used to find fault with the ruling of the shariʿa. They would say: the Qurʾan has forbidden you your paternal aunts and your maternal aunts, yet you have married the daughters of the paternal aunts and the daughters of the maternal aunts; so on this reckoning marrying the daughters of the sister and the daughters of the brother is lawful — they are alike. The daughters of the sister are forbidden in the Qurʾan, and the paternal aunts are forbidden, yet you have married the daughter of the paternal aunt and you have married the daughter of the maternal aunt; so how have you forbidden the brother's daughter and the sister's daughter?
«And those who follow the desires wish that you should deviate with a great deviation»

(Q. 4:27). These are the ones who wished deviation for you, and Allah wished guidance for you. He wished four things for us: that He make clear to us the shariʿa — it is plain, its night like its day; and He wished to guide us to the straight path, which is the path to Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and He wished to accept repentance from us, so that we return to Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and He wished to lighten [the burden] for us — and this is the greatest blessing upon us. He placed the lightening upon Muhammad ﷺ and upon his community, so that their journeying came to be by assistance (
), as the journeying of those before us was by their own effort (
«I am going to my Lord; He will guide me»
(Q. 37:99) — so the going, on Ibrāhīm's part, was

(Q. 4:28), because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created things differing one from another. The angel is luminous: his life is in worship alone, and he continues in that and does not change. Beasts and animals — their life is in their appetites alone, and they do not change from that. And He created man weak, such that he cannot hold to one state; and so, through his weakness, he reached the highest station. Man, since he is weak, you find him at one time following appetite as though he were a beast; at one time he eats and at one time he marries and drinks; at one time he is angry and at one time he schemes; and at one time he prays and remembers Allah and devotes himself to worship as though he were an angel. This changing is in none but man. The angel cannot turn about into the state of the animals, and the animals cannot turn about into the state of the angel, while man is at one time an angel and at one time an animal. Because of man's weakness he cannot hold to one state, for the thing he loves most is eating: if the food is set before you and you begin to eat, half an hour does not pass before you are unable to eat. Drinking is likewise, and the appetite for women is likewise. If you stand, standing defeats you; and if you sit, you cannot keep on sitting; if you lie down on your side, you cannot keep on at that; if you sleep, you are unable to sleep on, and if you wake, you are unable to stay awake. Whatever man does, he does not continue in it but that he is unable to do it, because of his weakness. So, for this weakness, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, aided him, until he became the best of creation. Allah says: ⟨I am a king, living, who does not die. Son of Ādam, if you obey Me I will make you a king, living, who does not die⟩. By that he becomes the best of creation. And by this weakness too man is corrupted, until he becomes the worst of creation, because he cannot hold to one state: if he commits an indecency he passes from it to another indecency, and passes from that, and man never wearies; he does no evil but that he wishes to do an evil worse than that, until he becomes the worst of creation. So for this reason man is described as the best of creation and described as the worst of creation — this because of his weakness. This weakness is praise in the case of one whom Allah loves and blame in the case of one whom Allah, Blessed and Exalted, hates.

(the soul) is its attachment to this world and its greed for it, because this world — her sons, who busy themselves with her, she must needs kill them to the last of them. ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace, was travelling, and with him was a Jew who claimed that he believed in him. ʿĪsā took three loaves and loaded them on the Jew. When the journey grew long the Jew stole one of them and ate it. When midday came ʿĪsā called him and said to him:

[Bring] the food. So he brought two loaves. ʿĪsā said to him: Where is the third? He said: I did not see it — he swore that he had not seen the third loaf. A gazelle passed by. ʿĪsā said to him: Tell this gazelle to come to me; say to it: Answer the Spirit of Allah. So he said: O gazelle, answer the Spirit of Allah. The gazelle came and lay down. He said to him: Slaughter it. So he slaughtered it. He said to him: Kindle a fire. So he kindled a fire and roasted, and the two of them ate. When they had eaten until they were full, ʿĪsā said to it: Rise, by the permission of Allah. So it rose and went away. The Jew said: This is a wonder. He said to him: By the right of the One who did this for us, where is the third loaf? He said: I did not see it. They went on and came to a sea. He said to him: This is a sea before us; what is to be done? He said: This we cannot cross except by ship. He said to him: Close your eyes. So he closed his eyes, and there the two of them were beyond the sea — they had crossed the sea. He said: Glory be to Allah, this is a wonder. He said: By the right of the One who did this for us, where is the loaf? He said: I did not see it. So they went on and found three heaps of gold, and the two of them sat down. ʿĪsā said to him: This is some gold for us; let us divide it between us — a part for me, and a part for you, and a part for whoever ate the bread. He said to him: I am the one who ate it. ʿĪsā said: Fie on you! All the signs you saw did not move you to tell the truth, and this world moves you to truthfulness. Take the heaps, all of them. And ʿĪsā went away from him. He remained sitting by the heaps of gold, unable to carry them and unable to go away from them; so he just sat by them. When night fell three men came and said: What are you doing here? He said: This gold is mine, and I am sitting here guarding it. So they killed him and took the gold — they were three, each of them took a heap. They sat until the morning, and hunger hurt them. They said: Let us send one of us to a village to buy us food for us to eat. So they sent one of them. When he had gone the two men took counsel together; they said: When so-and-so comes, let us kill him before we eat, and the gold will remain for us, the two of us. And when he went to the market he bought food and said: I shall put poison in it; when my two companions eat it they will die, and the gold will remain for me. So he put the poison in the food and returned to the two men; and when he set the food down they killed him there and then, and ate, and they died too. So ʿĪsā came back
and found all four dead beside the gold. He said: This is what this world does to its children.

) forbids coveting what Allah has given to a person other than you; and that is because a man's felicity falls into three divisions: a felicity of the soul, such as intelligence and knowledge and the sciences, in quantity and in quality, and chastity and courage and generosity — all these are traits of character that attach to a man's soul; and a division of them is bodily, such as health and length of life, what attaches to a man's body; and [a division] external, such as many children and property and friends and brethren and good repute and people's love for the person, and other things besides. So when a man looks at a man with whom these things are abundant while he himself has nothing of them, either he wishes to obtain what the man has, or he wishes those blessings to pass away from the man. If he wishes them to pass away, that is envy; and if he wishes that there come to him the like of what has come to the man, that is emulation, and it is not an act of disobedience — except that the Qurʾan has forbidden us to covet what another man has in every case,

so then, let no one covet what another has. Do not say: O Allah, give me a house like so-and-so's house, and property like so-and-so's property, and a wife like his wife. It may be that a thing is good with one man and, when it is with another, is evil. There is many a one who had much property and his religion was sound, and if this property passed over to the one coveting it his religion would be corrupted. So then, let a man not covet what another has; rather let him ask Allah of His bounty. Let him ask Allah for that in which lies the soundness of his religion and of his world and of his hereafter.
And when you look into this you find that the supplication (

«Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the hereafter, and guard us from the punishment of the Fire»

So then, if you wish to look, look at the one beneath you — that is more conducive to thanksgiving — and do not look at the one above you — that is more conducive to envy and discontent. until you are like him; and do not look to the one who is below you, lest you see yourself to be in a praiseworthy state. One class embraced Islam and did righteous work and died in that state; they are of the people of the Garden by consensus. And a class disobeyed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and repented and sought forgiveness for their sins; those are of the people of the Garden by consensus. And a class disobeyed and died before repenting; concerning those there is disagreement. The Murjiʾa say that acts of disobedience do a believer no harm — he simply enters the Garden — and that all the threatening in the Qurʾan is only in respect of the unbelievers, while as for whoever has merely believed, he is safe from all the threatening. And a party says that whoever has committed a grave sin has gone out of Islam; so whoever has committed

a grave sin is of the people of the Fire. The people of the sunna do not put a Muslim out of Islam on account of a grave sin; so if a Muslim commits a grave sin and dies before repenting, his affair rests with Allah. The truth in this is what the people of the sunna have said, on the evidence of this verse:
«Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, and He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills»

(Q. 4:48). That rests with the will: if He wills, He admits him to the Garden without punishment; and if He wills, He punishes him and then admits him to the Garden after a time. All of that rests with Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The Muslims who have committed grave sins until they have merited entry into the Fire — when they enter the Fire they are not like the unbelievers in the Fire. The face that has prostrated itself to Allah never enters the Fire. Among them is one whose two feet are in the Fire while his person stands clear of the Fire, and among them one up to his knee, and among them one up to his backbone, and among them one up to his neck; but as for the face that has prostrated itself to Allah, the Fire does not touch it. These are the ones who, once they have been punished — after a day, or after days, or after a year, or after years — will come out of the Fire and enter the Garden. The last of the people of the Fire to come out of the Fire comes out and stands before Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and says: ⟨My Lord, take me to the gate of the Garden, and I shall ask nothing of You but this.⟩ So he makes a covenant with Allah that if he reaches the gate of the Garden that will suffice him, and he gives such covenants and compacts as he gives. Then the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says: ⟨Bring him near to the Garden.⟩ And when he is at the gate of the Garden and looks upon what the Garden holds of bliss and of the wide-eyed maidens (

), he waits a long while and says: ⟨My Lord, admit me to the Garden, though I have no share of it.⟩ So He admits him to the Garden. And he waits a time and says: ⟨My Lord, give me of the bliss of the Garden.⟩ It is said to him: ⟨Did you not give covenants and compacts that you would ask for nothing but what you were given?⟩ He says: ⟨My Lord, let me not be the least of Your servants in portion from You.⟩ Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ⟨Make a wish. Would it content you if I gave you⟩
⟨ten times the measure of the world, in the Garden?⟩
At that the Messenger ﷺ laughed. He said:
⟨No — I am able to do all things; I have given you ten times the measure of the world.⟩
This is the least of the people of the Garden in fortune.
«And whoever associates partners with Allah has forged a sin»
— and they are the Jews. This verse came down concerning Ḥuyayy b. Akhṭab and Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf, who praised themselves, saying: We are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones.
— He purifies whom He wills, through faith (

⟨Did you not claim that you would ask Me for nothing besides it? Woe to you, son of Adam, how treacherous you are! And he does not cease to supplicate, and He says: Perhaps, if I give you that, you will ask Me for something besides it. He says: No, by Your might, I will not ask You for anything besides it. He says: O my Lord, do not make me the most wretched of Your creation. And he does not cease to supplicate until He laughs, and when He laughs at him He gives him leave to enter it. And when he has entered it, it is said to him: Wish for such-and-such; and he wishes. Then it is said to him: Wish for such-and-such; and he wishes, until the wishes are exhausted for him. Then He says to him: This is yours, and the like of it with it.⟩
⟨and that man is the last of the people of the Garden to enter it.⟩
«and that suffices as a manifest sin»
«those who were given a portion of the Book, believing in al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt»

(Q. 4:51). It was revealed concerning Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf and Ḥuyayy b. Akhṭab; they were the chiefs of the Jews. When the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina the Illumined they made a covenant with the Messenger ﷺ that they would not make war on him and he would not make war on them, and that if they met with a case that needed help the Muslims would help them and they would help the Muslims, as with blood-money and the like. When the day of Badr came and the Muslims were victorious they said: This is the Prophet who is mentioned in the Torah; and they confirmed their covenant with the Messenger ﷺ. And when the day of Uḥud came in the following year they doubted, and said: After what has befallen the Muslims we do not know whether this is the Prophet who is to come at the end of time or not. So a company of them rode to Mecca and said to Abū Sufyān: Let us make a pact with you to fight Muhammad ﷺ. He said to them: I do not trust you, because you are People of a Book and he is the possessor of a Book; he is nearer to you than we are. They said: No, he is the most hostile of our enemies, and we will fight him alongside you. Abū Sufyān said to them: I will accept nothing from you unless you prostrate to the idol: al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt.

So they prostrated to al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt, and they were learned men, out of envy of the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims. Abū Sufyān said to them: I set my religion before you and I set the religion of Muhammad before you, and you are People of a Book, learned men; judge between us and Muhammad: are we better than he in religion, or is he better than we in religion? We give the pilgrims drink, we feed the guest, we ransom the captive; and Muhammad has severed kinship, parted from the Sanctuary, and brought a religion at variance with the religion of our fathers. They said: You are more rightly guided in the way than Muhammad ﷺ; your religion is more rightly guided than the religion of Muhammad. Allah Exalted said:
«Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, believing in al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt»
two idols of Quraysh. Learned men who took to prostrating to the idol out of envy, and out of love of this world and nothing else.
— to Abū Sufyān and his companions —
«are more rightly guided in the way than those who believe»
is more rightly guided than the religion of the Muslims.
«Those are they whom Allah has cursed; and whoever Allah curses, you will never find for him any helper»
(Q. 4:52) — any to ward off His punishment —
«Or have they a share in the dominion?»
— nay, they have nothing of the dominion; the Jews do not attain dominion, because of their envy —
«for then they would not give the people a speck»
(Q. 4:53) — some paltry thing, the measure of the notch on the back of a date-stone, so excessive is their miserliness. They combined envy and miserliness.
«for what Allah has given them of His bounty»
— they envied al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ and the Muslims for the bounty of Allah, which is prophethood and the multitude of wives; and they say: Had he been a prophet he would have been too occupied for women.
«for We gave the family of Ibrāhīm»
— [Ibrāhīm being] his forefather — such as Mūsā, Dāwūd and Sulaymān —
«and We gave them a mighty dominion»

(Q. 4:54). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, bestowed favour upon the family of Ibrāhīm, such as Mūsā, Dāwūd and Sulaymān. Mūsā was king of Egypt and Syria after the destruction of Firʿawn, and he was a prophet; and Dāwūd was a king and a prophet; and Sulaymān was a king who ruled the whole world, and a prophet. The One who gave this — was it not for Him to give Muhammad ﷺ prophethood and the wives he had?
«and We gave them a mighty dominion»

. Dāwūd had ninety-nine wives, and Sulaymān a thousand, between free women and concubines. In the shariʿa of Mūsā marriage was without limit of number, and for this reason Dāwūd married ninety-nine women, making them up to a hundred. And Sulaymān said: By Allah, I shall go in tonight to a hundred women, every one of them conceiving and bringing forth a horseman who will wage jihad in the way of Allah. And he forgot to say
. So he went in to them all, and none conceived but one, and she brought forth half a human being. And Sulaymān had a thousand women: three hundred

free women and seven hundred slave-girls; and the Messenger had only eleven. They envy him for this, while the prophets before him had this number and it did not debar them from their prophethood? This is the envy of the Jews. They combined miserliness and envy. Miserliness is that you withhold your property from another; envy is that you withhold from him the bounty of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The miser withholds his own bounty from another, while the envier, for his part, wants the bounty of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to be withheld from His servant. So Allah withheld dominion from them: they have no share in the dominion, because of their envy. This is why they say: the envious man will never rule. The envious man will never rule — why? Because man has been moulded to hate following another. A man obeys another man only for some cause that makes it preferable for him to be his follower, either provision that comes to him from him, or some bounty. So since Allah, Blessed and Exalted, who is the Fashioner of creation, has made His bounty run upon His creation and has thereby deserved worship from them, the envier who wants to cut off this bounty wants to depose Allah, Blessed and Exalted; because when human beings are certain that nothing comes to them from Allah, they see no reason to obey Him. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave an outward dominion to some people and an inward dominion to some people, and joined the two dominions in some people. The outward dominion is that of one who was a king over this world; and the inward dominion is the dominion of the
(the friends of Allah) and the ulama, which is inward. And whoever joined the two things, a king outwardly and a
inwardly, or a prophet, has joined the two dominions. Among the prophets there is one who is a prophet and a king; and among the
there is one who is a
and a king; and among them there is one who is only a
«That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He will, and Allah is the possessor of mighty bounty»
«So some of them believed in him»
«and some of them turned away from him»
— turned aside from him and did not believe —
«Indeed those who disbelieved in Our signs, We shall soon roast them»
«their skins, We give them in exchange other skins»
— by their being restored to their first state, unburnt —
— that they may suffer its severity —
The unbeliever's frame is enlarged until the span between his shoulders is a distance of seventy years, and his molar is greater
than Mount Uḥud, so that the Fire may have full power to burn him. When they are burnt until they become charcoal, Allah restores them as they were.
is not [to be taken] in its own meaning;
means that they are restored to their [former] state, not that they are exchanged for skins other than them, because Allah does not punish a skin that has not disobeyed Him.
«And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We shall admit them to gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding therein forever; they shall have therein purified spouses»
— purified of menstruation and of every filth —
«and We shall admit them into a deep shade»
(Q. 4:57) — lasting; a shade that no sun effaces, which is the shade of the Garden. The Messenger ﷺ says:

⟨And the shade of a single tree — the rider travels in it more than a hundred years and does not reach its end. Recite, if you wish:⟩

) was revealed at the conquest of Mecca, when ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, took the key of the Kaʿba by force from ʿUthmān b. Ṭalḥa al-Ḥajabī, its custodian. When the Prophet ﷺ came to Mecca in the year of the conquest, he had refused him, and said:

, so the Messenger ﷺ ordered that it be given back to him, and said:

. He marvelled at that, and he [the Prophet ﷺ] recited the verse to him, and he accepted Islam. Then, at his death, he gave it to his brother Shayba, and it has remained among his descendants to this day. Although the verse came down on a particular occasion, its generality holds, by the indication of the plural.
«Indeed Allah commands you to render back the trusts to their owners»
— Allah commands His servants to render the trusts back to their owners —

— rendering the trust and judging with justice —
(Q. 4:58) — of what is done. The trust is of [several] kinds: a kind between the servant and his Lord, a kind between the servant and his

(the soul), and a kind between the servant and [other] creatures. The trust between you and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and that you comply with His command and avoid what He has forbidden. The trust between you and your
is that you not employ it in what harms it in your hereafter. When the

clings to something in which lies its harm, justice is that you employ it in that in which lies its safety in this world and the hereafter. And the trust between you and creatures: the nearest of creatures to you are wives and children, and you must discharge the trust concerning them. The child — you must give him a good name, and teach him the Book of Allah when he reaches the age of discernment, and teach him the religion, then command him to worship Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and when he comes of age, you marry him. And everyone who entrusts you with something — that you not betray him in his trust.

— for you than disputing and speaking by [mere] opinion —

He said: Yes. So ʿUmar killed him.

— who will take charge of our affairs —

— from fighting the unbelievers, when they sought it at Mecca —

— why did You not grant us respite —

— of the good and the evil —

(Q. 4:80) — a keeper of their deeds; rather, a warner —

and rouse their desire for it —

— a proper name for the Divine Majesty —

(Q. 4:87) — there is no uncertainty in it.

«And on the Day the Hour comes, on that Day they will be divided»

(Q. 30:14), and a party in a seat of truth with an Omnipotent Sovereign. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has multiplied the mention of Himself in order to call the servant to abundant remembrance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. So there must be remembrance of Allah with the tongue first, then remembrance with the heart, then remembrance with the spirit; and at that point His being engulfs the being of all that is other than He, and the servant passes away and being passes away, and the true
(the divine oneness) and the everlasting life are attained.
«He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection»

(Q. 4:87). The Resurrection is of three ranks: lesser, middle and greater. The lesser is the death of a man — whoever dies, his resurrection has come upon him. The middle is the death of all creatures at the first blast. The greater is the raising of the creatures and their gathering to the Day of Resurrection at the second blast. He has sworn that He must gather the creatures, and when He gathers them He must divide them: a party in the Garden, a party in the Blaze, and a party in a seat of truth with an Omnipotent Sovereign.
«And who is more truthful than Allah in speech»
(Q. 4:87) — in word. This is a report that has come to us from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and no one is more truthful than He

in speech. Every reporter — doubt finds its way into his report, whether it is true or a lie — except He, Blessed and Exalted: no doubt finds its way into His report; rather it is true. For that reason He mentioned that He is the most truthful of speakers. And so it has come in the hadith that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ⟨The son of Ādam has called Me a liar, and it is not for him to call Me a liar; and he has reviled Me, and it is not for him to revile Me. As for his calling Me a liar, it is his saying, 'He will not bring me back after death' — and I originated him, and the bringing back is easier than the originating. As for his reviling Me, it is his saying, 'Allah has taken a son' — and I am the One, the Unique, the Eternally Self-Sufficient; I have not begotten, nor was I begotten, and there is none equal to Me.⟩.
«What is the matter with you, that you are two parties concerning the hypocrites?»

— what is your affair, that you have become —
) and acts of disobedience. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, decreed upon them that they should turn back from the jihad and join the unbelievers, because of their earning unbelief and disobedience.

— that is, to count them among the guided —
«And whomever Allah leads astray, you will never find for him a way»

— they disbelieved and wished for your unbelief —
«so do not take allies from among them»
— whom you befriend — even if they make a show of faith —

(Q. 4:89) — a sound emigration that makes their faith real. Emigration was a condition of faith at the beginning of Islam, so whoever claimed faith and did not emigrate after the emigration of the Messenger ﷺ was a liar, until it was abrogated at the conquest of Mecca by his saying ﷺ: ⟨There is no emigration after⟩
⟨the conquest⟩. The hypocrites — the Muslims differed about them: some of them said that they are unbelievers, and some of them say that they are Muslims.
«And Allah has thrown them back by what they earned»

(Q. 4:88). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the One who turned them back to unbelief. So the deed was in reality from Allah, Blessed and Exalted — since He is the creator of the servant and of his acts — and figuratively from the servant. From here the two factions parted: the Jabriyya and the Qadariyya. The Jabriyya say: the servant has no act at all; all acts are the acts of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and so there is no sin upon the servant and nothing at all, because he has no deed. And they went astray because they did away with the obligations of the Law. The Qadariyya said: the servant is the creator of his own acts, the servant is able to create his acts, and so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has no entry into the acts of the servant. So they fell into unbelief by ascribing the act to other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The people of the Sunna took hold of a lesser compulsion: they say that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave us power over acquisition, so the acquisition is ours and Allah creates the deed at the moment of acquisition. And
(those who know Allah) joined together the two creeds of the two errant factions, and so were guided to the evenness of the path (

). In reality they see the act as belonging to none but Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and this is not the doctrine of the Jabriyya in their view, but rather, by witnessing and plain sight, there is no agent in existence save Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And even so, outwardly they take upon themselves righteous deeds and avoid evil deeds as though they were the creators of their own deeds. So they brought out a result lying between the two traits: from between dung and blood they brought out pure milk, and that is the straight path. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has ascribed the act sometimes to Himself and sometimes to another.
«Say: the angel of death, who has been charged with you, will take you»
«Allah takes the souls at the time of their death»

(Q. 39:42). The causing of death is in reality from Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and since He commanded the angel to carry out this command and the angel performed it, the angel was the one who took [the soul], while the one who takes it in reality is Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

And the servant too: when Allah created him and manifested Himself in him, He placed in him strength, intellect, knowledge and discernment, by which he is able to acquire a righteous deed and to avoid by it an evil deed; and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the One who carries out the creating [of the act]. This is the straight path. Whoever says that the act belongs to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has spoken truly; and whoever attributes the act to its doer figuratively — the Qurʾan has spoken with the like of this.
«Do you wish to guide him whom Allah has led astray?»

(Q. 4:88). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the One who led astray whoever went astray. The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨Allah sent Satan as one who makes [falsehood] alluring, and nothing of the leading astray is in his hands; and He sent me as a caller to guidance, and nothing of the guidance is in my hands.⟩
«They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved»
(Q. 4:89). Whoever wishes that someone be an unbeliever is as though he were an unbeliever himself, because he has loved unbelief, even if for any person at all.
«so that you would be alike. So do not take allies from among them»
«until they emigrate in the way of Allah»
— and persist in what they are upon —
«and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them any ally»
(Q. 4:89) — by whom you gain victory over your enemy.
«to a people between whom and you there is a covenant»
— a pact of security for them, as the Prophet ﷺ made a covenant with Hilāl b. ʿUwaymir al-Aslamī —

(Q. 4:90) — along with you — that is, holding back from fighting you and from fighting them. So do not approach them with capture or killing; and this and what comes after it is abrogated by the verse of the sword
— their being given power over you —
«He would have given them power over you»
but He did not will it, and so He cast terror into their hearts.
«So if they withdraw from you and do not fight you and offer you peace»
«then Allah has given you no way against them»
(Q. 4:90) — a road, by capture and killing.
«You will find others wishing to be secure from you»
— by showing faith in your presence —
«and to be secure from their own people»
— by unbelief, when they return to them; and they are Asad and Ghaṭafān —
«every time they are returned to temptation»
they fall in with the severest falling.
«So if they do not withdraw from you»
— and do not offer you peace —
«and kill them wherever you overtake them»
«and those — We have given you against them a clear warrant»
(Q. 4:91) — a clear and manifest proof for killing them and taking them captive, because of their treachery.
«It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake»
(Q. 4:92). The occasion of the revelation of this verse (

) is that ʿAyyāsh b. Abī Rabīʿa, the brother of Abū Jahl by his mother, became a Muslim; and when he became a Muslim his mother said that she would not take shelter in any shade, nor eat, nor drink, until he turned back from Islam. So Abū Jahl travelled out with al-Ḥārith, a companion of his, and the two came to ʿAyyāsh and said to him: we have agreed with you about your Islam, but the Messenger ﷺ commands the keeping of the ties of kinship; so since the Messenger commands the keeping of the ties of kinship, come with us and keep the tie of kinship with your mother, and we will leave you upon your religion. And he accepted that. Then when they had taken him away, they seized him and bound his arms behind him, and Abū Jahl struck him a hundred lashes, and his companion struck him a hundred lashes likewise. So he said to al-Ḥārith:
⟨This one is my brother, my mother's son; he has struck me. But you — why do you strike me a hundred lashes? By Allah, I shall not meet you alone without killing you.⟩

After that al-Ḥārith went to Medina and entered Islam, and ʿAyyāsh returned and met him on the road alone and did not know of his becoming a Muslim, so he set upon him with the sword and killed him. Then he came to the Messenger ﷺ and said to him:
⟨I killed him before I knew of his becoming a Muslim, and after that it became clear to me⟩
«It is not for a believer to kill a believer»
— it is not fitting that a killing of him should issue from him —
— being mistaken in his killing of him.

«who is a believer, and a blood-money delivered»
) is what is paid to the heirs of the slain —
unless they give it to him as a charitable gift, by pardoning it. And the sunna has made clear that the blood-money is a hundred camels: twenty she-camels in their second year (

— a pact, like the protected peoples (

— the slave, in that he lacks one and lacks what he might obtain one with —

that the servant set his own soul free from whatever

is other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and failing that, he keeps to abandoning food and drink and renounces this world and its desires, until he finds a purification from Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
