(Q. 4:93). This verse was sent down concerning Miqyas b. Ṣubāba. Miqyas accepted Islam and was with the Prophet ﷺ, and his brother was with him, and he was killed

or something of that sort. This alerts you to the greatness of knowledge. Two words only, and Jibrīl travelled on their account a distance of two thousand years. Between us and the lowest heaven is a distance of five hundred years, and the heaven, its thickness is a distance of five hundred years, and the Qurʾan had been in the lowest heaven ever since it was sent down on the Night of Power. So he went a distance of a thousand and returned a distance of a thousand for two words only, which are
. For this reason, when al-Rashīd asked Imam Mālik to teach him — to relate the hadith to him — while he was a king seated upon his couch, Mālik said to him:
⟨Knowledge is come to; it does not come. You must come yourself.⟩
Then when he came to him and the chair was set up for him, Mālik said to him:
⟨You must sit upon the ground in humility before I teach you.⟩
So he did, and he taught him.
«Allah has given precedence to those who struggle with their wealth and their selves over those who sit at home»
— an excellence, since the two are equal in intention and those who struggle have the increase of direct engagement —
«and to each Allah has promised the best»
«Those who sit at home among the believers, other than those possessed of injury, and those who struggle are not equal»
, those who sat at home supposed that they had no reward at all, and for this reason He said
«and Allah has given precedence to those who struggle over those who sit at home»
— stations, some of them above others, of honour. The degrees of the one who struggles will be mentioned in Sūrat al-Tawba,
«and forgiveness and mercy; and Allah is ever forgiving»

(Q. 4:96) — […]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Yaḥyā said to his people: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commanded him to believe in Allah alone and that he associate nothing with Him, and commanded him to establish the prayer, and commanded him to fast, and commanded him to give alms, and commanded him to remember Allah, Blessed and Exalted. He said to him: the likeness of one who associates partners with Allah is as a man who bought a slave and handed him money to trade with and to live from and to give the profit to his master; and the slave took to doing this work with the money and giving it to his master’s enemy and leaving his master. This is the likeness of associating partners with Allah. And when you are occupied with the prayer, do not turn aside to anything else. The likeness of one who turns aside in the prayer is as a man whom a mighty king has honoured and has brought before him to speak with him intimately, and he took to turning aside to another. And He commanded him to fast, and said to him: the likeness of fasting is a man who has an enemy, so he took a coat of mail and took a sword and weapons to fortify himself against his enemy — fasting is a shield. And the likeness of alms is as a man whose enemies took him captive and he bought himself from them with his wealth. And the likeness of one who remembers Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is as a man who fled from his enemies and entered an impregnable fortress, fortifying himself in it against his enemies. This is the likeness of one who remembers Allah, Blessed and Exalted.⟩ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨I command you with five: hold to hearing and obedience, and emigration, and jihad, and holding fast to the community.⟩
«Indeed those whom the angels take in death, wronging themselves»
— by remaining with the unbelievers and abandoning emigration. Emigration was a condition in Islam at the beginning of Islam.
«They say, ‘In what [state] were you?’ They say, ‘We were oppressed in the land.’ They say»
— the angels, to them, in rebuke —
«Was not Allah’s earth wide, so that you might emigrate in it?»
) to another country, as others besides you did. He, Exalted, said:
«Hell, and an evil destination it is»
(Q. 4:97). Whoever abandoned emigration, He promised him Hell.
«Except the oppressed among the men and the women and the children»
⟨I and my mother were among them.⟩
«who are unable to contrive a means»
— they have no power for the emigration nor for the expense —
«nor are they guided to a way»
(Q. 4:98) — a road to the land of emigration —
«Those — it may be that Allah will pardon them»
— He gave them no definitive assurance of the pardon; rather ‘it may be’: they hope that Allah will pardon them —
«And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find a refuge»

(Q. 4:100) — in provision. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has promised everyone who emigrates that He will give him a spacious place and provide for him wherever he is. If we say that the emigration came to an end with the conquest of Mecca, that is because of its being a condition in the servant’s submission (

), and the emigration never comes to an end. There enters into the emigration from the place of unbelief to the abode of Islam: the emigration from innovation to the sunna, and the emigration from ignorance to knowledge, and the emigration from a place in which Islam is weak to a place in which Islam is strong,
everyone who moves from one land to another land for the good of his religion is an emigrant, until the Day of Resurrection. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ says:
⟨Emigrate, and you will bequeath to your sons glory.⟩
«And whoever goes out from his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger»
(Q. 4:100). This verse was sent down concerning Jundub b. Ḍamra

al-Laythī was a very old man, and he resolved upon the emigration, so he charged his slaves to carry him, and they carried him from Mecca to Medina, and he died on the road. The unbelievers used to gloat over him, saying: he fled from us and did not reach the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — he has lost twice over. And the Companions were saying: would that he had arrived, so that he might attain the reward of the emigration. So there was sent down:
«And whoever goes out from his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him»
«that his reward is upon Allah; and Allah is ever forgiving, merciful»

(Q. 4:100). The Muslims rejoiced at that, and so the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ⟨When the son of Ādam dies his work is cut off…⟩, is not to be taken absolutely. ⟨When a man dies his work is cut off except from three: an ongoing alms, and a righteous child who supplicates for him, and knowledge he has disseminated in the hearts of men.⟩ That is, whoever dies and leaves behind […]: the wealth is the ongoing alms (
), and the child of the loins

is the righteous child who supplicates for his parents, and the child of the spirit is the knowledge he has disseminated in the hearts of men. And it is soundly established that whoever dies while he is reciting the Qurʾan and has not memorized it, Allah charges an angel to complete the memorization of the Qurʾan for him. So on this reckoning, the cutting off of the work at death is only for one who has no intention; as for one who was in a work in which he intended to continue, and death cut it off, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, completes it for him. The Qurʾan is an outward Qurʾan and an inward Qurʾan; the outward Qurʾan

is this one that we recite. If a man occupies himself with the recitation of the Qurʾan and dies before he has memorised the Qurʾan, our Master commands an angel to complete the memorisation of the Qurʾan for him, and so he is raised on the Day of Resurrection having memorised it, a bearer of the Book of Allah. So every righteous deed is included in the Qurʾan: whoever resolves upon jihad and dies without completing it, and whoever goes out for the hijra and does not arrive, and whoever goes out in search of knowledge — all of this Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will complete for him, and he is raised on the Day of Resurrection complete. His bounty is vast.
«in the land, there is no blame upon you that you shorten the prayer»
— by bringing it back from four to two —
«if you fear that they may harry you»
— that they inflict something hateful upon you —
(Q. 4:101). [The condition] has no converse implication. The sunna has made clear that what is meant by the long journey is four

(post-stages), which are two stages, even without fear. They shortened [the prayer] with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when they were as secure as they had ever been — that is, in great security. The verse came down only in a case of fear; the shortening was prescribed together with the fear at one and the same time, but when the fear is lifted it does not bar the shortening.
«Indeed the unbelievers are to you a manifest enemy»
«and you lead them in the prayer, let a party of them stand with you»
— and let another party hold back —
— the party that stood with you —
— standing guard until you have finished the prayer, and then this party goes and stands guard —
«and let another party come that has not prayed, and let them pray with you, and let them take»
(Q. 4:102) — with them, until you have finished the prayer. And he ﷺ did just that at Baṭn Nakhl; the two Shaykhs relate it.
«Those who disbelieve wish that you would be heedless»
— the cause of this is that the unbelievers wished, that is […], that you would be heedless when you stood for the prayer —
«of your weapons and your baggage, so that they might fall upon you all at once»
— by charging upon you and seizing you —
«And there is no blame upon you, if there is harm upon you from rain or you are sick, that you lay down your weapons»
«and take your precaution. Indeed Allah has prepared for the unbelievers a humiliating punishment»

(Q. 4:102) — one carrying humiliation (ihāna). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on the raid of Banū Anmār. When Allah routed the enemies of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out alone and crossed the valley, and the sky was sprinkling a light rain, until he came to be far from his Companions. He sat down beneath a tree to relieve himself. Ghawrath, one of the unbelievers of Banū Anmār, looked at him and said: this is the Messenger, alone, withdrawn from his Companions; may Allah kill me if I do not kill him today. So he took his sword and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and drew his sword bare, and said: who will protect you from me, O Muhammad? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
He drew the sword, and fright and trembling seized him, and he fell, and his sword with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the sword and said to him:
⟨And you — who will protect you from me?⟩
He said: no one. He said:
lā ilāha illā Llāh, Muhammad rasūl Allah
He said: I will not say it, but I will never make war on you, and I will not be with anyone who makes war on you. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left the sword to the man and said to him:
He said: by Allah, you are better than I am. He said:
prayers in the day and night. He said:
⟨They are, O Muhammad, five prayers in the day and night, and whoever brings a good deed shall have ten the like of it, so those are fifty prayers. The word is not changed with Me.⟩

Since the original obligation of the prayer was fifty prayers, and the unbelievers refused the prayer, He appointed for them on the Day of Resurrection fifty thousand years, each prayer a thousand years. For this the Resurrection is long upon them, and it became a day whose measure is fifty thousand years, because they left the prayer, fifty prayers every day, so each prayer a thousand years. He made them few, so they are five, and He set their times, because man is by nature given to putting things off. Had He not set the times of the prayers for us — pray the dawn prayer, the noon prayer, the afternoon prayer, the sunset prayer, the night prayer — those given to putting off would not have prayed the dawn prayer down to this time of ours; they would put it off. But He Himself set the time, so that you should not put it off, and He made the time wide as well, so that it should not be compulsion. You pray by your own choice; the time is wide. The one under obligation is able to perform the prayer by his own choice, and it is not by coercion. And He commanded a crier to call to the prayer; you hear the muezzin always, calling at every time to the prayer. He commanded the establishing of the prayer,
(Q. 2:43), and its performance in its time,
«Indeed the prayer is for the believers a prescription at appointed times»
(Q. 4:103), and He commanded humility in it,
«those who are humble in their prayer»
(Q. 23:2). Among them is he who has kept to this number, since Allah made fifty prayers obligatory: they impose upon themselves fifty cycles of the prayer (
) every day and night. The five prayers are seventeen cycles, and with the

(the odd) — that is twenty. Whoever keeps to the two cycles of the dawn and the two cycles of the forenoon, and four before the noon prayer and four after the noon prayer and four before the afternoon prayer, and two after the sunset prayer and two before the night prayer, and ten cycles before the

— these are fifty prayers. Among the servants of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, there is he whom Allah has strengthened until he was in prayer continually. Among them is he who has found the perpetuity of the prayer; they are in prayer continually,
«those who are constant in their prayer»

(Q. 70:34). Guarding these five is not perpetuity in the prayer. Among the servants of Allah there is he who has the perpetuity of the prayer, in prayer continually; and that is by the intention. A man intends that he is one who prays continually, and so he is one who prays continually. ⟨The intention of the believer is better than his deed, and the intention of the unbeliever is worse than his deed.⟩!
Those who have been granted the perpetuity of the prayer are those who performed this prayer until they reached the true nearness

(Q. 96:19), until they passed away from existence, and passed away from themselves, from existence and from the existence of existence, so that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, remains. They are there in prayer continually, in a single prostration; they do not raise their heads until the Hour comes.
«Indeed the prayer is for the believers a prescription at appointed times»
(Q. 4:103) — at the five times — or a prescription appointed over them: they are in the time of the prayer continually.
«And do not flag in the pursuit of the people»

(Q. 4:104). When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a party in pursuit of Abū Sufyān and his companions when they had returned from Uḥud, they complained of their wounds — when Abū Sufyān said: our appointment is tomorrow at Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad, and he turned coward and said: next year, at Badr al-Ṣughrā. Some of the Companions pleaded excuses, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
⟨By Allah, I shall go out to them even if I am alone, and none shall go out with me but one who was present at yesterday's battle.⟩

«Indeed We have sent down to you the Book with the truth»

(Q. 4:105). It came down concerning Ṭuʿma b. Ubayriq, a man of the Anṣār who used to display faith while in reality he was a hypocrite. He stole a coat of mail belonging to his neighbour and hid it with a Jew. The coat of mail had been stored in a place in which there was some wheat flour, and when he stole the coat of mail the wheat flour kept dropping along his path until he deposited it with a Jew. When the owner of the coat of mail demanded his coat, he saw the dropping of the flour until it reached the house of the Jew, so he asked him about the coat, and he said to him that Ṭuʿma b. Ubayriq had deposited it with him. And he summoned Ṭuʿma, and [Ṭuʿma] gathered a group of his own people, hypocrites like himself, and they swore by Allah that the Jew was the one who stole the coat of mail and that Ṭuʿma had not stolen it. So they came to the Messenger ﷺ, and he swore and his witnesses swore; and the Messenger ﷺ saw nothing but a Muslim claiming his own innocence, with Muslim witnesses swearing for him in whom he saw no suspicion at all, so his heart inclined to [the view] that the right was with him, and he wished to judge in his favour against the Jew. So there came down
«Indeed We have sent down to you the Book»
«with the truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you»
— by what He has taught you —
«and do not be for the treacherous»
(Q. 4:106). The ulama differed over whether the Messenger ﷺ has independent legal reasoning (
) or whether it is not for him to reason independently, for he does not speak out of caprice:

(Q. 53:4). Some of them said that he has no share in independent reasoning, and some of them affirmed that it is for him to reason independently ﷺ, but that when he reasons — after the verse — his reasoning is revelation.
«that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you»
Allah granted him that what Allah shows him is that which Allah has commanded. So his reasoning is revelation.
«And do not be for the treacherous a contender»
«And ask forgiveness of Allah; indeed Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful»
«And do not argue on behalf of those who act treacherously against themselves»
— they betray them by acts of disobedience, because the evil consequence of their treachery is upon them —
«Indeed Allah does not love one who is treacherous»
— that is, Ṭuʿma and his people, out of shame —
«from the people, but they do not hide themselves from Allah, and He is with them»
«what He is not pleased with, of speech»
— their resolve to swear denying the theft and to cast it upon the Jew
«And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do»
«in the life of this world; then who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection»
«or who will be a guardian over them»

(Q. 4:109) — taking charge of their affair. No one will do that. When the verse came down, the Messenger ﷺ declared the Jew innocent and cut off Ṭuʿma's hand; and he fled to Mecca and apostatised and became a thief. One night he dug beneath someone's house until he found a hole by which to enter the house to steal, and the house collapsed upon him and he died. In the end it became clear that he was the thief.
— by committing an offence confined to himself —
«then he earns it only against himself»
— because its evil consequence is upon it, and he does not harm anyone else —
«then casts it upon an innocent man»
— by his casting it upon him —
«And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you»
«but they lead none astray but themselves, and they do not harm you in anything»
— because the evil consequence of their leading astray is upon them —
«and Allah has sent down upon you the Book»
«and He has taught you what you did not know»
«and the grace of Allah upon you is»

(Q. 4:113). This verse comprised several things: that nothing profits a person but his good deed and nothing harms him but his evil deed; that a person is obliged to repent and to strive at good works at every one of the times; and that the one who judges is obliged to deal justly between people. This one is a Jew, an unbeliever, and this one claims Islam and is an Arab; and when the right belonged to the Jew, the Messenger ﷺ judged in his favour by the command of the Qurʾan, and judged against the Muslim. For this reason they have said that a ruler who has no justice is like a river that has no water; a scholar who does not act by his knowledge and does not teach it is like wealth from which nothing is spent; a rich man who has no generosity is like a tree that has no fruit; a poor man who has no steadfast patience is like a lamp that has no light; and a woman who has no modesty is like food that has no salt. And they have said: the setting right of four lies in four — the boys, their setting right is in the schools; the elders, their setting right is in the mosques; the women, their setting right is in the houses; and the thieves, their setting right is in the prisons. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, bestowed knowledge upon His Messenger ﷺ, and He said that this is a great grace upon the Messenger ﷺ. Allah gave the Messenger ﷺ such greatness of rank as He has given to no servant other than him ﷺ. The rank of the Messenger ﷺ with Allah is of three degrees: he has a small rank, he has a middling rank, and he has a great rank. The small rank of the Messenger ﷺ is that everyone who teaches some good or teaches some knowledge, Allah apportions to him the reward of that, and He multiplies the reward of the teacher for his teacher, and multiplies that for the teacher of that one — the higher the chain, the greater the multiplication — until it ends at the Messenger ﷺ. So he has in every question the largest share of the reward and the merit, and everything of good that is taught issues from the Messenger ﷺ. This

is his small rank. His middling rank — none knows it in reality but the Messenger ﷺ; and his great rank — none knows it but Allah. Every day he ascends in the knowledge of himself and comes to know of himself what he did not know. And this is his asking forgiveness ﷺ: ⟨Indeed a clouding comes over me, so I ask forgiveness of Allah seventy times in the day⟩ — and in one narration, a hundred times. And he ﷺ is preserved from sin, incapable of committing any contravention with an incapacity belonging to his very essence, like a man's incapacity to fly in the air; and even so he was addressed with
«Indeed We have granted you a manifest victory, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what came after»
(Q. 48:1–2). If we were to suppose that he had a sin, Allah has forgiven him what preceded and what came after. So then, his asking forgiveness — for what? And his clouding (ghayn) — of what?
(those who know Allah) see nothing other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and he is the imam of

(the gnoses), and he finds in himself of service and of

— of what they confer secretly about

As for the estates, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, undertook their division, because people are moulded upon the love of this world and eagerness for wealth; and the inheritance, since it gives to some people and deprives other people — had the Messenger himself undertaken this, there would have been in the hearts of some of them something against him ﷺ, and whoever hates him is wretched with a wretchedness after which there is no happiness ever. So Allah undertook the division of the estates and charged no one with it. The science of the appointed shares of inheritance (

) has been described as half of knowledge, and it is a small compass, which a man completes in a short span. How is it half of knowledge, when knowledge multiplies without end? That is because man has only two states, life or death: so long as he is alive all the rulings run upon him, and when he dies there remains for him nothing but the appointed shares, nothing but the science of inheritance. For this it came to be half of knowledge.

— the shafts from which the unbelievers used to take knowledge of the unseen. They had seven shafts with the keeper of the Kaʿba: one, 'my Lord has commanded me'; one, 'my Lord has forbidden me'; one, 'from you'; one, 'from other than you';

one, 'blood-money' or indemnity; one, left blank. If a man wanted to do any matter, he would come to the idol, and the keeper of the Kaʿba would bring something of water, and he would shake the shafts and set [them down]. If the shaft on which was written 'my Lord has commanded me' came out to him, he went out to what he wanted and said that the idol had commanded him to that, and that he had found the permission (

) from his lord. And if 'my Lord has forbidden me' came out, he desisted and said that his lord had forbidden him. And if they differed over the lineage of a child that was born, and disputed over its father, they came to the shaft: if 'from you' came out, they attached it to the lineage, and if 'from other than you' came out, they disowned it. And if a man was slain, if 'blood-money' came out they imposed the indemnity in his case, and if the blank came out they let it lie, that there was no indemnity in it. These are the divining arrows (

) by which they used to seek division before Islam. And there falls under it every prying into the unseen by a way not sanctioned by the Law; there falls under it whoever goes to the diviner and the soothsayers, and the seeking of guidance by dreams (
), and the tables — all this falls under this heading. As for the prophetic seeking of guidance, it is that you pray two cycles of the prayer (

) for Allah and supplicate that Allah choose for you what is better for you; whatever comes to pass after that is good. That is what agrees with the Law. As for prying into the unseen, that is contrary to the Law.

ʿUmar answered him that the Muslims had taken the day of its coming down as two feasts: Friday is a feast day, and ʿArafa is a feast day. And on that day the feasts of all the communities came together — Friday, and the day of ʿArafa, and the feast day of the Christians, and the feast day of the Jews, and the feast day of the Magians: all of them fell on that day, and the feasts of the communities have not coincided on a single day before it or after it. When this verse came down, ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, wept. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
⟨Because we were always in increase, and today, when He has perfected our religion for us, we know that the increase has come to an end; and a thing that does not increase must needs decrease.⟩
So ʿUmar was the most understanding of the Companions. This verse gave notice of the nearness of the death of the Messenger ﷺ: after eighty-two or eighty-three days he ﷺ died.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made lawful in this verse the giving of believing women in marriage to one another, because they are upon a sound religion, and the giving of Jewish and Christian women in marriage, because they are People of the Book — and though they have altered and substituted and swerved from the path, their religion is heaven-sent. As for the polytheist women who have professed no heaven-sent religion, they have no right to marriage with the Muslims. Giving polytheist women and the Magians in marriage is forbidden; and the difference between them and these others is that those [the People of the Book], though they are unbelievers, are upon a heaven-sent nurture, while these have had no prior heaven-sent nurture, and it is not fitting for a Muslim to marry from among them.

— from among them, with whom you commit fornication in secret. Marriage in the Jāhiliyya was of four kinds. The marriage known today: that the man comes to the woman's guardian and brings a dowry, and he contracts her to him. And a woman — a man would come to her and marry her, and another would come and marry her; and when she bore a child, they would gather the trackers (

) to look, and when they said, ‘the child has in him the blood of so-and-so’, they attached him to so-and-so, and he would be the father. The Arabs used to love nobility of stock in children: if they saw a household whose traits of character were praiseworthy and who were

champions and possessed of noble traits of character, one of them would love to get a child like them. He says to his wife: when you have become pure, you will go to so-and-so and be with him as a wife to him until you conceive; when you have conceived, you will come back to me. So the wife comes to a man, consenting to remain with him as a wife to him, until, when she has conceived by him, she returns to her husband, so that the child may come out of noble stock; and they ascribe him to the father. And the women of the banners: the prostitutes who had banners, and they were just like shops, just like stalls — every man comes to them. The Muhammadan shariʿa confirmed the first marriage, which is the contract by means of a guardian and a dowry and witnesses, and abolished all the other kinds of marriage; but if a man became Muslim, he was confirmed in his marriage, and the children who grew up out of unbelief are children who are attached [to their fathers] when they enter Islam. For this reason the shariʿa gave weight to their marriages after their entering Islam, as a comfort to them. Among the unbelievers there is no child of
fornication, because with them their contracts and other than them are alike; when they enter Islam, all of them — his lineage is sound.

) that he perform the ablution; so the one in minor impurity, whether he has urinated or defecated, performs the ablution only. Why is the bath obligatory upon the emission of semen, while the bath is not obligatory upon the exit of excrement, which is by far more impure than semen and filthier? Because the appetite of intercourse engrosses the body of a person, so that he employs all the strength of his body, outwardly and inwardly, and for this reason the washing of the whole of his body is obligatory upon him — unlike food or drink, which you take in by a single extremity: eating is with the mouth, and drinking likewise, and for this reason nothing was made obligatory for them but the washing of the extremities. Or because intercourse is infrequent, so He made the bath obligatory in it, while urine and excrement recur often, so He was content with the washing of the extremities that are visible of people, such as the face
and the hands and the feet up to the ankles, as a lifting of hardship, because if a bath were obligatory in every [instance of] ritual impurity, it would be a hardship upon the Muslims. He said:
«then betake yourselves to good earth and wipe your faces and your hands with it»

— because He did not make clear the extent of the wiping. The sunna made plain the covering of the two limbs by the wiping, so al-Shāfiʿī was content with the wiping of the wrists, while Mālik said that it is to the elbows. Hārūn and Mūsā died in the wilderness, and it was a mercy for the two of them and a punishment for those others. At his death Mūsā asked his Lord to bring him within a stone's throw of the holy land, and He brought him near, as in the hadith. Yūshaʿ was made a prophet after the forty years and was commanded to fight the giants, and he set out with those who remained with him and fought them — and it was a Friday — and the sun stood still for him an hour until he had finished fighting them. Aḥmad related in his Musnad the hadith: ⟨The sun has not been held back for any human being save for Yūshaʿ, on the nights he marched to Bayt al-Maqdis.⟩ This is the story of Mūsā with the giants, together with the Children of Isrāʾīl: they refused the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and so Mūsā invoked against them with his words
«So part between us and the wicked folk»
his supplication, in that He informed him that they would wander in the land forty years. Mūsā grieved at this, and so it was said to him:
«So grieve not over the wicked folk»

(Q. 5:26) — do not sorrow over them; they only deserve the affliction that has befallen them. They wandered for the space of forty years within nine parasangs, by the power of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Had they reflected upon the sun or upon the stars, or looked to the sea, they would have found a way to get free of that patch of ground. But Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made them powerless, and so they remained for that span within a distance of nine parasangs — and it is said six parasangs — for forty years, as a punishment for them, because they went against the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. As for Mūsā and Hārūn, the two of them remained with them in the wilderness, and they had not gone against the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; so how could the two of them be in the punishment when they were innocent? It is said that the two of them were not with them in the wilderness; and the sound view is that they were with them in the wilderness, but it did not harm them. It was for them coolness and peace, as the fire was for Ibrāhīm coolness and peace. This affair tells you the outcome of companionship: the Children of Isrāʾīl went against the command of Allah, and so they remained in the wilderness forty years; and Mūsā and Hārūn, who had not gone against the command of Allah — when they kept company with these wicked men, they remained in the wilderness with them forty years. And these wicked men, since Mūsā and Hārūn were among them, remained in the wilderness in the greatest favour: when they asked for food, Allah sent down upon them manna and quail, the most wholesome food found in this world; and when they asked for clothing, their clothing stayed neither soiling nor ever wearing out; and they asked for light in the darkness, and Allah sent columns of light; and they asked to be given water, and Mūsā struck his rock, and twelve springs gushed forth for them,

(Q. 2:60). This was by the blessing of the companionship of Mūsā and Hārūn; and the remaining of Mūsā and Hārūn in the punishment along with them was by the ill fortune of the companionship of those who went against the command of Allah. So when they had remained in the wilderness forty years, Hārūn died — and he was more beloved among the Children of Isrāʾīl than Mūsā. When Mūsā told them that Hārūn had died, they accused him of having killed him, because he was more beloved to them than he was. When the time came for the marrying of Hābīl and Qābīl, Ādam wanted to marry Qābīl's sister to Hābīl and Hābīl's sister to Qābīl. Ādam spoke with him, and he said to him: you have only wronged us (

); this is no ruling of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. So Jibrīl came down and said: Allah commands you to offer a sacrifice. If Allah accepts Hābīl's offering, then he has the better right to the girl who is disputed over; and if He accepts Qābīl's offering, then likewise. As for Hābīl, he used to raise livestock, so he chose a handsome ram and implored Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to accept it from him, and he set it down. When he threatened him with killing, he said that he would not kill him, because he himself fears Allah; and whoever kills his believing brother bears his own sin and the sin of his slain brother — and he wants that for him and does not want it for himself. How is this, when the Muslim loves for the believer what he loves for himself? He said this only as an admonition from him: he admonished him that whoever kills his brother returns with his own sin and the sin of the slain, so that he might be held back from killing him — not that he wished for him to fall into that.
«And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers»
«— his soul — to the killing of his brother, and he killed him, and he became»

(Q. 5:30) — by killing him. And he did not know what to do with him, because he was the first dead man upon the face of the earth from the children of Ādam; so he carried him upon his back after his death for a time.
«So Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth»
— digging up the dust with its beak and with its feet and heaping it over a dead crow that was with it, until it had covered it —
«He said: woe to me! was I unable»
«to be like this crow, and so conceal the corpse of my brother? And he became one of the regretful»

(Q. 5:31) — over having carried him. And he dug for him and covered him. This is the story of Qābīl and Hābīl. It was the first act of disobedience that fell upon the face of the earth: Qābīl envied his brother Hābīl and killed him. Ādam was absent — he was at the hajj — and he saw that the earth had changed and had grown dusty, and the waters had all been

sweet, and the waters of the seas all turned salt; and all the trees — their fruits had been good — so the earth and the fruits and the waters changed. Ādam knew that something had happened upon the earth. When he returned he looked and did not see Hābīl, and he said to Qābīl:

where is Hābīl? He said: I am not his keeper. He said to him: you have killed him. And he denied that he had killed him. So they went to the place where he had slaughtered him, and behold, the earth had drunk Hābīl's blood and no trace of him remained. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, threatened the earth for swallowing the blood of the slain, and after that the blood came out of the earth; and when the reproach had fallen upon the earth for that, the earth remained such that it does not drink the blood of anything slaughtered — even a chicken: it stays upon the face of the earth. When that happened, Ādam knew that Qābīl had killed Hābīl, so he drove him out; and he settled in Yemen and took to trading and to play, and he fathered children of the reprobates, with no good in them. That story Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to recount to the Children of Isrāʾīl, because they had opposed the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and had refused to enter the Holy Land; and he recounted to them the story of the two sons of Ādam. It was among the secrets of their books, and the Prophet ﷺ was unlettered, born in the land of the Ḥijāz; he had not read, nor had he kept company with anyone who had read anything. So he brought them what was hidden of their own sciences. This is the most telling proof of his messengership ﷺ. Many of the Jews accepted Islam because of these two stories.

«And the thief, male and female: cut off their hands»

(Q. 5:38) — the right hand of each of them, from the wrist. And the sunna has made clear that the amount for which it is cut off is a quarter dīnār and upward, and that if he repeats, his left foot is cut off at the joint of the foot, then the left hand, then the right foot, and after that he is disciplined with beating. He mentioned that the thief, male and female — their ruling is that their hands be cut off; and the sunna has made clear that the amount for which the hand is cut off is a quarter dīnār. A Jew raised an objection against Islam. He said: this Islam is inconsistent, in that it has made five hundred dīnārs obligatory as the blood-money for a hand — whoever cuts off a man's hand gives him five hundred dīnārs — while a man who has stolen only a quarter dīnār has his hand cut off. What is the matter with it? Ibn Ḥajar answered him that it is trustworthiness that made the hand dear, until it came to be five hundred dīnārs, and treachery that made it cheap, until it came to be only a quarter dīnār. This is the wisdom of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And He began with the man in the mention of theft, because the man is stronger at theft than the woman, just as He began with the woman in fornication, in His words, Blessed and Exalted:
(Q. 24:2) — because the woman is stronger at fornication than the man: if the woman does not consent, the indecency never occurs.
