— for the sake of a people —
— among them is one who comes to the Prophet ﷺ, takes the report, and goes off with it to the Jews.
— and they are the people of Khaybar. Two married persons among them committed adultery, and they were loath to stone them, so they sent Qurayẓa to ask the Prophet ﷺ about the ruling.
— which is in the Torah, such as the verse of stoning —
— upon which Allah had set it —
— to those whom they had sent —
— the distorted ruling, that is, the flogging, Muhammad having given it to you as his ruling —
«and if you are not given it»
in that he gives you a ruling contrary to it,
«then you will never possess for him»
«those are they whose hearts Allah does not will to purify»
— humiliation, through public exposure and the jizya —
«and theirs in the hereafter is a great punishment»
— that you may judge between them —
(Q. 5:42). This option is abrogated by His saying,
(Q. 5:49), and the rest of the verse. So judgement between them is obligatory
when they bring their case to us, and that is the sounder of al-Shāfiʿī's two views. And were they to bring their case to us together with a Muslim, it would be obligatory by consensus.
«And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you in anything. And if you judge»
«then judge between them with justice; indeed Allah loves the just»
(Q. 5:42) — those who are equitable in judging, that is, He rewards them.
«And how is it that they make you their judge, when they have the Torah with them, in which is the judgement of Allah»
— by stoning. They did not intend by that the knowing of the truth, but rather what was easier for them.
— they turn aside from your judgement of stoning, which agrees with their own Book —
«after that? And those are not the believers»

(Q. 5:43). The Jews of Khaybar, when a nobleman among them committed adultery, would lighten the ruling of Allah for him: they flogged him and took property from him; and when one who was not a nobleman committed adultery, they stoned him. Two noblemen of their eminent men committed adultery, so they sent to the Prophet ﷺ, hoping they might find some dispensation with him. He said to them: ⟨The ruling of Allah is stoning.⟩ They said: you have dealt harshly with us, O Abū al-Qāsim; this is not the ruling of Allah. He said to them: ⟨This is the ruling of Allah, and it is in the Torah.⟩ They said to him: how do you know that it is in the Torah? He said: ⟨Bring the Torah.⟩ So they went and brought the Torah. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣūriyā was reading it, and when he reached the verse of stoning he placed his finger upon the word of stoning and read what came after it. ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām was present, and he had the Torah by heart, so he moved his hand aside and read the verse of stoning to the Prophet ﷺ — the Prophet neither reads nor knows writing. When it became clear that this was the ruling of Allah, the Prophet ﷺ took the two of them and stoned them, and they were angered. They are the ones whom this verse reproaches. They did not come to the Prophet ﷺ seeking the ruling, because they knew the ruling; they only wanted something easy for them. Had they wanted the ruling, the Torah would have sufficed them. This is the ruling of Allah in the Torah.
«Indeed We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance»
— a plain exposition of the rulings —
— they yielded themselves to Allah, Blessed and Exalted

The prophets after Mūsā, of the Children of Isrāʾīl, had no books and no law. Rather every prophet of the prophets of the Children of Isrāʾīl held fast to the Torah alone. Every prophet in his generation guided the people by the Torah, just as the ulama guide the people now by the shariʿa of Muhammad ﷺ. For this reason he ﷺ said: ⟨The ulama of my community are like the prophets of the Children of Isrāʾīl.⟩ The prophets after Mūsā judged by the Torah:
«for those who are Jews, and the rabbis»
«with what they were entrusted to keep»
— they were given it in trust; Allah made them its keepers —
— so Allah made the Torah a deposit held with the Children of Isrāʾīl.
For this reason they were able to distort and to alter, and so they changed and altered — unlike the Qurʾan. He said:
«Indeed We, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its keepers»

(Q. 15:9). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has taken upon Himself the keeping of the Qurʾan from distortion and alteration, so it will not be altered until the Day of Resurrection — so much so that a boy, if he hears a distortion of the Qurʾan from an eminent reciter, corrects it for him. This is by the keeping of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
— of this world, which you take in return for concealing them —
«and whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the unbelievers»
(Q. 5:44) — whoever abandons the ruling of Allah and judges by other than the ruling of Allah, those are the unbelievers. And the Prophet ﷺ mentioned:

⟨Five for five: no people broke a covenant but that their enemy was given mastery over them; nor did they judge by other than what Allah has sent down but that poverty spread among them; nor did indecency appear among them but that death spread among them; nor did they skimp the measure but that they were denied the produce of the earth and were seized by years of dearth; nor did they withhold the zakat but that the rain was held back from them⟩
— the soul is slain for the soul, when it has slain it —
«for the tooth, and for wounds, retaliation»
) is exacted in them where it is possible, as with the hand, the foot, the male member and the like; and that in which retaliation is not possible — in it there is the arbitrated indemnity (

), at the discretion of the imam. And this ruling, though it was prescribed upon them, is established in our own shariʿa. Everything the Qurʾan mentions of the ruling of the Torah and the Gospel whose abrogation has not been made plain to us is a ruling for us; this is a ruling for us.
— by way of retaliation, in that he gave himself up to it —

(Q. 5:45) — for what he has committed. Whoever gives retaliation as alms — that is, the killer gives himself up to be killed — it is an expiation for him. Or whoever gives it as alms by way of retaliation: one to whom it fell due to kill a man and who then pardoned him, seeking nearness to Allah — it is an expiation for him. From this verse (
) Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī differed over the prescribed penalties (
): al-Shāfiʿī said that the prescribed penalties are deterrents (
), and Mālik said that the prescribed penalties are restoratives (

). So whoever has a prescribed penalty fallen due upon him and gives himself up, and the penalty is carried out upon him — it is an expiation for him, and the verse indicates that. And the hadith of al-Ghāmidiyya:
a woman who committed fornication after marriage (

). She came to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him: I have committed fornication; carry out upon me the prescribed penalty that Allah has made due upon me, and I am pregnant from the fornication. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
So she went and delivered, and she came with the child, suckling him. She said: carry out upon me the prescribed penalty that Allah has made due upon me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:

He is a prophet of mercy. So she went, until she had weaned the child; then she came again, and he was carrying bread and eating it. She said to him: the boy is weaned, and here he is eating; carry out upon me what Allah has made due upon me. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that they take her out to al-Baqīʿ and stone her until she died. They pelted her with the stones, and when the stones bore hard upon her she fled; so they overtook her and stoned her
until she died. They mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and one of them said: we have stoned the wicked woman. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
⟨Do not say 'the wicked woman'. She is wholesome. By Allah, had the people of Medina shared in her repentance, it would have purified them all!⟩

This showed us that the prescribed penalties are restoratives. And al-Shāfiʿī says: the prescribed penalties are deterrents, set up to deter others only, and the sin remains. Al-Shāfiʿī was severe on this.
«So whoever gives it as alms, it is an expiation for him»
— whoever gives himself up for the prescribed penalty to be carried out upon him, that is an expiation for him; and this indicates that the prescribed penalties are restoratives.
«And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down»
— in retaliation and in other matters —
«with ʿĪsā son of Maryam, confirming what was before him»
«of the Torah, and We gave him»
«and confirming what was before it of the Torah»
«and a guidance and an admonition for the godfearing»
«And let the people of the Gospel judge»
«by what Allah has sent down therein»
«And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the transgressors»
«with the truth, confirming what was before it»
— between the People of the Book, if they bring their case to you —
«by what has been sent down by»
«from what has come to you of the truth. For each one of you We have appointed»
— a clear road in religion upon which they walk —
«and had Allah willed He would have made you one community»
— of the differing revealed laws, that He might see which of you is obedient and which disobedient —
«so vie with one another in good works»
«To Allah is your return, all together»
— your return is to Allah, all of you, by the resurrection —
«and He will inform you of that wherein you used to differ»

(Q. 5:48) — of the matter of religion — and He will requite each of you according to his deed. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the True Sovereign, and He is the one who disposes of His creation however He wills. It is His to set a ruling in force for a span of time, then to bring that ruling to an end and bring another ruling; there is in this no objection against Allah, Blessed and Exalted. He sent the prophets, and all of them agreed upon the creed, which is the oneness of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, the magnifying of the Creator, and compassion for creation. All of them agreed upon this, because Allah charged the prophets: uphold the religion and do not become divided in it. And the division there is division in the creeds.

⟨The Jews divided into seventy-one sects, all of them in the Fire; and the Christians divided into seventy-two sects, all of them in the Fire; and my community will divide into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire save one — what I and my Companions are upon.⟩
that is, those who are upon the sunna and the community
⟨The hand of Allah is with the community.⟩
, and the division intended there is division in the creeds. As for disagreement in the branches, there has come concerning it:
⟨The disagreement of my community is a mercy.⟩

— because whoever follows a scholar meets Allah safe. Allah completed the revealed laws with the shariʿa of Muhammad ﷺ, and He sealed the books with His Mighty Book, which He named a guardian over all the books, after the books of Ādam had been words only:
«Then Ādam received words from his Lord»
(Q. 2:37). And the books of Ibrāhīm were words:
«And when his Lord tried Ibrāhīm with words»
(Q. 2:124) — and the books of Mūsā were scrolls only

(Q. 87:19). This is a Book that is a guardian over all the books. And just as his Book is the most excellent of the heavenly books, and his religion the most excellent of religions, and his community the best community, so he is the most excellent of all the prophets, by consensus.
And every one of them gave his community good tidings of Muhammad ﷺ, the last of them being ʿĪsā:
«and bringing good tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Aḥmad»

(Q. 61:6). He did not name him Aḥmad, because their language is not Arabic; but he said: ⟨It is better for you that I go. I go to my Father⟩ — in the language of the Gospel 'the Father' means 'the master' — ⟨my returning to my Father is better for you, and the Paraclete will come to you: the Spirit of truth.⟩ The Paraclete (

) in their language means Muhammad, or Aḥmad. And he said: ⟨When he comes he will confirm me, as I confirm him.⟩ And it is mentioned in a verse: ⟨He, when he comes, says nothing but what Allah has said to him, and does nothing but what⟩
⟨Allah has said to him! And were I to live to see him, he would deserve that I tie his sandal for him and wipe his foot for him.⟩
No creature has come after ʿĪsā more exalted in worth than ʿĪsā in this rank, except Muhammad ﷺ.
«And judge between them by what Allah has sent down, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they seduce you»
— that they not seduce you, that is,
«away from some of what Allah has sent down to you. But if they turn away»
— from the judgement sent down, and they desire something other than it —
«then know that Allah only wishes to afflict them»
— with the punishment in this world —
— which they have committed, among them the turning away; and He will requite them for all of them in the hereafter —
«And indeed many of the people are deviators»
«Is it the judgement of the Jāhiliyya that they seek?»
— do they seek, do they demand, the judgement of the Jāhiliyya, of flattery and partiality —
«And who is better than Allah in judgement»
— none is better in judgement than Allah, Blessed and Exalted —
— that is, in the sight of a people —
— of Him. They were singled out for mention because they are the ones who ponder it (Q. 5:50).
«O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians»
— the hypocrite ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy b. Salūl used to go and befriend the Jews and the Christians, and when he was forbidden that he would say:
⟨Reversals come about, and we shall have need of them one day.⟩
«O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies»
— making allies of them and showing affection to them —
«Some of them are allies of others»
— the unbelievers are united in unbelief (
); unbelief is all one creed; all the unbelievers are agreed upon unbelief and all of them are against the Muslims —
«some of them are allies of others»
«And whoever of you allies with them, he is of them»
— one of their number. Whoever befriends the unbelievers has gone out of the religion —
«And indeed Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people»
— by their allying with the unbelievers (Q. 5:51).
«So you see those in whose hearts is sickness»
— weakness of belief, like ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy the hypocrite —
«We fear that a reversal may befall us»
— that time may turn with it against us, whether drought or defeat, and Muhammad's affair will never be brought to completion, and then they will not provision us. He, Exalted, said:
— the help for His prophet, by making His religion manifest —
by the rending of the hypocrites' covering and their exposure —
«so that they become, over what they concealed within themselves»
— of doubt and of allying with the unbelievers —
— to one another, when their covering is rent, in astonishment —
«Are these the ones who swore by Allah their most binding oaths»
— the utmost of their effort in them —
— they used to say that they were with the Muslims. He, Exalted, said:
— their righteous deeds were made void —
— in this world by the disgrace and in the hereafter by the punishment (Q. 5:53).
«O you who believe, whoever turns back»

— to unbelief. A telling of what Allah, Blessed and Exalted, knew would come to pass. This verse came down before this matter occurred, and a group did apostatise — Jalāl said — after the death of the Prophet ﷺ.
«then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him»
⟨They are the people of this man⟩

(Q. 5:54). In the first age eleven sects apostatised. Three sects apostatised in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. Among them was al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī; he apostatised in Yemen and gained mastery over Yemen, until he drove out Muʿādh b. Jabal, the governor of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So the Messenger ﷺ sent word to Muʿādh that they should stand against him and that he should hold the people to remaining upon Islam. A man called Fīrūz killed him. The Prophet ﷺ gave word that al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī had been killed — a blessed man killed him — while he was in the illness of his death. It was said to him: who is the blessed man? He said:

Then the Messenger ﷺ passed away that night. This was on the twelfth of Rabīʿ al-Awwal, and at the end of the month the report came from Yemen that Fīrūz had killed al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī, just as he ﷺ had given word. And Musaylima the Liar apostatised in al-Yamāma and wrote to the Messenger ﷺ:
⟨the Messenger of Allah, to Muhammad the Messenger of Allah: the earth between us is two halves, half for me and half for you.⟩
His two envoys came to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said to them:
⟨Were it not that envoys are not to be killed, I would strike off your two necks.⟩
And the Prophet ﷺ wrote him a reply:
⟨From Muhammad the Messenger of Allah to Musaylima the Liar:⟩
«The earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as an inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the outcome belongs to the godfearing»

(Q. 7:128). When the Prophet ﷺ passed away, Abū Bakr sent out an army whose commander was Khālid b. al-Walīd, and they came and raided them, and Waḥshī — the slave of Muṭʿim b. ʿAdī, the one who killed Ḥamza at the battle of Uḥud — killed him. For this reason he used to say:
⟨I killed the best of men in the Jāhiliyya and the worst of men in Islam⟩

— meaning in his Jāhiliyya and in his Islam: when he was an unbeliever he was the one who killed Ḥamza, and when he was a Muslim he was the one who killed Musaylima the Liar. And Ṭulayḥa too laid claim to prophethood and apostatised, and a group apostatised with him. Abū Bakr fought them and gained mastery over them, and Ṭulayḥa fled to Syria, and after that he returned to Islam; Allah guided him and he died a Muslim. These three sects apostatised in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. And in the time of Abū Bakr seven sects apostatised. The Arabs apostatised entirely, from Syria and Yemen and Iraq; none remained but the people of Mecca and the people of Medina — on account of the zakat. They said:
⟨We will perform the prayer as Allah said; as for the zakat, our properties shall not be seized from us after the Prophet ﷺ. Allah said:⟩
⟨and the one who was addressed with ‘take’ has gone⟩
⟨We will not give anything of our properties after the Prophet ﷺ.⟩
So Abū Bakr stood up and said:
⟨By Allah, if they withheld from me a hobbling-cord that they used to hand over to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would fight them over it.⟩
⟨Gently, Abū Bakr! Will you fight one who performs the prayer and bears witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?⟩
⟨Away from me, ʿUmar! A tyrant in unbelief, a weakling in Islam! By Allah, I will never separate the prayer from the zakat. Allah says:⟩
«Perform the prayer and give the zakat»
(Q. 2:43). And he girded on his sword alone. ʿUmar said:
⟨When I saw that in Abū Bakr I knew that this which he held to was the truth.⟩

They had disliked this matter at the beginning and loved it at the end. So they fought the Arabs: everyone who did not render the zakat they would fight, until they returned to accepting the zakat. Were it not for Abū Bakr this pillar would have fallen and they would have made light of Islam. For this reason ʿUmar said:
⟨By Allah, no child has been born after the prophets better than Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq; and were it not for him the Arabs would all have apostatised by abandoning the zakat.⟩

And one sect apostatised in the time of ʿUmar: Jabala b. al-Ayham, the king of Ghassān. He came and embraced Islam, and he travelled with ʿUmar to the hajj. He was circumambulating the House, trailing his cloak behind him, and one of the Companions trod on his cloak — and he was a proud king — so he struck him in the face. The man complained of that to ʿUmar, and ʿUmar summoned him and said to him:
⟨Retaliation? I am a king and he is a commoner:⟩
⟨There is nothing of this in Islam. Islam has made us equal; the king and the commoner are alike, and Allah's judgement is retaliation.⟩
⟨I will give you a hundred camels, and you do not retaliate against me.⟩
⟨I will give you a thousand camels, and you do not retaliate against me.⟩
The man refused, and ʿUmar said:
⟨Commander of the Faithful, grant me a little respite until tomorrow.⟩
So ʿUmar granted him respite, and he fled and apostatised. He said:
⟨between the king and the commoner — this is a religion that is not to be accepted.⟩ This is the one who apostatised in the time of ʿUmar, and Allah gave word of this before it came to pass.
«O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion, then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble»

(Q. 5:54). The Messenger ﷺ was asked about these, and he said: ⟨The people of Yemen; faith is Yemeni and wisdom is Yemeni.⟩ And he was asked a second time, and he pointed to Salmān and said: ⟨The people of this man.⟩ ⟨Were Islam in the Pleiades, men from among these would reach it⟩ — an indication of the black-skinned, when they believe in Allah. And he was asked again, and he said: ⟨The people of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī.⟩ And the point holds for everyone who answers to these descriptions:
«humble toward the believers, mighty toward the unbelievers»
this matter: they are harsh toward the Muslims and merciful toward the unbelievers.
«in the way of Allah, and they do not fear the blame of any blamer»
— as the hypocrites fear the blame of the unbelievers —
«is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is all-encompassing»
«Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger»

— this came down when Ibn Salām said: O Messenger of Allah, our people have shunned us; everyone who has entered Islam, his unbelieving people have cut him off and taken him as an enemy. So Allah said:
«Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, those who establish the prayer and give the zakat, and they are bowing»

— humbly submissive (Q. 5:55). And this ruling has remained until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever is content with Allah as Lord and with Islam as religion — Allah is his ally, and His Messenger, and the believers all together.
«And whoever takes Allah as ally, and His Messenger and those who believe»
— so He helps them and gives them victory —
«then indeed the party of Allah — they are the victors»
— by His giving them the victory (Q. 5:56).
«O you who believe, do not take those who take your religion in mockery»

— this came down concerning the hypocrites and the Jews. The Messenger ﷺ was greatly concerned about something by which the people might be called to the prayer, so he consulted the Companions and said: We should like to find something by which the times of the prayer may be announced. Among them one said: We shall kindle a fire; when they see smoke in the daytime they know that the time has come, and when it is at night, when they see the light they know that the time has come. But the Prophet ﷺ disliked the fire. Among them one said: We shall strike a bell. But he disliked the bell. So they dispersed; and a group of the Companions, all of them, saw the call to prayer (

) in sleep: Abū Ṣudāʾ saw the call to prayer, and Bilāl, and a group. So the Prophet ﷺ ordered the call to prayer, and they began to call it. The Jews laughed a great laugh and said: We have never seen a religion more hideous than the religion of Muhammad; this braying of a donkey that he has brought — no religion ever brought the like of it. So He said:
«O you who believe, do not take those who take your religion in mockery»
«and sport, from among those who were given the Book before you, and the unbelievers»
«as allies; and fear Allah, if you are believers»
they mock it and laugh together on hearing the call to prayer.
— by reason of their being a people

— they have no intellect (Q. 5:58). So the call to prayer: it is not that it was established by a dream alone, for a group of the Companions; rather it was established by this verse as well. This verse established the ruling of the call to prayer. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
⟨The muezzins will be the longest of neck on the Day of Resurrection⟩
. And he said: Four — the earth does not eat their bodies when they die:

the prophets — the earth does not eat their bodies; and the bearers of the Muhammadan shariʿa, the scholars who act upon their knowledge; and the bearers of the Qurʾan; and the muezzins — whoever has given the call to prayer for seven years, the earth does not eat his body. He is in the lofty rank: the prophets, the bearers of the shariʿa, the bearers of the Qurʾan, and the muezzin. And the repeating of the call to prayer is recommended for everyone who hears it: when he says Allah is greater, you say Allah is greater; when he says I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, you say I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; and when he says I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, you say I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; when he says Come to the prayer, you say There is no capacity and no power save by Allah; and when he says: Come to prosperity, you say: What Allah wills comes to be, and what He does not

the Messenger of Allah, and the later ones interpret figuratively, so they interpreted the hand as power. And if they interpret the hand as power, what then do they do with the two hands here? Power is one, and this is a dual. And it has come as a plural:
«And the heaven — We built it with hands»

(Q. 51:47). This is a plural, more than two; we do not know whether six or eight. So the right course is that the hand be left upon its apparent sense and that we refer the meaning to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. His two hands are not two hands as with us.
— in widening and in straitening; there is no objecting to Him —
«and what has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them»
— because of their unbelief in it —
«and We have cast enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection»
«Whenever they kindle a fire for war»
— for war against the Prophet ﷺ
«Allah extinguishes it, and they strive on the earth for corruption»
— working corruption through acts of disobedience —
«and Allah does not love the corrupters»
«[And if] the People of the Book had believed»
«We would have effaced their evil deeds from them and admitted them into gardens of bliss»
«And if they had upheld the Torah»
— that is, had acted upon the Torah —

— they acted upon what is in them both, and what is in them both is faith in the Prophet ﷺ. The mention of Muhammad has come in the Torah and in the Gospel; both of them gave glad tidings of him. ʿĪsā said:
⟨I shall go, and the Paraclete will come to you.⟩
«and what was sent down to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet»

— had they acted upon what the Torah and the Gospel directed them to, namely faith in Muhammad ﷺ, Allah would have opened to them and widened their provision and poured out upon them from every side —
«Among them is a community keeping to the middle course»
— yes, among them is a group that acts upon it, and they are ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām —
«and many of them — evil is what they do»
«O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord»
— and do not conceal anything of it for fear that you should meet
— convey all that has been sent down to you —
«then you have not conveyed His message»
(Q. 5:67) — from their killing you. And he ﷺ used to be kept under guard until it came down, whereupon he said:
[by] transforming them, and of them him who
— Satan, by obeying him. A group of them prostrated themselves to al-Jibt and to the false deity when they came to Abū Sufyān at Mecca.
) — they have nothing but the Fire
«and further astray from the even path»
(Q. 5:60) — the road of truth; and the root meaning of
«they say, ‘We believe,’ while they have entered»
«with unbelief, and they have gone out»
— from you, clothed with unbelief likewise —
— with unbelief; and they did not believe —
«and Allah knows best what they were concealing»
«and their consuming what is unlawfully got»
«evil indeed is what they were doing»
«Why do the rabbis not forbid them»
— why did the ulama who act upon their knowledge not forbid them —
«and their consuming what is unlawfully got? Evil indeed is what they were working»
(Q. 5:63) — their leaving off forbidding them. The severest verse upon the ulama.
«Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from their uttering of sin and their consuming what is unlawfully got? Evil indeed is what they were working»
— when Allah straitened them on account of their calling the Prophet ﷺ a liar, after they had been the wealthiest of people in property they became poor, and they said —
May Allah withhold their hands from the doing of every good — this is an imprecation against them.
«And they were cursed for what they said. Rather, His two hands are outstretched»

(Q. 5:64) — an intensification in describing Him as liberal; and He put the hand in the dual to convey abundance, since the utmost that the generous man expends of his wealth is to give with both his hands. Allah, Blessed and Exalted — His two hands are outstretched. The hand of Allah is not a bodily limb, by the proof of ⟨both His hands are right hands⟩. These attributes that have come in the Qurʾan and the hadith — the early generations used to affirm them according to their outward sense and to commit the meaning to Allah, Blessed and Exalted: we believe in it as Allah intends, we believe in it as intended by

the Messenger of Allah. The later scholars interpret figuratively, and so they interpreted the hand as power. And if they interpret the hand as power, what will they do with the two hands here? Power is one, and this is a dual. And it has come in the plural:
«And the heaven — We built it with hands»

(Q. 51:47). This is a plural of more than two; we do not know whether it is six or eight. So the right course is that the hand be left according to its outward sense and that we commit the meaning to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. His two hands are not two hands as ours are.
— in enlarging and in straitening; there is no objection against Him —
«and what has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them»
— because of their unbelief in it —
«and We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection»
— and every sect of them opposes the other —
«Whenever they kindle a fire for war»
— for war against the Prophet ﷺ —
«Allah extinguishes it, and they strive on the earth in corruption»
— working corruption by acts of disobedience —
«and Allah does not love the workers of corruption»
«And had the People of the Book believed»
«We would have effaced from them their evil deeds and admitted them into gardens of bliss»
— that is, acted by the Torah —

— they acted by what is in them both, and what is in them both is faith in the Prophet ﷺ. The mention of Muhammad has come in the Torah and the Gospel; both of them gave tidings of him. ʿĪsā said: ⟨I shall go, and the Paraclete will come to you.⟩
«and what was sent down to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet»

(Q. 5:66). Had they acted by what the Torah and the Gospel directed them to, which is faith in Muhammad ﷺ, Allah would have opened to them and enlarged their provision and poured upon them from every side.
— yes, among them is a group that acts by it, and they are ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām —
«and many of them — evil is what they do»
«O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord»
— and do not conceal anything of it for fear that some harm reach you —
«and if you do not do so»
— convey all that has been sent down to you —
«then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people»
(Q. 5:67) — from their killing you. And he ﷺ used to be kept under guard until it came down, and he said: ⟨Disperse, for I have been protected by⟩
«Indeed Allah does not guide the unbelieving people»

(Q. 5:67). The Messenger ﷺ, when a verse came down that was severe upon the unbelievers, would hesitate to convey it to them, fearing that they would increase in unbelief; and so this verse came down upon him:
«O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord; and if you do not do so, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people»

(Q. 5:67). So he conveyed everything that had been sent down to him. For this reason ʿĀʾisha said: ⟨Whoever claims that Muhammad concealed anything of what Allah taught him has fabricated a monstrous calumny against Allah⟩ — that is, the lie. And the Messenger ﷺ: Allah gave him the knowledge of the first and the last and gave him more besides. He gave him three knowledges: a knowledge over which Allah took the covenant from him that he convey it and conceal nothing of it — and he conveyed it and did not conceal a letter of it, and that is the Qurʾan and everything he was asked about of the rulings of the shariʿa. And a knowledge in which Allah gave him the choice: if he wished he conveyed it and if he wished he did not convey it — so he conveyed that knowledge to the elect and concealed it from the rest; and it is the knowledge that the

(those seized by divine attraction) utter when they reach sheer annihilation. And a knowledge over which the covenant was taken from him to conceal it, and he concealed it — and it is the knowledge of the secret of the decree; he conveyed it to no one.
«Convey what has been sent down to you»
— this pertains to the Qurʾan and to the whole of the shariʿa, or to something he was asked about —
«And Allah will protect you from the people»
So when night came, a guard would stand at his door; and when this verse came down he raised the curtain from the door and said:
⟨Disperse, disperse, for Allah has sufficed me.⟩
«Say: O People of the Book, you stand upon nothing»
— of religion that counts for anything
«until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been sent down to you from your Lord»
— by acting upon what is in it, which is faith in the Messenger ﷺ —
«and what has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them»
— because of their unbelief in it —
(Q. 5:68) — if they do not believe in you, do not concern yourself with them.
«Indeed those who believe and those who are Jews»
«in Allah and the Last Day and does righteousness: no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve»
(Q. 5:69) — in the hereafter. Islam has done away with division by race.
— so all the believers are brothers:

(Q. 49:10). Whether his origin is Jewish or Christian or Sabian or Magian, or black or red or Arab — Islam has made them all brothers to one another when they pronounced the two testimonies of faith (
«Indeed We took the covenant of the Children of Isrāʾīl»
— upon faith in Allah and His Messenger —
«and We sent to them messengers. Whenever a messenger came to them»
«with what their souls did not desire»
— of the truth, they declared him a liar —
(Q. 5:70) — they killed him, like Zakariyyā and Yaḥyā; and the expression 'they slay' rather than 'they killed' tells a past state in the present, out of regard for the rhyming verse-end.
— a punishment upon them for their declaring the messengers liars and for killing them —
— to the truth, so they did not see it —
«many of them; and Allah is seeing of what they do»
«Indeed those have disbelieved who said: Allah is the Messiah son of Maryam»
— a sect of them said that Allah is the Messiah —
«And the Messiah said: O Children of Isrāʾīl, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord»
— for I am a servant and not a god. The first thing he uttered was
«Indeed I am the servant of Allah»
«Allah has forbidden him the Garden, and his refuge is the Fire; and the wrongdoers have no helpers»
«Indeed those have disbelieved who said: Allah is the third of three»
— a sect said that the gods are three: Allah is a god, and ʿĪsā, and his mother; and they too are a sect —
«and there is no god but one God. And if they do not desist from what they say»
— of the trinity, and do not profess the oneness —
«there shall surely touch those who disbelieved»

(Q. 5:73). ʿĪsā, upon him be blessings and peace, when he was raised up, left those who believed in him upon his religion, which is faith in Allah and that ʿĪsā is the servant of Allah and His messenger. The unbelievers used to fight the Muslims, and Allah would give the Muslims victory over them, until a man called Būlus led them astray — he is the one they call Paul down to our own day. When he had fought them for a time and was unable to overcome them, he made an outward show of Islam, that he had entered their religion. He entered their religion and strove hard until he gained great fame and renown and acceptance with them all. And one day, when they had prayed the dawn prayer, he said to them: I have seen the Deity. I saw ʿĪsā; he came down to me and entrusted to me a secret which I am to leave with a trustworthy man from among you; and I must draw near to Allah with my own self. So he summoned three: a man named Yaʿqūb, a man named Malkān, and a man named Nasṭūr. He took Yaʿqūb aside and said to him: Do you know that I entered your religion late and outstripped you all? Yes. That is for a secret which I have come to know and you do not know it; and so long as you do not hold this belief, you will gain no benefit from this religion. He said to him: And what is that? He said to him: The Deity is ʿĪsā, upon him be blessings and peace. He came down in His own person and returned to His

(unseen dominion). Whoever does not hold that ʿĪsā is Allah will never gain any benefit from this religion — until he had put this into his heart. When he knew that he had accepted it from him, he said to him: Set out towards this quarter, and admonish the people and call them to this creed. Then he took Malkān aside and said to him: I entered your religion late and outstripped you all by reason of a creed, which is the one by which Allah profited me; and so long as you do not know this, you will never profit. He said: And what is that creed? He said: The deities are three — ʿĪsā is a deity, and his mother is a deity, and Allah is a deity, the third of three. And when he accepted it from him, he sent him to another quarter to call the people to that creed.

Then Nasṭūr came, and he summoned him too and said to him: Do you know that I entered your religion newly and outstripped you all? Because I know a creed such that whoever does not know it gains no benefit from this religion. That creed, what is it? It is that ʿĪsā is a son to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And when he accepted it from him, he sent him out as a caller to a third quarter; and he himself — the enemy of Allah — took his own life, he killed himself

So those factions have remained, calling to these creeds down to our own day. And the fourth faction, which remained upon the Israelite creed of ʿĪsā, are those who believed that Allah is one and that ʿĪsā is the servant of Allah and His messenger. Among them was the Negus; and for this reason, when the Qurʾan reached him, he believed in the Prophet ﷺ and held him truthful, because it agreed with what
«And if they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment will surely touch those of them who disbelieve»
«Will they not turn in repentance to Allah and seek His forgiveness»
— for what they said; an interrogative of rebuke —
«the son of Maryam but a messenger; there have gone»
— so he passes away as they did, and he is not a deity as
they claimed; otherwise he would not have passed away.
«and his mother was a veracious woman»
«the two of them used to eat food»
— like others among the animals; and whoever is so cannot be a deity, because of his being composite and his weakness and what issues from him of urine and excrement —
«Look how We make clear to them the signs»
— how Allah made His oneness plain by His words
«the two of them used to eat food»
: whoever eats food must needs relieve himself, and this does not befit the side of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
«Look how We make clear to them the signs»
«Then look how they are turned away»
— they are turned aside from the truth, though the proof stands (Q. 5:75).
«Say: do you worship, apart from Allah»
«that which has no power to harm you or to profit you? And Allah is the Hearing»
— do not pass beyond the limit —

— by your putting ʿĪsā down or raising him above his right. Both factions went astray concerning ʿĪsā: the Jews accused his mother and said that Maryam was a fornicatress and that ʿĪsā was a child of fornication; and the Christians raised him above his measure.
And so they made him a son to Allah, or [said] he is Allah. Both factions went astray.
«And do not follow the desires of a people who have gone astray before»
«Those who disbelieved among the Children of Isrāʾīl were cursed by the tongue of Dāwūd»
— Dāwūd supplicated against them and they were transformed into apes, and they are the people of Ayla —
— he supplicated against them and they were transformed into swine, and they are the people of the Table —
— the cause of their destruction was this —
«Evil indeed was what they used to do»

(Q. 5:79). And for this reason commanding the good and forbidding the wrong is obligatory. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Whoever among you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand if he is able; and if not, then with his tongue; and if not, then with his heart — and that is the weakest of faith.⟩
«many of them taking those who disbelieve as allies»
— of the people of Mecca, out of hatred for you —
«Evil indeed is what their souls have sent ahead for them»
— of the deeds for their return, which brings upon them —
«that Allah is angry with them, and in the punishment they shall abide forever»
«and what was sent down to him, they would not have taken them»
«as allies, but many of them are transgressors»
(Q. 5:81) — they have gone out from faith. O Allah, bless our master Muhammad and grant him peace.
«You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah»
. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, told us in this verse (
) that the Jews are the most intense of people in enmity toward the Muslims, then the polytheists.
«And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe to be those who say: we are Christians»
. And you find the Christians nearer to affection for the Muslims than the Jews and than the polytheists.
— the nearness, the nearness of their affection for the believers —

(Q. 5:82) — against following the truth. In this verse He described the condition of the Jews and the condition of the Christians. It has been said that this is specific to the delegation of the Negus and not to all the Christians, because among the Christians are those who show the Muslims the most intense enmity; and it has been said that it is unrestricted. So the Jews are more intense in enmity toward the Muslims than the Christians — this, although the unbelief (

) of the Christians is grosser than the unbelief of the Jews. The Christians: their unbelief is in the divinity and in prophethood; and the Jews: their unbelief is in prophethood only. But the Jews were formed by nature to love this world, and because of the intensity of their love for this world they became worse than the Christians, who are the more intense in unbelief; so they became more intense in hostility toward the Muslims than others, on account of their envy and their arrogance and their love of leadership, on the strength of the hadith:
⟨The love of this world is the head of every sin.⟩
The Jews, when they have power over
) among his patricians with gifts, so that they might incline the heart of the Negus toward them. And when the two of them came to the Negus, they said to him:

⟨There have appeared among us a people given to corruption. They have corrupted our land and have joined themselves to your land. Give us power over them, that we may take them away to our land; for they are not upon your religion and they are not upon our religion. Had they been upon your religion we would have been content with them, or upon our religion [we would have been content]; but they are not upon your religion nor upon our religion, and their case is such and such.⟩
So the Negus sent to a company of the Companions that they should attend his assembly, and they attended, with Jaʿfar al-Ṭayyār at their head. And when they reached the door they said:
⟨Did you hear? They did not greet you with what your people greet you with. This is a proof of what we are telling you.⟩
⟨And why did you not greet me as people greet me?⟩
⟨We greeted you with the greeting of the Garden, and the greeting of Islam, and the greeting of our Prophet.⟩
⟨How noble is this! I am content.⟩
He asked them what their religion was, and they said to him:

⟨We were people of the Jāhiliyya: we worshipped the idol, and we severed the ties of kinship, and we did and we did, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us and called us to Islam — the worship of Allah alone, and the performance of the prayer, and the fasting, and voluntary alms, and chastity, and the joining of the ties of kinship.⟩
⟨What does your companion say of our companion ʿĪsā?⟩
«The Messenger of Allah and His word, which He cast to Maryam, and a spirit from Him»
(Q. 4:171). So he took a small stick and said:
⟨Your companion has not added to what our companion said by the measure of this stick. Have you anything of his Book?⟩
So Jaʿfar recited Sūrat Maryam. Around the Negus were priests and monks, and they wept until their tears overflowed, and they said:
⟨How like this is to what the Spirit used to bring!⟩
The Negus said to the two envoys of the polytheists:
⟨May Allah disfigure you both! Is it against these men that you would mislead me?⟩
And he said to the Companions: ⟨You are
⟩ — its meaning is: you are in safety —
⟨Go; you are at liberty in your affair.⟩

The affair of the two envoys who had come from Mecca was ruined; and between the two of them there had been intense enmity. So when ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ saw that their affair was ruined, he set about contriving the destruction of his companion. He said to ʿUmāra b. al-Walīd:

⟨You are a handsome man, and these kings — their women rule them. You must go in to the king's wife and show her affection, until there is friendship between you two, so that she may incline the king's heart toward us.⟩
So ʿUmāra b. al-Walīd took to frequenting the woman's house. Then ʿAmr b.
al-ʿĀṣ was alone with the king and said to him:
⟨My companion is an evil man; beware of him with respect to your women, for he is a wicked man.⟩

So the Negus entered his house one night and met ʿUmāra b. al-Walīd coming out of his wife's chamber. He seized him and beat him and tortured him, and blew into his urethra until his belly swelled, and cast him into the sea; and he went mad and took to roaming with the wild beasts. And ʿAmr returned to Mecca disappointed, and Allah destroyed ʿUmāra b. al-Walīd.

Then the Negus wrote to the Messenger ﷺ informing him of his Islam, and he sent his son and seventy riders; and when they were in the middle of the sea they drowned. In that period the husband of Umm Ḥabība bt. Abī Sufyān died, and the Messenger wrote to the king, the Negus, that he should ask for her hand on his behalf ﷺ. So he sent Abraha to her as an envoy; and when the envoy came to Umm Ḥabība and brought her the good news of the proposal of the Messenger ﷺ, she gave him all that the Negus had given her. They contracted her [in marriage] to al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ for four hundred dīnārs, and they prepared her and sent her to the Prophet ﷺ. Jaʿfar brought her on the day of the Prophet's ﷺ return from Khaybar. On that day he ﷺ says: ⟨I do not know by which of them I should rejoice: by the Islam of the Negus, or by the arrival of Jaʿfar, or by my bride, or by the conquest of Khaybar.⟩ And he said to Jaʿfar: ⟨You resemble me in my form and in my character.⟩

that the king, until he came to look at him, and he prayed over him. This is the occasion of the verse's revelation. The description is general, for all the Christians, the priests and the monks: they are lighter in enmity toward the Muslims, because of their renunciation of this world and because their religion is the leaving off of injury — the opposite of the Jews, who are the more intense in enmity on account of their love for this world. Whoever is avid for this world — whenever he sees a servant whom Allah has raised up, he envies him and shows him enmity and makes war on him, inescapably.
«And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger»
«you see their eyes overflow with tears at what they have recognised of the truth. They say: our Lord, we have believed»
— we have affirmed the truth of Your Prophet and Your Book —
«so write us down with those who bear witness»
(Q. 5:83). This is the description of the monks and the priests.
«You see their eyes overflow with tears»
— they wept until their eyes overflowed with tears, from the abundance of their tears. The Messenger ﷺ says:
⟨Two eyes the Fire shall not touch: an eye that has wept out of fear of Allah, and an eye that has passed the night guarding the Muslims in the path of Allah.⟩
And they said, in answer to those of the Jews who reproached them for Islam:
«And why should we not believe in Allah and in what has come to us of the truth»
«and hope that our Lord will admit us among the righteous people»
(Q. 5:84) — the believers — into the Garden. The Exalted said:
«So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding therein; and that is the recompense of those who do good»
«And those who have disbelieved and denied Our signs, those are the companions of the Blaze»
(Q. 5:86) — they enter the Fire. Whoever believes in Allah enters the Garden, and whoever disbelieves in Allah enters the Fire. The Messenger ﷺ says:
⟨All of you will enter the Garden except whoever refuses. Whoever believes in me and affirms my truth and says 'there is no god but Allah, Muhammad⟩
⟨is the Messenger of Allah — he enters the Garden; and whoever refuses has refused to enter the Garden.⟩
A king rode out and came to a town in which Abū Yazīd al-Bisṭāmī had lived, and he asked:
⟨Is there here anyone who met him?⟩
⟨Yes. There is an aged shaykh who lived in the time of Abū Yazīd.⟩
So the king summoned him and asked him:
⟨Have you retained anything of his speech? Have you memorised anything of what he used to say?⟩
⟨Yes. I heard him say: whoever has seen me, the Fire will not touch him.⟩
⟨Glory be to Allah! How can this be, when Abū Jahl saw the Messenger ﷺ and he is of the people of the Fire?⟩
⟨O king, Abū Jahl did not see the Messenger ﷺ; he only saw the orphan of Abū Ṭālib. Had he seen the Messenger ﷺ he would have believed in him and would have entered the Garden.⟩

So the king understood, and affirmed his truth. They are two kinds of form: the forms of persons and the forms of beliefs. The forms of beliefs, when they are present, suffice in place of the forms of persons; and the forms of persons, when they appear, do not suffice in place of the forms of beliefs. Here we are today in the fourteenth century: we have not seen the Messenger ﷺ, nor have we seen the miracles. We heard of him and we heard of the miracles, and we saw the Qurʾan, and so we believed in him and affirmed his truth. These, the Quraysh, witnessed his noble face and saw his miracles, and they did not believe.
May Allah grant us the beliefs.
«O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful to you»
The occasion of this verse's revelation is that the Prophet

ﷺ gave the Companions a penetrating admonition, at which hearts softened and eyes shed tears. Ten of the Companions gathered in the house of ʿUthmān b. Maẓʿūn, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said:
⟨We must have monasticism, and castration, and the abandoning of the eating of meat and of perfume; and we shall fast forever and not⟩
⟨break the fast, and we shall pray forever and not sleep until we die.⟩
The Messenger ﷺ heard of that and said:
⟨Are you the ones who say that you are going out for monasticism, and for castration, and for abandoning the good things?⟩
The Messenger ﷺ said to them:
⟨Gently, ʿUthmān! The monasticism of my community is jihad. There is no monasticism in Islam.⟩
⟨The castration of my community is fasting.⟩
⟨Then I shall divorce the woman, or I shall never go in to her.⟩

⟨Gently, ʿUthmān! If you are able to have two, or three, or four, then do so. For every time you lie with one of them and Allah does not decree a child for you, you will find a young servant in the Garden; and if Allah decrees a child for you and he dies before you, he will be a forerunner and an intercessor on the Day of Resurrection; and if you die before him, he will be a light for you on the Day of Resurrection.⟩
⟨Gently, ʿUthmān! I eat meat whenever I find it, and were I to ask my Lord He would feed it to me every day.⟩
⟨I do perfume myself. Jibrīl commanded me to perfume myself on alternate days; but on Friday perfume is indispensable.⟩
⟨Then I shall pray and never sleep, and fast and not break the fast.⟩
⟨Gently! I pray and I sleep, and I fast and I break the fast; and whoever turns away from my sunna is not [of me].⟩
So this verse came down. The verse accords with what comes before it, for the verse before it praised the priests
and the monks for their quality; and they had abandoned the world entirely. For this reason it was imagined by some people that that is better than partaking of

the good things. So this verse came down. He makes clear to them that even though those monks were described with a praiseworthy quality, the Muslims are better than they; for the verse forbids the Muslims to make unlawful what is lawful, just as it forbade them at the beginning of the sura to make lawful what is unlawful:
«Fulfil the contracts; the beasts of the flocks have been made lawful for you»
(Q. 5:1). One who makes the unlawful lawful is like one who makes the lawful unlawful.
«Do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you»
— the delectable among foods: if they are lawful, do not forbid them —
— do not overstep the command of Allah. The pivot is with the command of Allah alone: if Allah has forbidden a thing, leave it; and if He has made a thing lawful, partake of it —
«Indeed Allah does not love the transgressors. And eat of what Allah has provided you, lawful and wholesome»
«and fear Allah, in whom you are believers»

(Q. 5:87–88). The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Allah, Exalted, has imposed obligations, so do not neglect them; and He has set bounds, so do not transgress them; and He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; and He has kept silent about things, out of mercy to you and not out of forgetfulness, so do not inquire into them.⟩ And the gravest in crime among the Muslims is one who asks about a thing that was lawful until it was made unlawful.
«And fear Allah, in whom you are believers»

(Q. 5:88). Partaking of the good things of provision is no deficiency in the servant's case. Yes — whoever is extravagant and occupies himself with procuring the delectable among food and drink, perhaps

that leads him to eagerness for acquiring them, and that drags him into occupation with this world and the abandoning of the worship of Allah and forgetfulness of the remembrance of Allah. And whoever rejects these good things and takes to monasticism as the monks did — that too diminishes his constitution, and so diminishes his intellect; for some foods strengthen a man's constitution and strengthen his intellect, and

(gnosis) together with the loss of the intellect is impossible. There must be thought, and there must be reflection, and the way to that is the intellect. As for the monks, monasticism stripped them of their intellects, and so they did not arrive at the

of Allah, because their intellects were diminished. And those who occupied themselves with this world and scrambled greedily after the appetites and forgot the remembrance of Allah — they too did not arrive at
. And the end, in reality, is
«And eat of what Allah has provided you, lawful and wholesome, and fear Allah, in whom you are believers»
«Allah will not take you to task for what is thoughtless in your oaths»

— that which occurs in your oaths. The commentator said: ⟨It is what the tongue runs on to without the intent of swearing, as when a man says: No, by Allah; and Yes indeed, by Allah.⟩ And this is the school of al-Shāfiʿī.
«but He will take you to task for what you have made binding»
«is the feeding of ten poor persons from the average of what you feed your families»
(Q. 5:89). Whoever swears by Allah and breaks his oath, the expiation is upon him; and the expiation is the feeding of ten poor persons, for each poor person a dry measure of grain (
«from the average of what you feed your families»

— neither its highest nor its lowest. The imams differed over this — the feeding of ten poor persons. Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī said: for each one a dry measure of grain, and transfer of ownership suffices. Abū Ḥanīfa says: a midday meal and an evening meal suffice, because the text speaks of feeding, so feeding dispenses with transfer of ownership. And the Qurʾan says
«the feeding of ten poor persons from the average of what you feed your families»

(Q. 5:89), and a man's custom in feeding his family is that he makes over to them their sustenance, not that he feeds them; for this reason making over ownership to the poor persons suffices, for each one a dry measure of grain. As for the midday meal and the evening meal — a man's midday meal may be less than a dry measure of grain, or more. And the sunna made clear that for each poor person a dry measure of grain. So on this basis the feeding of ten
poor persons, for each one a dry measure of grain. A dry measure of grain — that is the way. And if he feeds one poor person a dry measure of grain each day for ten days, that suffices him.
— with what is called clothing, such as a shirt, a turban and a waist-wrapper; and it does not suffice to hand over what has been mentioned to a single poor person, and al-Shāfiʿī holds this —

— by which the affair of their religion stands, through the pilgrimage to it, and their worldly life, through the security of whoever is within it and its not being assailed, and the gathering of the fruits of everything to it. The Kaʿba is the House of Allah which is at Mecca. Allah made it a sanctuary, and made it secure, and made it a support for the people — that is, that by which the interests of their religion and of their worldly life stand. As for their religion, the Kaʿba is the qibla of the Muslims in all the regions of the world, and the place of their rites, their hajj. And the interests of this world [lie] in the security which the people of the House find: in the Jāhiliyya they were in wars continually and had no security, except when the months of the hajj came, [when] they strove to earn their livelihood, every one of them earning the food of a year and gathering it before the sacred months ran out. That was a support for them, that is, the cause of their livelihood —
— the sacred months: Dhū al-Qaʿda, Dhū al-Ḥijja, al-Muḥarram and Rajab — a support for them in their security, since they knew that there was no fighting, and so they earned their livelihoods —

He mentioned four things and made them a security for the people and a support for them: the Kaʿba itself, and the sacred month, and the offering — when a man garlands an offering, it is likewise — and the garlands.
«is so that you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and that Allah is knowing of all things»

«Know that Allah is severe in punishment»

— it is the practice of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in His Book that whenever He mentions a threat He joins to it a promise, as He has done in this verse:
«Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is forgiving, merciful»
«Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving»

(Q. 15:49–50). And as He said in another verse:
«And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is kind to the servants»
(Q. 50:33). When He mentioned the word of fear He joined it to al-Raḥmān. Had He joined it to

«Nothing is upon the Messenger but the conveying»
— what you make manifest of deed —
(Q. 5:99) — what you hide of it, and so He will requite you —
«the abundance of the foul. So fear Allah»
«O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they are disclosed to you, will grieve you»
(Q. 5:101). The occasion of this verse's revelation is that they asked the Messenger ﷺ a great many questions, until one day he ﷺ grew angry and said:

⟨Ask me! By Allah, no one shall ask me about anything, so long as I stand in this place of mine, without my answering him.⟩ Then a man stood up, called ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥudhāfa, who was suspected of being ascribed to other than his father, and he said to him: O Messenger of Allah, who is my father? He said: ⟨Your father is Ḥudhāfa.⟩ And a man stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah, where is my father? He said to him: ⟨Your father is in the Fire.⟩ ʿUmar knelt before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he had repeated his words, 'Ask me, ask me, ask me' — ʿUmar knelt and said: ⟨We are content with Allah as Lord, and with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as prophet; we shall not ask about anything.⟩ And this verse was revealed. And a man asked him: Is the hajj obligatory upon us every year? He was silent, and the man said it three times. He said: ⟨Leave me be so long as I leave you. For had I said yes, it would have become obligatory, and you would not have been able. When I command you something, do of it what you are able; and when⟩
⟨I have forbidden you from a thing, then avoid it.⟩
Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made some things lawful and has forbidden some things and has been silent about

things, not being heedless [of them]; so do not search into that. Everything in which no prohibition and no permission is mentioned is among what Allah has been silent about, and it is pardoned. And so there was sent down:
«O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if made manifest»
— because of the hardship in them —
«when the Qurʾan is being sent down»
— that is, in the time of the Prophet ﷺ —
«they will be made manifest to you»
— if you ask about things in his time, the Qurʾan must needs come down making them manifest; and whenever it makes them manifest, they grieve you, so do not ask about them. Indeed,
— [pardoned] your asking, so do not go back to it —
«and Allah is forgiving and forbearing. A people before you asked about them, then became disbelievers because of them»
(Q. 5:101–102). He restrained the Muslims from forbidding the lawful; and one who forbids the lawful is like one who makes the forbidden lawful.
«any baḥīra, nor sāʾiba, nor waṣīla, nor ḥām»
(Q. 5:103). The unbelievers of Quraysh used to assign certain things of their camels to their idols.

— she is the one whose milk is withheld for the idols, so that no one of the people milks her. The first to slit the ears of the baḥāʾir (the camels with slit ears dedicated to the idols) and to set loose the sawāʾib (the camels set loose by pagan vow) was ʿAmr b. Luḥayy. Quraysh were upon the religion of Ibrāhīm until the time of ʿAmr; he was the first to set these animals apart for their idols, and Quraysh followed him in it one after another. The Messenger said:
⟨I saw ʿAmr b. ʿĀmir b. Luḥayy al-Khuzāʿī dragging his entrails in the Fire.⟩

the stud of the camels: he covers a counted number of times, and when he has completed his covering they consign him to the idols. How extreme their folly! Allah did not ordain for them these baḥāʾir, nor the sawāʾib.

(Q. 5:104) — to the truth; and the interrogative is one of denial. Imitation of the fathers: if the fathers were guided, then praise be to Allah; and if they went astray, going astray is inevitable. And the religion of the fathers — the sons for the most part do not leave it.
«O you who have believed, upon you is [the care of] your own souls»
— guard them and undertake their setting right —
«those who go astray will not harm you when you have been guided»

(Q. 5:105). It is said: what is meant is that those who go astray among the People of the Book will not harm you; and it is said: what is meant is others than they, on the evidence of the ḥadīth of Abū Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said:

⟨Enjoin the good upon one another and forbid one another the wrong, until, when you see avarice obeyed, caprice followed, this world preferred, and every man of an opinion pleased with his own opinion⟩
⟨then hold to your own particular self.⟩
This verse is not [a warrant] for silence concerning enjoining the good or [forbidding] the wrong; rather it is about enjoining the good and forbidding the wrong.
The unbelievers and the Jews and the Christians are one side, and the Muslims another side.
«upon you is [the care of] your own souls»
— that is, your own souls, you, all the Muslims. A man gives his concern only to himself and to his Muslim brethren, enjoining them and forbidding them.
«those who go astray will not harm you when you have been guided»

— if the Christians and the Jews are in error and you Muslims are upon guidance, that does not harm you. For this reason, when they supposed that the verse was about abandoning the enjoining of the good and the forbidding of the wrong, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

⟨Enjoin the good upon one another and forbid one another the wrong, until, when you see avarice obeyed, caprice followed, this world preferred, and every man of an opinion pleased with his own opinion.⟩
When the world has become corrupt to the point that enjoining the good and forbidding the wrong is of no benefit, then at that point hold to your own particular selves.
«To Allah is your return, all together»
— this return of yours is to Allah —
«then He will inform you of what you used to do»
«O you who have believed, testimony among you when there comes to one of you»

) in its parsing, its commentary, its meaning and its ruling. The occasion of its revelation: Tamīm al-Dārī and ʿAdī his brother, and the two of them were Christians upon the religion of the Christians, travelled to Syria, and with them was Budayl, the client of ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ al-Sahmī. Budayl was a Muslim and his two companions were Christians, Tamīm al-Dārī and ʿAdī his brother. When they were midway along the road Budayl fell ill, and he wrote a document in which were the names of all his goods and hid it inside the goods, and he charged the two of them:
⟨When I die, deliver these goods to ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ al-Sahmī.⟩

Then he died, and the two of them searched the goods and saw a goblet — a vessel of silver inlaid with three hundred mithqāls of gold — and they sold it for a thousand dīnārs and divided it between themselves. When they returned to Medina they delivered the goods to ʿAmr, and he searched them and saw the document and read what was in it, and saw the mention of the goblet.
So he came to the two of them and said to them:
⟨Your companion — perhaps he sold something of his goods before his death?⟩
⟨No; he did not reach the place of the market, he died on the road.⟩
⟨Perhaps his illness was prolonged and he disposed of some of his property?⟩
⟨Then this goblet of silver, whose value is such and such — he mentioned it in his document.⟩

So ʿAmr came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and the two verses came down. After a time the goblet was found in Mecca; rather, Tamīm al-Dārī embraced Islam and acknowledged the truthfulness of the Qurʾan — that the two of them had stolen the goblet and sold it for a thousand dīnārs; and he himself returned five hundred dīnārs, and he went to the heirs of his companion and took from them five hundred dīnārs. Concerning that case these verses came down:
«the bequest: two men of probity from among you»
— what suffices by way of testimony is two Muslim men —
«or two others from other than you»
— if they do not find two Muslims, two others from outside your community bear witness, as Tamīm and ʿAdī did —
«in the land, and the affliction of death befalls you: you shall detain the two of them»
— you make the two of them stand —
— the two of them take an oath —
«by Allah, if you are in doubt»
about it. And the two of them say:
«We will not take in exchange for it»
«even though he be a near relative; and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed we then»
(Q. 5:106). So the Messenger ﷺ summoned the two of them after the prayer of
the afternoon, and he made the two of them stand, and they swore — two unbelievers who took no care for the oath; they swore by Allah falsely.
«But if it is discovered that the two of them have incurred sin»
— and after a time it came to light, after their oath, that the two of them had lied; Tamīm acknowledged it when he embraced Islam —
«then two others shall stand in their place from among those against whom the claim was established, the two nearest of kin»
— then the heirs come forward and the two of them swear in place of the two unbelievers, from among the relatives of the deceased —
«and the two shall swear by Allah: our testimony is truer than the testimony of those two, and we have not transgressed; indeed we would then be among the wrongdoers»

(Q. 5:107). When the second verse came down, the Messenger ﷺ sent to ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ, and he stood up and swore, he and a companion of his; the two of them swore by Allah that the two Christians had lied in what they had sworn to, and that it was the two of them who had stolen the goblet. So the Messenger ﷺ gave judgement against the two of them. And when Tamīm embraced Islam he acknowledged the truthfulness of the Qurʾan and returned the property.
— the ruling mentioned, the returning of the oath to the heirs —
(Q. 5:108). Since the oath passed over to the heirs, that is closer to the establishing of the right than

is not said of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; perhaps that is because of the tāʾ of the feminine. One says

that they would bring him something of clay, and he would shape it into a bat, and he would blow into it, and it would fly by the permission of Allah. The bat is the most complete of

the birds: it has no feathers, and it does not lay eggs but gives birth as the animals give birth, and it menstruates, and it laughs, and it sees in the darkness and does not see in the light. Allah informed ʿĪsā, the spirit of Allah, that when he shaped clay and blew into it, there would come out a bird resembling the bat, until it passed from the sight of the people and fell down dead — a distinction between the creating of Allah and the creating of what is originated.

— when a human being born blind, or a leper, was brought to him, he wiped him and he was healed —

when they intended to kill you —

— I commanded them by his tongue —

— are you able to ask your Lord — or
— is your Lord able, that is, will your Lord do —

— to ask for it, for the sake of —

— be settled, by an increase of certainty —

(Q. 5:113). When they had made plain the reason for their asking, ʿĪsā rose and performed the ablution and put on wool and prayed two cycles of the prayer (
«ʿĪsā son of Maryam said: O Allah, our Lord, send down upon us a table from heaven that shall be for us»
— on the day of its coming down —
— which we magnify and hold in honour —
«for the first of us and the last of us»
— of those who come after us —
— of Your power and of my prophethood —
«Indeed I am sending it down upon you; so whoever disbelieves afterward»
«of you, him I shall punish with a punishment wherewith I punish no other of the worlds»
(Q. 5:115). So the angels came down with it from heaven, upon it seven loaves and seven fish, and they ate of it until they were filled. Ibn ʿAbbās said this. And in a hadith:

⟨The table was sent down from heaven with bread and meat, and they were commanded not to act treacherously and not to store up for the morrow; but they acted treacherously and stored up, and so they were transformed into apes and swine.⟩

ʿĪsā, upon him be blessings and peace — his people asked that a table be sent down to them from heaven, so he prayed two cycles of the prayer and supplicated Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with this supplication:
«O Allah, our Lord, send down upon us a table from heaven»
— and then there was a cloud with a cloud above it, and between the two of them the table, until it came down before ʿĪsā, upon him be blessings and peace. He said:
⟨Let the most godfearing of you toward Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and the most hallowed of you, uncover — let him uncover this.⟩
They said: that is you. Shamʿūn said to him:
So ʿĪsā uncovered it, and there was a fish that had no bones, cooked, part of it with olives and part of it with honey, and in it were all the kinds of food. ʿĪsā said to them:
⟨Eat, and give thanks to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and do not store up, for every day it will come to you; and do not betray. Carry out Allah's command and leave off His prohibitions.⟩
Whoever ate of this food: if he was poor he became rich, and if he was sick he became sound, and if he was lowly he became eminent. So they ate, and the matter was so.
Then after that they quarrelled over it, and they took and stored up, and ʿĪsā supplicated against them, and they were transformed into apes and swine, just as Allah had threatened them:
«Then indeed I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one among the worlds»
(Q. 5:115) — they were transformed into apes and swine.

This Table came down on a Sunday, and for this reason the Christians took Sunday as a feast day among them, down to this day of ours — just as the Jews took Saturday as a feast day among them. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
⟨You are the last, the foremost. Today is ours, and tomorrow is the Jews', and the day after tomorrow is the Christians'. This is the day which⟩
⟨they were given, and they differed over it, and Allah guided you to it: it is Friday.⟩
The feasts of the Muslims are at their completion of their acts of worship. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created this world [as] seven days. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

⟨This world is seven days.⟩ Its first is Saturday and its last is Friday. And Allah has made obligatory upon us five prayers in the day and the night; when Friday comes, and it is the seventh day, we have completed what is due from us of the prayers in the week. At the completion of what is due from us of the prayer in the week, Allah gave us Friday as a feast. For this reason we pray on Friday two cycles of the prayer (

), because a feast must have a sermon in it; the two sermons stand in the place of the two remaining cycles. The noon prayer is four cycles: two cycles are the two sermons, and two cycles are the prayer. This is the feast of the Muslims' completion of their prayer. And the second feast is the feast of their completion of their fasting, which is the day of the Breaking of the Fast; and the third feast is the feast of their completion of their hajj, which is the Feast of the Sacrifice. The Muslims have three feasts. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, manifests Himself to the people of the Garden, in the Garden, on the days of the feasts. So whoever has in the year only two feasts — the Breaking of the Fast and the Sacrifice — sees Allah in the Garden twice every year; and whoever has the feast of Friday sees Allah every week; and the people of the litanies — their feast is every morning and evening, and they see Allah every day, morning and evening; and the gnostics

their feasts are the number of their breaths, because all their breaths are with Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and so their feasts in the Garden became the number of their breaths, and at every feast they must see Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
