The Qurʾan is of two parts: Meccan suras and Medinan suras. The Meccan suras are marked out by being more concise and more eloquent, because those addressed are Quraysh, and they are the Arabs of pure and eloquent speech: they understand of Arabic what others do not understand. In the Medinan suras there is the long expansion and the amplification, because those addressed are the Jews, and they are not like Quraysh in understanding and in acuity; so the Medinan suras needed an expansion of the speech greater than the Meccan suras. For this reason you find eloquence and rhetorical excellence and composition and inimitability in the Qurʾan, the Meccan of it and the Medinan alike; but concision is greater in the Meccan suras than in the Medinan suras, for this cause. And the Qurʾan is inimitable: its eloquence, its rhetorical excellence, the beauty of its composition, its announcing of the unseen, its freedom from contradiction, and its being ever new with the passing of the days. There is nothing that points more plainly to the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ than the Qurʾan. The Prophet ﷺ was unlettered; he grew up among an unlettered people, in a barren waste of the earth. He never saw a scholar, nor ever sat with a scholar; and he himself neither read writing nor wrote, and he never sat with a scribe nor with a reader. Then he brought this Book, a single sura of which defeats us — we study it night and day and it slips away from us — and he neither writes nor reads, yet he brought us this Book; and what came down in Mecca and what came down in Medina is all upon one pattern of eloquence and rhetorical excellence and brilliance and composition. For this He, Blessed and Exalted, addressed us:
«Do they then not reflect upon the Qurʾan? And had it been from any other than Allah»
«they would have found in it much discrepancy»

(Q. 4:82). The author among us, when he writes on history or on anything else, and it stays with him a year and he then goes back over it, is bound himself to replace something and change it, for the turning of the age — all the more so if another man criticizes him. You find that the books of history written in a past age do not suit this age of ours. And this Qurʾan: fourteen centuries have now passed, and the Qurʾan is new with every century; no event comes about that contradicts the Qurʾan, ever. Every nation and every state makes a constitution, and when years have passed the age outstrips that constitution and it needs changing — even Senegal: they have now taken to changing their constitution these four years past. And the Qurʾan is the constitution of all, in every age and in every place; no event comes about that contradicts the Qurʾan, ever, or belies the Qurʾan. And he who brought it was unlettered, born in a land of mountains; he never saw a sea, nor ever a city. This comes from none but Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

[When] they accused the Prophet ﷺ of having learned this Book from someone else, they said: ⟨Perhaps it was from his journey to Syria.⟩ Yes: the Prophet, when he reached twelve years, Abū Ṭālib took him out to Syria; and when they drew near to Syria the monks said to him: ⟨Take this boy back. Let the Jews not see him, for they are envious and will kill him.⟩ So Abū Ṭālib took him back. In that span of time, is it possible that he learned this Qurʾan from the rabbis of the Jews in Syria? They accused him with another piece of silliness: there was a smith in Mecca called Jabr, a Christian smith who had read the former scriptures and who believed in the Prophet ﷺ. Whenever the harm done by Quraysh to the Prophet ﷺ grew severe, he would bid him be patient and would encourage him, and say to him: ⟨The prophets before you — thus was it done with them.⟩ — supporting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Whenever the harm done to him grew severe, he ﷺ would go and sit with him, for the comfort he found in his speech. So they said: Now we know whence Muhammad learned this Qurʾan — from this smith. And the smith does not speak Arabic;
the two of them cannot do without an interpreter.
«It is only a human being who teaches him. The tongue of him to whom they incline is foreign, and this is a clear Arabic tongue»
(Q. 16:103). They did not ponder the Qurʾan:
«Do they not then ponder the Qurʾan?»
This sura is Meccan — Sūrat al-Anʿām. It came down at one time. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
Glory be to Allah the Great, glory be to Allah the Great!
⟨This sura — seventy thousand angels escorted it, and they had a resounding chant of glorification.⟩
So when the Prophet ﷺ recited it, he ordered that it be written down, the whole of it, in a single night! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

⟨Whoever recites this sura, Allah appoints over him forty thousand angels who write for him the like of their worship until the Day of Resurrection; and an angel comes down from the seventh heaven with an iron mace with him, and when Satan means to whisper to him he strikes him, so that there are seventy veils between him and the devils. And on the Day of Resurrection, when he is raised from his grave, the Lord says: O man, walk in My shade on a day when there is no shade but My shade, and enter My Garden, and drink of al-Kawthar, for you are truly My servant and I am your Lord.⟩
And three verses from the beginning of this sura — whoever recites them every

and the sunna of the Messenger — the Qurʾan said:
«And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it»
(Q. 59:7). Rather, in the Qurʾan there is everything. Ibn ʿAbbās says: ⟨Even the hobble of my camel, if it strays from me, I am able to find it in the Qurʾan.⟩
A story: I was at Rabat last year, and we were in a place in which the Christians and the Muslims and the boys had gathered. A Christian, who knew Arabic, said: the Qurʾan says
«We have not neglected anything in the Book»

(Q. 6:38) — and I have seen a thing that is not small, a very great thing, and the Qurʾan has not mentioned it. A boy said to him: and what is it? He said to him: the Qurʾan mentioned Mecca as a town, and mentioned Egypt as a town, and I know a town much greater than the two of them, and the Qurʾan has not named it. The boy said to him: and what is this town? He said to him: Paris. He said to him: the Qurʾan has mentioned it —
«I shall show you the abode of the transgressors»
I was waiting, so that if the lad proved unable I would answer him; but the lad answered him with an answer better than every answer. He said to him:
«I shall show you the abode of the transgressors»
«We have not neglected anything in the Book, then unto their Lord they shall be gathered»

(Q. 6:38) — and judgement is passed between them, and retaliation is exacted for the hornless beast from the horned. Al-Shāfiʿī was asked about these ships of the sea and of the land: whence has the Qurʾan mentioned them? Al-Shāfiʿī said:
«And horses and mules and donkeys, for you to ride them, and as adornment; and He creates what you do not know»
(Q. 16:8). These ships, all of them, have entered into
«and He creates what you do not know»
. I was asked about this question in Medina. I mentioned to them al-Shāfiʿī's answer, and I said to them: and I see a second answer
«And there is not a thing but that with Us are its storehouses, and We do not send it down save in a known measure»
— as to hearing them with a listening of acceptance —
«He leads astray; and whom He wills»

Abū Jahl was sitting one day, and Iblīs came to him and said to him: take this idol of yours and set it down with the Messenger ﷺ; perhaps you will hear from him what will gladden you. Abū Jahl's idol was inlaid with jewels and rubies. So Abū Jahl carried his idol and set it before the Messenger ﷺ, and said to it: this is Muhammad — he reviles us and curses our gods and taunts us continually, and you are our god, and you avail nothing at all in this.

So Satan entered into the idol and spoke, and he fell to cursing the Prophet ﷺ and reviling him. The Prophet ﷺ grew angry and entered his house, and one who had come knocked at the door upon him and said to him: command me with whatever you wish and I shall do it. The Messenger ﷺ said to him: who are you? He said: I am a jinnī. I was in the seventh earth, and when the idol spoke before you what it spoke, Jibrīl summoned me to come; and I have killed the Satan who spoke in the hollow of the idol, and I have come to you that you may command me with whatever you wish. The Messenger ﷺ said to him: what is your strength? He said to him: I am able to bring together the two mountains of Abū Qubays and Quʿayqiʿān and to lay waste what is between them. The Messenger ﷺ said to him: Allah suffices me. He said to him: go back to the idol. And the Prophet ﷺ went back, and the idol fell to saying: there is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; I am an idol, I avail nothing, I neither profit nor harm; I am an idol; there is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; believe in Muhammad — the truth is with him. Abū Jahl grew angry and broke it, and said: Muhammad has bewitched everything, until he has bewitched the idols. This one — had Allah willed his guidance He would have guided him, but He did not will it.
«if Allah's punishment should come upon you»
«or the Hour should come upon you»
— the Resurrection, which comprises it, suddenly —
«would you call upon any other than Allah?»
the idols profit you, so call upon them.
«and He removes that for which you call»
[that is, you call] that He should remove from you the harm and the like of it, if He wills to remove it —
(Q. 6:41) — with Him, of the idols; so you do not call upon them.
«And We did indeed send to nations before you»
«Then why, when Our might came to them, did they not humble themselves»
— would that they had humbled themselves when Our might came to them; that is, they did not do that, though what called for it was present —
— so they did not soften to faith —
«and Satan made alluring to them what they used to do»
(Q. 6:43) — of acts of disobedience, and so they persisted in them.
— they were admonished and made to fear
— of the hardship and the adversity — and they did not take heed —
«We opened upon them the gates of everything»
(being drawn on to ruin by degrees) for them —
«until, when they rejoiced in what they were given»
— We destroyed them with the punishment —
«and at once they were in despair»
«So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off»
their last, in that they were extirpated.
«And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds»
(Q. 6:45) — for the victory of the messengers and the destruction of the unbelievers.
Praise is obligatory in every condition. Praise for safety, and praise for the destruction of the enemies, and praise in the time of blessing. The praise of Nūḥ — and Nūḥ's praise was for safety:
«It was said: O Nūḥ, descend in peace from Us, and blessings upon you and upon nations from among those with you»
(Q. 11:48) — and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. As for the community of Muhammad, they are the praisers (

); they were named in the former Books as being the praisers. Their messenger is Muhammad and Aḥmad, and the head of their Book is: praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. When they eat they say: praise be to Allah; and when they drink they say: praise be to Allah; and when they clothe themselves they say: praise be to Allah; and when they wake they say: praise be to Allah; and when they die it is said: praise be to Allah; and when they are raised up they say: praise be to Allah; and when they enter the Garden they say: praise be to Allah; and their banner on the Day of Resurrection is the Banner of Praise. The praising community that was praised in the Torah and the Gospel is this community — and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. When Allah bestows a blessing upon His servant he says: praise be to Allah, praise be to Allah by whose blessing good works are completed; and when an affliction befalls he says: praise be to Allah in every condition. Praise at
affliction, because every affliction, however far it may reach in severity, it lay within the power of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that it be more severe
than what it is; so then praise is obligatory upon him in every condition.
«and set a seal upon your hearts»
— stamped them, so you do not
«who is a god other than Allah who could bring it to you?»

— with what He took from you, by your claim. If Allah were to take these three — among the most exalted of Allah's blessings upon His servant is the hearing faculty. The Qurʾan always puts hearing before sight, because the attachment of faith to hearing is stronger than its attachment to sight. A man hears the verses (

) of Allah even if he is blind, and he believes in Allah; and were it not for hearing, guidance would never have been possible for him. So hearing is more profitable than sight. This hearing faculty, and this seeing faculty, and this perceiving faculty — the heart — are three blessings; were Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to take them, the servant would never find anyone to bring them to him.
(Q. 6:46). They used to worship gods, but they could not claim that their gods would bring them this.
«Say: Have you considered — if the punishment of Allah came upon you suddenly or openly»
«would any be destroyed but the wrongdoing people?»
(Q. 6:47) — the unbelievers; that is, none are destroyed but they.
«And We send not the messengers except as bearers of good tidings»
— to whoever believes, of the Garden —
— to whoever disbelieves, of the Fire —
«no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve»
«And those who denied Our signs — the punishment shall touch them for that they used to transgress»
«I do not say to you that with me are the treasuries of Allah»
— I do not say to you that I know the unseen, what is hidden from me and has not been revealed to me —
«nor do I say to you that I am an angel»
«I follow only what is revealed to me. Say: are the blind»
«and the seeing equal? Will you not then reflect?»

(Q. 6:50). He mentioned in this verse that the Prophet ﷺ does not claim that the treasuries of Allah are with him, nor does he claim knowledge of the unseen, nor does he claim that he is an angel; for a claim is ugly even when it is sound.
— this does not indicate that he does not have them.
«I do not say to you that with me are the treasuries of Allah»
with me the treasuries of Allah.
«And nor do I know the unseen»
— I do not say to you that I know the unseen, even though I do know the unseen.
«And nor do I say to you that I am an angel»
— even though I am more exalted in rank than the angels.
«I follow only what is revealed to me»
The Messenger ﷺ follows only what is revealed to him, and this agrees with His word
«Nor does he speak from caprice; it is only a revelation revealed»
(Q. 53:3–4). By this some of the ulama held fast who said that the Messenger has no independent judgement (
«I follow only what is revealed to me»
«Nor does he speak from caprice; it is only a revelation revealed»
. The correct view is that he has
[leave] to exercise independent judgement; and when he exercises it, it falls within the revelation, on the evidence of the verse (
«We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you»

(Q. 4:105). When he exercises independent judgement and arrives at an opinion, it is what Allah has commanded in the Qurʾan, and so his independent judgement is revelation. He who said that he exercises independent judgement spoke truly, and so did he who said that he does not: he follows only what is revealed to him. Among them are those who annulled analogy (
), [holding] that the ruling of the law is the Qurʾan and the sunna only. But analogy — another verse brought it:
«If you dispute over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger»
«And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those of them who draw out the meaning would have known it»
«those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord; they have, apart from Him»
(Q. 6:51) — by their desisting from what they are in.
«And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, desiring His face»

(Q. 6:52). The occasion of the revelation of this verse is that the chiefs of the polytheists came to the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ and found him ﷺ sitting, and with him were ʿAmmār and Bilāl and Ṣuhayb and Salmān al-Fārisī, the poor among the Muslims, the People of the Bench (

). They addressed the Prophet ﷺ: are you not ashamed to sit with these? Drive them away, if you would like us to believe in you and to sit with you. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨I am not one to drive away the believers.⟩ They said: then appoint for us two assemblies — an assembly in which you sit with the poor, and when we come to you, you set us apart by ourselves in an assembly until we go, and then you may sit with them if you wish. ʿUmar said to the Messenger ﷺ that he should accept this from them, so that they might see whether they would be guided or not. So the Prophet

ﷺ wished to accept that from them, out of desire for their guidance. So they said: order someone to write you a document to that effect. He called ʿAlī and was about to write, and then this verse came down:
«And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, desiring His face»

(Q. 6:52) — not anything of the trappings of this world; and they are the poor. The polytheists had impugned them and had asked that he drive them away so that they might sit with him. ʿUmar said: ⟨I offer you my excuse, O Messenger of Allah⟩ — because he had counselled accepting this opinion. And here is Nūḥ, upon him be blessing and peace: when they ordered him to drive away the weak among the believers he said
«I am not one to drive away the believers»

(Q. 26:114); and the Messenger ﷺ at first answered ⟨I am not one to drive away the believers⟩; but from the breadth of his mercy, when they asked of him that he appoint two assemblies for them, out of desire for their acceptance of Islam he inclined to this opinion, until Allah forbade him
Blessed and Exalted. This does not show that the Prophet ﷺ went against [the command], or that he is not preserved from error, on account of His words at the end of the verse,
«so that you drive them away and become one of the wrongdoers»
; for he did not resolve upon driving them away, but only upon dealing gently with those men, and he says:
⟨I was sent as one who deals gently, so deal gently.⟩
When the verse came down, the Prophet ﷺ drove the polytheists away and held firm to sitting with the poor.
«And no part of their reckoning is upon you»
— they had said: these men are not truthful in their submission, they are only poor men who live by being near you —
«in anything, nor any part of your reckoning upon them in anything, so that you drive them away and become one of the wrongdoers»
(Q. 6:52) — if you were to do that. People fall into classes. The sons of this world want this world only:
«Whoever desires the tillage of the hereafter, We increase for him in his tillage; and whoever desires the tillage of this world, We give him of it, and he has no share in the hereafter»
(Q. 42:20). And the sons of the hereafter want the hereafter:
«and strives for it with the striving due to it, being a believer — those, their striving shall be thanked»
(Q. 17:19). And the people of Allah want the face of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
«And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening desiring His face»
(Q. 6:52) — they want neither this world nor the next. The elect:

drew them away from the hand of this world and set them apart for the hereafter. As for the elect of the elect, He stripped them of this world and of the hereafter and set them apart for the beholding of His noble face. They are the people of Allah.

(Q. 6:53). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made a difference between the portions: He made a noble man and a lowly man, a rich man and a poor man — a trial by which He tried some of them through others. The noble man and the rich man, if they give thanks to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and humble themselves before the poor man and the lowly man, that is thankfulness on their part; and if they grow proud and withhold the due of the destitute, they have spurned the favour of Allah.

And the lowly man and the poor man, if they envy, they have not given thanks; and if they are steadfast, they have given thanks for the favour of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. People are either a rich man who gives thanks or a poor man who is patient. They differed over which of the two is better: it is said, the rich man who gives thanks; and it is said, the poor man who is patient

⟨Shall I not teach you something by which you may overtake those who have gone before you, and outstrip those who come after you, and none shall be more excellent than you save one who does the like of what you have done?⟩
They said: Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah. He said:
⟨You shall glorify Allah, and magnify Allah, and praise Allah after every prayer thirty-three times.⟩
⟨The poor among the Muhājirūn came back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: Our brethren, the people of wealth, have heard of what we did and have done the like of it.⟩
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
«That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills»
Had what they are upon been guidance, they would not have got to it before us. He, Exalted, said:
«Is not Allah best aware of the thankful»
(Q. 6:53) — to Him, and so guides them? Yes indeed.
«And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you. [Your Lord] has prescribed»
— Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave this community good tidings that He has prescribed mercy for Himself. He says:
«that whoever among you does an evil in ignorance»

— commits an act of disobedience in ignorance. Ignorance is of two kinds: the ignorance of straying, like the ignorance of the unbelievers; and an ignorance belonging to the deeply ignorant, an ignorance of […]. Ignorance is of two kinds: ignorance of Allah and of the rights of His divinity, which requires its possessor's everlasting abiding (
) in the Fire; and the ignorance which is the very
(gnosis) of Allah, which is ignorance of the innermost reality of the Essence inasmuch as it is what it is, and which requires its possessor's everlasting abiding in the Garden.
«And man bore it; indeed he was a wrongdoer, deeply ignorant»
(Q. 33:72). So then, whoever among you does an evil in ignorance
«And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you»
) is the greeting between Muslims among themselves in this world, and with it the angel greets them when they enter the Garden:
«Peace be upon you; you have been good»
(Q. 39:73) — until the Lord Himself greets them with peace:
«Peace — a word from a merciful Lord»
«Your Lord has prescribed mercy for Himself»
The first thing Allah, Blessed and Exalted, brought into being was the Pen. He said to it: Write. The Pen spoke: What shall I write? He said: Write

what has been and what shall be until the Day of Resurrection. So it began to write. Write: Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace — I shall send him to his people, and whoever believes in him I shall admit to the Garden, and whoever disbelieves in him I shall admit to the Fire. Write: Ibrāhīm, likewise. Write: Mūsā, likewise. ʿĪsā, likewise. Write: Muhammad. So it wrote Muhammad, and said: He is sent to his community, and whoever believes in him I shall admit to the Garden, and whoever disbelieves in him —
spoke: Observe proper comportment, O Pen; this is the

(the beloved). The Pen shuddered until it split, and so it does not write unless it is split. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write — the community of Muhammad is a community that sins, and I am a forgiving Lord, and My mercy has outstripped My wrath in their regard.
— the Qurʾan — so that the truth may appear and be acted upon —
«and so that there may become clear»
(Q. 6:55) — the path of the sinners, so that it may be shunned.
«Say: I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon»
«apart from Allah. Say: I do not follow your desires»
if I were to follow them.
«And I would not be among the rightly guided»
«Say: I am upon a clear proof»
«from my Lord, and you have denied it»
, that is, my Lord, in that you have associated partners with Him —
«I do not have that which you seek to hasten»
— they asked him to send the punishment down at once, and he answered:
«I do not have that which you seek to hasten»
— in that and in other than it —
«the truth, and He is the best of deciders»
«if I had that which you seek to hasten, the matter between me and you would have been decided»
— by my hastening it for you, so that I might be at rest; but it is with Allah —
— His treasuries, or the roads that lead to knowledge of it —
(Q. 6:59). None knows the unseen but Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and they are the five that are in His words, Exalted:
«Indeed Allah — with Him is the knowledge of the Hour»
(Q. 31:34), to the end of the verse. He has mentioned in this verse that the keys of the unseen — none knows them
but He. And the keys of the unseen — the hadith has explained them by the verse of Luqmān:

«Indeed Allah — with Him is the knowledge of the Hour; and He sends down the rain; and He knows what is in the wombs; and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow; and no soul knows in what land it will die»
We have seen many of the
(the friends of Allah) and of the righteous telling of these things before they occur, and the truth of what they have told of comes about. This does not conflict with
(Q. 6:59), because this is of the knowledge of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The unseen which […] save Allah is a single unseen: the coming of the Hour, and that alone. As for
«and He sends down the rain, and knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die»

(Q. 31:34) — the knowledge of all this is with some of the servants of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, by Allah's knowledge. Shaykh Aḥmad al-Tijānī, may Allah be pleased with him, says that were he to die
and be buried, and then taken out and asked about these five, he would surely tell of them.
«And He knows what is in the land»
— the villages which are upon the rivers —
«And no leaf falls but He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear book»
«And He it is who takes your souls by night»
«and He knows what you have committed»
«by day, then He raises you up therein»
— in the day, by returning your spirits —
— it is the term of life —
«then to Him is your return, then He will inform you of what you used to do»
(Q. 6:60) — and so He will requite you —
«until, when death comes to one of you»
«By those that tear out violently, and those that draw out gently»
(Q. 79:1–2). The Angel of Death has deputies over the seizing of spirits, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is in reality the one who seizes the spirits. For this He said:
«Say: the angel of death, who has been given charge of you, will take you»
«Allah takes the souls at the time of their death»

(Q. 39:42). The one who seizes in reality is Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and He deputes the angel. The angel, when he is commanded to seize the spirit of a servant, seizes it; and a servant whose spirit he has not been commanded to seize — he is powerless to approach him. And the servant: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has appointed over him angels who guard him, one on his right and one on his left, and one before him and one behind him, and the two keepers who write down everything he sends forward of deed, good or evil. And of the prevailing of His mercy: Raqīb is on the man's right and ʿAtīd on his left, and Raqīb is the commander over ʿAtīd. When he does a good deed, he commands that it be written ten times, or more, up to seven hundred. And when he does an evil deed, ʿAtīd does not write it unless Raqīb commands him; he says: give him respite for six hours — if he repents, or asks forgiveness, or does a good deed, do not write it. And when six hours have passed and the servant has not asked forgiveness and has not done a good deed, he says to him: write it a single time. The Messenger ﷺ says:
⟨Woe to him whose ones have overcome his tens.⟩

The good deed is tenfold its like, and the evil deed is written only as a single evil deed, and if he asks forgiveness within the space of six hours it is not written. So whoever is heedless until these ones become more than these tens, he is heedless, and Allah is the granter of success.
«Then they are returned to Allah their Master»
— the established, the just — that He may requite them —
— the decree carried into effect upon them —
«and He is the swiftest of reckoners»
(Q. 6:62) — He reckons all creatures in the measure of half a day of the days of this world, for a hadith to that effect. Our master ʿAlī was asked: how does
Allah reckon creation in half a day? He said: how does He feed them in half a day?! He feeds them all, and that does not render Him powerless.
«who delivers you from the darknesses of the land and the sea»
«we shall surely be among the thankful»
«Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you»
— Allah is able to rain down upon the community stones from the heaven, or a cry —
— such as being swallowed up by the earth —
«and make some of you taste the violence of others»
(Q. 6:65) — by fighting. When this verse was revealed,
⟨O Allah, I seek refuge in Your face.⟩
⟨O Allah, I seek refuge in Your face.⟩
«or to confound you in sects and make some of you taste the violence of others»
⟨O Allah, I seek refuge in Your face.⟩
⟨The pen has dried; the decree has passed upon that.⟩
And for this the community does not cease to be divided, some of them making others taste violence.

It began with the killing of ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him, and so on and so forth. The sovereignty of divinity, when it attaches to a thing, is turned back neither by a sent prophet nor by an angel brought near. The most exalted of the prophets in station with Allah are three: Muhammad and Ibrāhīm
and Mūsā. Ibrāhīm — when Allah willed the destruction of the people of Lūṭ and he wanted to intercede for them:
«O Ibrāhīm, turn away from this. The command of your Lord has already come»

(Q. 11:76), and al-Khalīl was of no avail in it. And Mūsā — when the Arabs in their Jāhiliyya knew neither a god nor a messenger and were fighting the Children of Isrāʾīl, and the Children of Isrāʾīl in that age were Muslims while these were unbelievers in their Jāhiliyya, yet among them was one who is a forefather of al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ: Mūsā wanted to invoke [Allah] against these Arabs, and he was rebuked from the Presence, that he should not invoke against them. The sovereignty of divinity. And the Prophet ﷺ, when He said
«or to confound you in sects and make some of you taste the violence of others»
(Q. 6:65), said: ⟨O Allah, I take refuge in Your face.⟩ He said: the Pen has run dry.
— those that point to Our power —
«by your people, while it is the truth»
«Say: I am not a guardian over you»
— not a compeller, that I should requite you; I am only a warner, and your affair rests with Allah (Q. 6:66) — and this was before the command to fight.
— a time at which it falls out —
«And when you see those who plunge into Our signs»
«until they plunge into some other talk. And if Satan should make you forget»
— move you to forgetfulness, so that you sat with them —
«then do not sit, after the reminder,»
— when you remember, do not sit with them —
(Q. 6:68). And the Muslims said: if we rise every time they plunge [into such talk], we shall not be able to sit in the mosque or to make the circumambulation. So there came down:
«And nothing is upon those who fear»
— that is, of those who plunge [into such talk] —
«And leave those who have taken their religion»
«and whom the life of this world has deluded»
— so do not concern yourself with them; this was before the command to fight.
«lest a soul be given up to destruction»
— lest a soul be delivered over to perdition —
«there is not for it, besides Allah,»
— to ward off the punishment from it —
«it will not be taken from it»
«those are they who are given up to destruction for what they earned. For them is a drink of scalding water»
— water reaching the utmost of heat —
— by leaving it; and that is the idols —
«and be turned back upon our heels»
«like one whom the devils have lured away»
— perplexed, not knowing where he goes —
— to guide him to the road, and they say to him —
— but he does not answer them, and so he perishes —
— and what is other than it is error —
«and we have been commanded to submit»
«you establish the prayer and fear Him»
«and He it is to whom you will be gathered»
— you will be assembled on the Day of Resurrection for the reckoning (Q. 6:72).
«And He it is who created the heavens and the earth in truth»
and that thing is the Day of Resurrection: He says to creation, Arise, and they arise.
— the veracity that comes to pass inescapably —
«and to Him belongs the dominion on the day the Trumpet is blown»
— the horn; the second blast, from Isrāfīl. No one other than He has dominion on it:
«To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Overpowering»
«Knower of the unseen and the witnessed»
— what is absent and what is beheld —
— of the inward of things as of their outward (Q. 6:73).
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: what is the Trumpet? He said:
⟨A horn which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and in it is a hole for every spirit of all living creatures.⟩
And when Allah wills the passing away of this creation, He commands the angel to blow the Trumpet, and he blows the Trumpet:
«and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth is terrified»
(Q. 27:87). Then he blows a second time:
«and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth falls dead, save whom Allah wills»

a third time, and Allah raises up everyone who had died. The blasts are in reality two blasts: the blast of the swoon, at which he dies along with [all] created beings, and the blast of the raising. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
It was said to Abū Hurayra: forty years? He said: I decline. It was said: forty days? He said: I decline. That is, he refused to interpret it, because the Prophet ﷺ did not interpret it.

— whether it is forty years or forty months or forty days, Allah knows best. When the Trumpet has been blown so that the created beings have died, they remain forty, asleep; the sky rains upon them the water of semen and they grow — their bodies grow in that span — until, when it is blown a second time, they are raised. For this they say:
«Woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting-place?»
(Q. 39:68) — its interpretation will come: that they are the wide-eyed maidens of Paradise (

) or the four angels, Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl and Isrāfīl and ʿAzrāʾīl. They are the last to die, as will come. So when it is blown a second time — and this is after the raising of the Prophet ﷺ — he said: ⟨I am the first over whom the earth will split open, and I shall sit up straight, and I shall speak to Abū Bakr and he will rise, and I shall speak to ʿUmar and he will rise.⟩ When Allah wills to raise all created beings, He sends Jibrīl and the servant of the Garden and al-Burāq and servants with them: bring me my beloved, this is the Day of Resurrection. Then they lose the way. They say: Jibrīl, you are the one who knows the road to Medina, because you went to and fro to it often. So Jibrīl leads them to the burial-place of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they awaken the Prophet ﷺ and clothe him, and he mounts his beast and goes to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. After that the Trumpet is blown, and all created beings are raised, and they are gathered to the place of gathering. The hadith of the raising and the intercession will come at its full length.
«when Ibrāhīm said to his father Āzar»
— Āzar is his byname; his name is Tārakh —
— worshipping them? An interrogative of rebuke —

(Q. 6:74). Ibrāhīm speaks to his father Āzar, forbidding him the worship of idols; and this runs against the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ saying that Allah moved him through the loins of believing men and believing women, from Ādam, from Shīth, to Ibrāhīm, to Ismāʿīl, to ʿAdnān, to ʿAbd Allāh and Āmina — that he was not born of fornication but of sound marriage. Ibn ʿAbbās said: ⟨I wrote out five hundred forefathers for the Prophet ﷺ; I did not see unbelief among them.⟩ How this is reconciled
This, along with his being of the progeny of Ibrāhīm — and Ibrāhīm says this to his father? Answers have been given to it. The ulama answered that this preservation from sin (

) belongs to the forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ so long as the light of the Prophet ﷺ is in their loins; but once the light has passed on, that one is merely like any one of creation. And Āzar, at the time he was worshipping the idols — the light had already passed to Ibrāhīm. This answer is not satisfactory. The Qurʾan supports that the forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ were all of them Muslims, by His saying
«and your turning about among those who prostrate»
(Q. 26:219) — that is, in the loins of those who pray.

The best that has been answered on this is what our shaykh, Shaykh al-Tijānī, may Allah be pleased with him, answered. He said: ⟨Āzar is a paternal uncle of Ibrāhīm, and the eloquence of the Qurʾan yields this. A man's father who begot him — he does not say of him 'my father so-and-so'; he says only 'my father'. And when it is said 'my father so-and-so', its meaning is only the paternal uncle. So had Āzar been Ibrāhīm's father, He would have been content with His saying:⟩
«And when Ibrāhīm said to his father»

(Q. 6:74) ⟨— this is another father, other than the father.⟩ If this is sound the difficulty is removed; and if not, then what is ruled out of the forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ is fornication, and that the light of the Prophet ﷺ should come into being without a contract of marriage — and the marriages of the unbelievers are valid in the shariʿa of Islam. In sum: this Āzar, Ibrāhīm addressed him:
«Do you take idols as gods? Indeed I see you and your people in manifest error»
(Q. 6:74). He said this speech when he was sixteen months old.
«And thus We show Ibrāhīm the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that he might be of those who are certain»
(Q. 6:75). Namrūd saw a fire that came out of some of the houses and burned

his kingdom. So he asked the astrologers about this vision. They said to him: A child will be born among these people who will be the cause of your kingship's passing away. He said: Then my kingship shall never pass away. So he separated the men from the women and forbade that a man should come to his wife, and a man came to see his wife only in the days of menstruation — they used to keep away from women in the time of menstruation, and everyone whose wife menstruated was given leave to go in to her. It happened that a need arose for Namrūd, and he sent the father of Ibrāhīm, who was his minister, to go to the town and attend to his need for him, and [warned] him against going near his wife. He said to him: I am more jealous for your kingship than you are; I shall never go near her. And when he entered the village and had attended to the king's need, he went in to the woman, and Allah made her fair in his eyes, and he had no command of himself until he lay with her. So she conceived Ibrāhīm. And when she had conceived Ibrāhīm, Allah concealed the pregnancy: whenever the pregnancy grew, the belly grew small, and the marks of pregnancy did not appear upon her, until the time of her delivery came. She fled to the open country and entered a cave — it had been a spring that had sunk away — and she bore him in it, and there he was, Ibrāhīm. She covered the mouth of the cave with a stone and returned to the village, and she became pure on the instant, as a protection from Allah, Blessed and Exalted. She took to going back and forth to him, and would find him sucking from his fingers: water from this finger, milk from this one, honey from this one, oil from this one, dates from this one. And he grew in a month as a child grows in a year, and after sixteen months he became a strong young man.

His mother came to him. When Ibrāhīm looked at her he said: O my mother, who is my Lord? She said: I am your Lord. He said: And who is your Lord? She said: My Lord is your father. He said: And who is my father's Lord? She said: Namrūd. He said: And who is Namrūd's Lord? She fled and came to her husband and told him the news. She said to him: The child he used to fear is this son of mine; come and hear from him. So he came to Ibrāhīm. He said to him: O my father, who is my Lord? He said: Your Lord is your mother. He said: And who is the Lord of
my mother? He said: I am. He said: And who is your Lord? He said: Namrūd. And who is Namrūd's Lord? He slapped him. So he went away from him and took to looking, wishing to know his Lord.
«And when the night grew dark over him»
— they brought him out of the cave; this was the first time he had seen the sky —
— it is al-Zuhara. He said to his people, and they were astrologers —
«he said: this is my Lord. But when it set, he said: I love not those that set»
(Q. 6:76) — that I should take them as lords, because change is not possible for the Lord —
«But when he saw the moon rising»
«he said: this is my Lord. But when it set, he said: if my Lord does not guide me I shall surely be of the people who go astray»
«But when he saw the sun rising»
— and on the morrow he saw the sun, the first time he had seen it —
«he said: this is my Lord, this is greater»
— greater than the star and the moon —
«he said: O my people, I am quit of what you associate»
(Q. 6:78) — with Allah, of the idols and the originated bodies —
«Indeed I have turned my face to Him who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining to the truth, and I am not of those who associate»
— as We showed him the straying of his father —
«We show Ibrāhīm the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that he might be of those who are certain»
(the divine oneness); Allah, Blessed and Exalted, never mentioned him but that He declared him quit of
because he said: this is my Lord. Had he meant that the star was his lord, this would have been
; but he did not mean the star. At that time he was immersed in

, seeing nothing but Allah, Blessed and Exalted. When he saw the star he said: this is my Lord. I say: had he meant the star he would have said 'that', because it is far from him; and of the sun he would have said 'that one', because it is feminine. But on every occasion he said
— his Lord is nearer to him than these things; he means the real Lord. For this reason, whenever Allah mentions him He says
«and he was not of those who associate»
, and the annihilation of the prophets does not last long. So too the
: when Allah wills for a servant that others should benefit by him, He annihilates him and restores him on the instant; he returns to his senses and others benefit from him. Ibrāhīm said
when he saw the sun. He came to himself:
«O my people, I am quit of what you associate»
«Indeed I have turned my face to Him who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining to the truth, and I am not of those who associate»
«Ibrāhīm the dominion of the heavens and the earth»
(Q. 6:75). He mentioned that Allah showed Ibrāhīm the
(the unseen dominion) of the heavens and the earth. The
is what is hidden and the
(dominion) is what is manifest: the unseen and the witnessed, this world and the hereafter, the sensory (
), the outward and the inward, creation and command, the
— all these are synonymous names. The
is what is manifest and the
is what is hidden. Allah showed Ibrāhīm the
of the heavens and the earth, and He showed Muhammad
«Glory be to Him who carried His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed, that We might show him of Our signs»
in the case of Muhammad ﷺ; and for Ibrāhīm,
«the dominion of the heavens and the earth»
in it. This does not require that Ibrāhīm is of loftier station than Muhammad. Rather, Ibrāhīm was shown the
of the heavens and the earth, and Muhammad was shown some of the signs — but the signs of what? They are not the signs of the heavens nor the signs of the earth:
— the signs of Allah. That Presence has no end, and for this reason the servant can do nothing but look upon some of it while some remains.
— they argued with him about his religion and threatened him with the idols, that they would strike him with evil —
«he said: do you dispute with me»
— the Exalted [has guided me] to it —
«and I do not fear what you associate with Him»
— of the idols, that they should strike me with evil, since they have no power over anything; your idols are nothing —
«that my Lord should will a thing»
— if my Lord wills something hateful, it strikes me —
«My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge»
«And how should I fear what you have associated»
— with Allah, when they neither harm nor profit —
— you threaten me with fear of your gods, and you do not fear Allah —
«that for which He has not sent down»
— a proof and a demonstration; and He is the one powerful over everything —
«so which of the two parties is more deserving of security»
(Q. 6:81) — who is the more deserving of it, we or you? We are. The Exalted said:
«Those who believe and have not confounded»
in this verse, and He mentioned it in another verse:
«Do they feel secure from the scheme of Allah? None feels secure from the scheme of Allah except the losing people»
«Those who believed and did not confound their faith with wrongdoing — those have security, and they are rightly guided»
(Q. 6:82). So security is of two kinds: the security of the people of the divine overpowering and of loss. They were addressed with His saying:
«Do they feel secure from the scheme of Allah? None feels secure from the scheme of Allah except the losing people»

(Q. 7:99). They opposed the command of Allah and did not draw near to Him, and with that they felt secure. This security is a scheme; its possessor ends in loss. And the security of the people of the divine gentleness, who arrived at the presence of Lordship and believed with a complete faith in which there is no
(associating partners with Allah). The wrongdoing is
«O my son, do not associate [partners] with Allah; indeed associating partners is a great wrong»
(Q. 31:13). Those felt secure — Allah informed [us] that they felt secure — and their security did not prevent them from guidance.
«Those who believed and did not confound their faith with wrongdoing — those have security, and they are rightly guided»
(Q. 6:82). You find among the prophets and the

(the friends of Allah) one who is made certain of his felicity and his triumph and his entering the Garden, and this is not security from the scheme of Allah, because that security does not belong to that rank.
— with which Ibrāhīm argued for the oneness of Allah, from the setting of the stars and what comes after it —
We directed him to it as an argument
«against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will»
«We guided. And Nūḥ We guided before»
«and of his descendants Dāwūd and Sulaymān»
«do We recompense the doers of good»
— the son of Maryam. This yields that 'descendants' takes in the children of the daughter —
— the son of the brother of Hārūn, the brother of Mūsā —
the son of Hārān, the brother of Ibrāhīm.
«and their descendants and their brethren; and We chose them»
«and guided them to a straight path»
— the religion to which they were guided —
«is the guidance of Allah; He guides by it whom He will of His servants. And had they associated [others with Him]»
«from them what they used to do»
«Those are the ones to whom We gave the Book»
— in the sense of the books —
«and prophethood. So if there disbelieve in them»
— We have set them in readiness for it —
«to a people who are not disbelievers in it»
(Q. 6:89) — they are the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār —
«Those are the ones whom Allah has guided»

— follow them all, O Muhammad, may Allah bless you and give you peace. This verse is the most telling proof of the superiority of the Messenger ﷺ over all the prophets and the messengers. Allah mentioned them, each one, and every one of them has a praiseworthy quality in which he surpassed the rest. All of them took on all the praiseworthy traits, but each of them was singled out by a quality for which he became known. Dāwūd and Sulaymān were of the people of thankfulness: they joined kingship and prophethood together and gave thanks to Allah, Blessed and Exalted; so the two of them are of the people of thankfulness. And Ayyūb was of the people of steadfast patience. And Mūsā of the people of the dazzling miracles. And Zakariyyāʾ and Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā of the people of renunciation of this world. And Yūsuf combined steadfast patience and thankfulness: in his beginning patient, and in his end thankful. Since they took on these traits, each one of them, Muhammad ﷺ was commanded to follow the example of them all. This is a proof that he is more excellent than all of them, because there was gathered in him what was dispersed among them.
«Say: I ask of you for it»
«no reward. It is only a reminder»
«And they did not measure Allah with His true measure»
(Q. 6:91). It came down concerning Mālik b. al-Ṣayf. The Jews sent him to the Messenger ﷺ at Mecca, and when he came to dispute with
the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: ⟨I adjure you by Allah: have you read in the Torah that Allah hates the fat rabbi?⟩ And he himself was a fat rabbi. So he grew angry and said:
«Allah has not sent down anything upon any human being»

(Q. 6:91). When he returned, the Jews blamed him, and he said: Abū al-Qāsim angered me, so I said this. They said: so when you are angry you disbelieve in Allah and disbelieve in what Allah has sent down? And he was their rabbi, so they deposed him and put Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf in his place, [one worse than him].
— they did not magnify Him as He deserves to be magnified, or they did not know Him as He deserves to be known —
«Allah has not sent down anything upon any human being. Say: who sent down the Book which Mūsā brought, a light and a guidance for the people, which you make into sheets»
— they write it in separated quires —
— that is, you disclose of it what you like to disclose —
— of what is in it, such as the description of Muhammad ﷺ —
— O you Jews, in the Qurʾan —
«what you did not know, neither you nor your fathers»
what was made obscure to you in the Torah — all of it the Qurʾan has explained for you.
— He sent it down; if they do not say it, there is no answer other than it —
«then leave them in their vain discourse»
«is a Book We have sent down, blessed»

(Q. 6:92) — abundant in blessing, abundant in good for whoever believes in it, and an evil for whoever disbelieves in it. And of its blessing is the endurance of this world, and the sprouting of the earth, and the raining of the sky, so long as the Qurʾan remains. When the Qurʾan is lifted away, a gentle wind comes, and by it every believer dies, and the unbelievers remain. So the endurance of good upon the earth lasts as long as the Qurʾan endures upon it. A blessed Book — it is this Qurʾan — blessed: it calls the common people to their Lord, and it guides the elect to their Lord, and it brings the elect of the elect to their Lord. And this
Qurʾan — its blessing is manifest. Whoever recites it attains a great reward, and whoever listens to its recitation likewise, and whoever holds the written codex (

) in his hand finds a recompense by that. A Muslim man died and was buried, and among the company who attended his burial there was a righteous man. When the people had departed, the righteous man heard a violent blow, and a black dog came out and addressed the righteous man. He said to it: Who are you? It said: I am his evil deed. And the blow that I heard — did it fall upon you, or upon him? It said: Rather upon me. I wanted to be joined to him, and a sura of the Qurʾan that he used to recite struck me and drove me out of the grave. He ﷺ says: ⟨Whoever recites the Qurʾan has for every letter ten good deeds. I do not say to you that alif lām mīm is a letter; rather I say that alif is a letter, and lām is a letter, and mīm is a letter.⟩ When the Qurʾan became famous for its blessing, and Musaylima the Liar laid claim to a Qurʾan with which to rival the Qurʾan, he sent envoys to the Prophet ﷺ: ⟨From Musaylima the Messenger of Allah to Muhammad the Messenger of Allah: the earth between us is two halves⟩ — until he said: ⟨Indeed We have given you the jewels⟩ — he wishes to rival Sūrat al-Kawthar — ⟨so pray to your Lord and proclaim aloud.⟩ This, for all the feebleness of its wording, is a lie. The jewels do not equal al-Kawthar, and we know of no jewels that Allah gave to the Messenger ﷺ in this world; and what comparison is there between jewels and the prayer? When the two came to the Messenger ﷺ, he said to them: ⟨Were it not that envoys are not to be killed, I would have killed you two.⟩ So they went to Musaylima and said to him:

⟨Muhammad the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — whenever a child of his companions falls ill they bring him to him, and he recites the Qurʾan over him, and Allah heals him.⟩ He said: ⟨Yes — bring me the sick.⟩ So when they brought him a sick man and he recited over him, he would die on the spot; and when they brought him one with inflamed eyes, he would go blind on the spot. Muhammad ﷺ would recite and spit into salt water, and it would become sweet; and whenever Musaylima spat into a well, that well sank away. Musaylima is not blessed.

(Q. 6:92). It was sent down upon the Prophet ﷺ over a period of twenty-three years, and whenever a verse came down they would write it on stones, and on the leaves of trees, and on bones; and the Qurʾan was not collected. Nine of his companions memorised the Qurʾan in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. When the Messenger ﷺ died, and Abū Bakr fought at al-Yamāma, and a company of the bearers of the Qurʾan were martyred, ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb came to Abū Bakr and said to him: ⟨I hold that this Qurʾan should be collected and written down, because martyrdom has become frequent among the bearers of the Qurʾan; and if this happens a second time, those who bear the Qurʾan will die out, and I fear that the Qurʾan will be taken away from us.⟩

Abū Bakr said to him: ⟨If the mountains of Tihāma were loaded upon me, they would be light upon me; but a thing the Messenger ﷺ did not do — there is no way to accept it.⟩ ʿUmar kept swearing to him until Allah gave light to the heart of the caliph, and he saw what ʿUmar saw. So the two of them summoned Zayd b. Thābit, who had been the scribe of the Prophet ﷺ — and Jibrīl used to present the Qurʾan to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ every year, and in the year of his death he presented the Qurʾan to him twice, each time in the presence of Zayd b. Thābit. The two shaykhs summoned him and said to him: ⟨We order you to write the Qurʾan for us.⟩ He said to them: ⟨The mountains of Tihāma are lighter upon me than that I should do a thing the Messenger ﷺ did not do.⟩ And he refused. So the two shaykhs swore to him until Allah gave light to his heart, and he accepted from them. And they said: Zayd is the one who undertakes the writing, and he writes no verse unless two upright witnesses testify to it. And they set about writing: whenever a verse was written, he would attach it

in its place in its sura, by the affirmation of twelve thousand of the Companions — and ⟨my community will not agree upon an error⟩ — until Zayd said: ⟨There remains of the Qurʾan only two verses, at the end of al-Tawba.⟩ A man of the Companions called Khuzayma came with these two verses. They sought a second [witness] and did not find him. Then they remembered that the Prophet ﷺ had one day stood him before them and said to them: ⟨I have made the testimony of this man stand in the place of two testimonies.⟩ So they wrote the two verses:
(Q. 9:128) — to the end of the sura. So the codex was completed, unordered, and it was with Abū Bakr; and when he died it was with

ʿUmar; and when ʿUmar died it was with Ḥafṣa. When ʿUthmān took charge — and he was of the bearers of the Qurʾan — he took this that had been collected and ordered it according to the order of the Qurʾan, from the beginning of al-Baqara to the end of the Qurʾan, in this order that is in the written copies today. ʿUthmān is the one who collected it thus, by the consensus of the Companions, and he wrote seven codices:

a codex that was in his own hand — it is the Imam [the master copy]; a codex he sent to Mecca; a codex he sent to Kūfa; a codex he sent to Egypt; a codex he sent to Baghdad; a codex he sent to Syria; and a codex he sent to the Maghrib. The reading of the Maghrib codex is the one that has reached us. — Last year, or two years ago, on my going to Cairo, I saw a codex in the hand of ʿUthmān, present now in Cairo, and a codex in the hand of ʿAlī. I never knew that this was in the world at all. —
— what was before it of the books —
«and that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it; and those who believe in the hereafter believe in it, and they are mindful of their prayer»
(Q. 6:92) — out of fear of its punishment.
«And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah»
«or says, It has been revealed to me, when nothing has been revealed to him»
— it came down concerning Musaylima the Liar —
«and who says, I shall send down the like of what Allah has sent down»
(Q. 6:93) — and they are the mockers [who said]:
«Had we willed, we could have said the like of this»
«when the wrongdoers are in the throes of death»
«and the angels stretching out their hands»
toward them in striking and torment, saying to them in rebuke:
— to Us, that We may seize them —
«Today you are recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say against Allah other than the truth»
— by the claim to prophethood and to inspiration, falsely —
«and because you used to be arrogant toward His signs»
(Q. 6:93) — you behaved haughtily. Had you seen this, you would have seen a dreadful thing.
— it is said to them when they are raised up —
«you have indeed come to Us alone»
— singly, apart from family and property and child —
«as We created you the first time»
«and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you»
— in this world, without your choosing —
— it is said to them in reproach —
«We do not see with you your intercessors»
«that they were, with respect to you,»
— your connection; your gathering is scattered —
«from you is what you used to claim»
«You have indeed come to Us alone»
(the divine oneness) is the way of
is a stripping away from all created things;
is that you single yourself out apart from every family and property and child; and
is that Allah alone remains in the heart, with no partner to Him. The beginning is in the end and the end is in the beginning. Man was born stripped bare, having no rag to cover his nakedness (

), and he will return to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in just that way. And the end is in the beginning: if he strips himself now of everything and Allah remains, he has entered a Garden such that he does not long for the Garden that is awaited.
«Indeed Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone»
— He who splits the grain for the plant, and the date-stone for the palm —
«He brings forth the living from the dead»
— as man and bird from the sperm-drop and the egg —
«Allah; so how are you turned away?»
(Q. 6:95) — so how are you turned away from faith, when the proofs stand? —
— who splits the column of dawn —
«and He made the night for repose»
in which created beings find rest from weariness —
«and the sun and the moon for reckoning»
— they run by a reckoning, that is, they succeed one another —
«And it is He who made for you the stars»
«that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of the land and the sea»
«And it is He who brought you into being»
«from a single soul, and there is a lodging-place»
— some of you, in the womb —
— some of you, in the loins —
«We have detailed the signs for a people who understand»
«And it is He who sent down water from the sky, and We brought forth»
— in it there is a shift of address (
«the growth of every thing, and We brought forth from it greenery»
— one part riding upon another, as the ears of wheat —
«and from the palm, from its spathe»
— the first thing that comes forth from it —
near one to another; and We brought forth —
«of grapes, and the olive and the pomegranate, resembling»
— O you who are addressed, with a looking of consideration —
«at its fruit when it bears fruit»
— the first of what appears, and how it is —
«And they made the jinn partners with Allah»
— and He it was who created them —
«for Him sons and daughters without knowledge»
— in that they said: ʿUzayr is the son of Allah, and the angels are the daughters of Allah —
«the Originator of the heavens and the earth»
«How should He have a son when He has had no consort»
— [every thing] whose nature it is to be created —
«and He is knowing of all things»
«That is Allah your Lord; there is no god but He, the Creator of all things; so worship Him»
«and He is guardian over all things»
— they do not see Him. Grasping is other than seeing: a man sees
a thing and does not grasp it —
— He sees them and grasps them. Just as we know Him and do not grasp Him, we see Him and do not grasp Him —
«There have come to you clear proofs»
— he sees, for the reward of his seeing is his —
— to them, and so goes astray —
— the evil consequence of his being led astray —
«and I am not a keeper over you»
(Q. 6:104) — a watcher over your deeds. I am only a warner.
— as We have made plain what has been mentioned —
— that is, you have read the books of those who went before —
«and so that We may make it clear to a people who know»
«Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord»
«there is no god but He; and turn away from the polytheists»
«And had Allah willed, they would not have associated partners; and We have not made you a keeper over them»
«and you are not a guardian over them»
— so that you should compel them to faith (Q. 6:107).
«And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah»
— it was revealed concerning a group who reviled the idols, whereupon the unbelievers reviled the Master, Mighty and Exalted. He, the Exalted, said:
«And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah»
«and so they revile Allah out of enmity»

— on this basis, every act of obedience that draws one on to disobedience is itself disobedience, because reviling the idols is an act of worship; but when it drew them on to reviling Allah they were forbidden it.
«Thus have We made fair-seeming to every community their deed»
«then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do»
«by Allah with their most earnest oaths that if a sign came to them»
«they would surely believe in it. Say: signs are only with Allah. And what will make you perceive that, when it comes, they will not believe»
— it had already gone forth in Allah's knowledge that they would not believe (Q. 6:109).
— We turn their hearts away from the truth —
— away from beholding the truth, so they do not believe —
«believe in it the first time, and We leave them»
O Allah, bless our master Muhammad and grant him peace.
«And even if We had sent down to them the angels»
(Q. 6:111). We mentioned that the sura came down all at once at Mecca, and this conflicts with this verse (

) having come down on account of the saying of the unbelievers, or with the unbelievers’ having proposed these signs and this sura having then come down, with these verses in it as an answer to them. As for a verse of this sura having an occasion of revelation of its own, after we have made clear that it came down all at once — that is among the things that are hard for the commentator. But in any case, the mockers of the Prophet ﷺ and of the Qurʾan — they were five, and they were of Quraysh: al-Aswad b. ʿAbd Yaghūth, and al-Aswad b. al-Muṭṭalib, and al-Ḥārith, and al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil, and Abū Jahl b. Hishām

to the Messenger ﷺ and said: Show us the angels. If you wish us to believe you, then show us the angels, that we may ask them. And once they said: Bring us Allah, that we may see Him and ask Him about your truthfulness. And once they said to him: Bring back to life for us Quṣayy b. Kilāb, our forefather, that we may ask him whether you are truthful or not.
«had sent down to them the angels»
«and the dead had spoken to them»
— and the dead spoke to them, such as Quṣayy b.
— and We added to that, until We gathered for them every
— in plain view, so that they beheld it —
— had all this come to pass they would not have believed, because of what had gone before in Allah’s knowledge —
— until Allah wills the faith of a servant, and so he becomes a believer; and whoever He does not will
his faith, he does not believe.

(Q. 6:111) — most people do not know that. Faith is by the will of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. For the sign, however great it be, does not bring [one] to faith except by the will of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
The greatest sign is the Day of Resurrection, and it has already been mentioned:
«And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden; and indeed they are liars»

(Q. 6:28). For it went before in pre-eternity that Allah sprinkled a sprinkling of light upon spirits, and those cannot but come to faith; and whoever missed that sprinkling, it cannot come about that he believe. And the signs profit none but the people of guidance and of divinely granted success. Every miracle of a prophet and every

(friend of Allah), whether it be of knowledge or other than that, is a training for the people of his time. So whoever is prepared is trained by the first indication and profits; and whoever has no preparedness in him says: had we seen a true guide we would have clung to his hem and attached ourselves to him, and we would have profited and we would have entered upon the path. And he whom Allah grants success, and whom the solicitude of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has met, finds the guide nearer to him than that he should seek him. For this He, Blessed and Exalted, told us that faith is by the will, not by the signs; for the signs are manifest to the eye, but none sees them except those granted success.
«And thus We appointed for every prophet an enemy»

— as We have made these men your enemies, We made for every prophet an enemy: Allah made Iblīs for Ādam, and made for Nūḥ his son Kanʿān, and for Ibrāhīm Namrūd, and for Mūsā Firʿawn (Pharaoh), and for ʿĪsā the Jews, and for Muhammad Abū Jahl and his people; and likewise He appointed [one] for every veracious one (
— and the rebels among the jinn —
— speciously decked out, drawn from falsehood —
«your Lord had willed, they would not have done it»

(Q. 6:112) — of unbelief and other than it, of what has been made alluring to them. And this was before the command to fight. Those enemies are a benefit to the servant of Allah whom He has chosen, because they disturb him and so he returns to his Creator and his Maker; for if he found in creation no one to harm him, he would incline to them by his nature and they would snatch away something of his heart. And

, Blessed and Exalted, loves to be alone in possession of the heart. So if your kind, and the sons of your kind, and the kinsfolk around you, agree with you in everything you love, and you see from them nothing but what you love, you must needs incline to them, and they take a great share of your heart if they do not take possession of it outright. And when harm disturbs you from every side, you return to your Creator and your Maker, and He chooses you for Himself; and this is better for you than this world and what is in it.
«and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the hereafter may incline to it»
— they incline to what the enemies of Allah deck out speciously —
«and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit»
(Q. 6:113) — of sins, so that they are punished for it.
«Shall I then seek other than Allah»
— a judge between me and you. They also wanted the Messenger to appoint a judge between them and him, while he seeks no judge other than Allah.
«And He it is who sent down to you the Book»
making clear in it the truth from the falsehood —
«And those to whom We gave the Book»
— the Torah, such as ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām and his companions —
«know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so be not among the doubters»
«And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled»
«And if you obey most of those on the earth»
«they will lead you astray from the way of Allah»
— in their disputing with you about the matter of carrion, when they said: what Allah has killed is more deserving that you eat it than what you have killed —
«who strays from His way, and He knows best the rightly guided»
(Q. 6:117) — and so He requites each of them.
«So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned»
— if you wish to eat, then eat of that over which the name of Allah was mentioned at its slaughtering —
«if you are believers in His signs»
«And what is it with you, that you should not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned»
«And He has set out in detail for you what He has forbidden you»
— He has made clear to you what He has forbidden you, in the verse (
«except what you have been compelled to»
— except a thing you are compelled to; necessities make the forbidden permissible. Whoever is compelled to eat carrion, carrion is lawful for him.
«And indeed many lead astray by their desires»
— by what their souls desire, of declaring carrion lawful and other things —
«Indeed your Lord — He knows best the transgressors»

(Q. 6:119) — those who pass beyond the lawful to the forbidden. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commanded in this verse that the animals be slaughtered in the name of Allah, and that is for a wisdom: because the throes of death are severe, so much so that the Messenger ﷺ said:
⟨Prompt your dying with 'there is no god but Allah'⟩

— it makes the throes of death easy for them, for the sweetness of the remembrance of Allah takes away the bitterness of the throes of death. So too the animals: when they are slaughtered in the name of Allah, the sweetness of the name of Allah takes away the bitterness of death. Whoever slaughters without the name of Allah has wronged the animal and committed an offence against it, and for this reason eating it is forbidden; and if it is slaughtered in the name of Allah it is lawful.
«And forsake the outward of sin and its inward»
«And He has set out in detail for you what He has forbidden you»
. The commentator said: in the verse
(Q. 5:3). They found this problematic, because the verse

was revealed in Sūrat al-Māʾida, and Sūrat al-Māʾida is among the last of what was revealed at Medina. How then can one argue from something in Sūrat al-Māʾida before it was revealed? The ulama gave several answers, among them that it was prior in the knowledge of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that in the ordering of the Qurʾan al-Māʾida comes before al-Anʿām, so that arguing from what is in Sūrat al-Māʾida is sound, because Allah's knowledge has in it neither past nor future. And it has been answered that the correct [sense of]
«And He has set out in detail for you what He has forbidden you»
(Q. 6:145), which is to come: the four forbidden things in that verse — and the sura is Meccan — are the four forbidden things

in Sūrat al-Baqara, and they are the four forbidden things in Sūrat al-Māʾida, exactly alike. The truth is that Allah, Blessed and Exalted — His presence has in it neither past nor future; so it is sound that He has made clear to you what He has forbidden you, even though the sura had not yet been revealed.
«And forsake the outward of sin and its inward»

(Q. 6:120). Sin is of two kinds, outward and inward. The outward is what a person commits with his limbs, and the inward is what he commits in his heart. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, forbade all of that. Killing a soul and fornication, for instance, are outward disobedience; and pride, envy, hatred and rancour — all these are inward acts of disobedience. Leave all of that.
«Indeed those who earn sin shall be requited»
«And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned»

— in that it died of itself or was slaughtered in the name of other than Him; otherwise, what a Muslim has slaughtered without pronouncing the name over it, whether deliberately or forgetfully, is lawful. Ibn ʿAbbās said this, and al-Shāfiʿī holds it.
— a going out from what is lawful —

(Q. 6:121) — like them. It was revealed concerning Abū Jahl and Ḥamza. The Prophet ﷺ was praying in the Sacred Mosque about the House, and a company of the chiefs of Quraysh were looking at him. They talked among themselves, and there was there dung and a foul stench which they found repugnant. One of them said: can any of you take some of that filth and put it on Muhammad while he is prostrate? ʿUqba b. Abī Muʿayṭ said: I can. So he took that foul thing — the afterbirth of a slaughtered camel, and dung — and placed it upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was prostrate. The unbelievers of Quraysh fell to laughing, laughing and mocking the Prophet ﷺ, rejoicing at that, until Fāṭima came to him

— the wont of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: the transgressors of Mecca were the great ones, and they were the criminals who showed enmity to al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ. So too you find in every town that the great ones are

— because the great ones are the ones who have wealth and standing in abundance, and whoever has this is more able to treachery and betrayal and wrongdoing than anyone else. Whoever has much wealth and has standing must needs be eager to increase his wealth and his standing, and that increase is not had except by every foul deed, such as hatred, envy, talebearing, backbiting and swearing by false oaths. All this they must needs acquire, to guard their leadership and out of eagerness to increase their wealth. For this reason they are the ones who are always occupied with harming the prophets of Allah and His
— because its evil consequence falls upon them; whatever plotting they do, the calamity comes back to them —
— of the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ —
«they say: we shall not believe until we are given the like of what the messengers of Allah were given»

— Abū Jahl b. Hishām said: our house and the house of Muhammad ﷺ were like two racehorses in the Jāhiliyya and down to this day of ours, and today Muhammad has taken to saying that he is a prophet, and we have no prophet. We shall never accept this, until a prophet like him comes forth from our house; otherwise
we shall not believe in him.
Supplication between the two Majestic Names (
) is answered, and this supplication has come soundly concerning it:

⟨O Allah, who is it that called upon You and You did not answer him? And who is it that sought refuge with You and You did not grant him refuge? And who is it that asked of You and You did not give him? And who is it that sought help of You and You did not⟩

⟨help him? And who is it that put his trust in You and You did not suffice him? O my succour, O my succour, O my succour! By You I seek succour, so succour me, O Succourer. Guide me with a guidance from You, and fulfil our needs, and heal our sick, and settle our debts, and forgive us and our fathers and our mothers, by the right of the Mighty Qurʾan and the Noble Messenger, by Your mercy, O most Merciful of the merciful.⟩
«Allah knows best where to place His message»
— Allah, Blessed and Exalted, knows who is deserving of the message, and so He gives it to him —
«There shall befall those who committed crimes»
«with Allah, and a severe punishment, for what they used to plot»
(Q. 6:124) — that is, because of their plotting.
«So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to submission»

— in that He casts a light into his heart, so that it opens to it and he accepts it, as has come in the hadith. The Messenger ﷺ told that when Allah wills to guide His servant He casts a light into his heart, and so his breast expands and he accepts the guidance of Allah. They said: ⟨Is there a sign of that, O Messenger of Allah?⟩ He said: ⟨Yes: withdrawing from the abode of delusion and making ready for the abode of the hereafter⟩ — renunciation of this world and turning towards Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
«And whomever He wills to lead astray, He makes his breast tight»
— when Allah wills to lead His servant astray He makes his breast too tight to accept anything —
— when he is charged with guidance it is as though he were charged with climbing to the sky —
«into the sky. Thus does Allah lay defilement upon those who do not believe»
— which you are upon, O Muhammad —
«is the path of your Lord, straight»
«the signs for a people who take heed»
(Q. 6:126) — because they are the ones who profit by it.
safety — and it is the Garden —
«with their Lord, and He is their protector by reason of what they used to do»
(Q. 6:127) — Allah, Blessed and Exalted, takes charge of their guidance. ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah Exalted be pleased with him, equipped an army of four thousand horsemen and sent them

to the land of the non-Arabs to fight. They went to a town and fought for many months, and their weapons did not reach the place of their enemy. There was a well-fortified stronghold, and its commander was a beautiful woman. The Companions were unable to take the stronghold and they remained a long while. Then she went up
one day upon her upper chamber, she looked at a young man among the Companions, and [then] she wept. The company said to her: What

makes you weep? You are in an impregnable fortress, and these Arabs have overrun all the lands and have been unable to take your fortress. What ails you that you weep? She said: I have seen a young man among the Companions who will certainly conquer this fortress of mine. It was said to her: By what means? She said to them: You will see presently. So she sent to him, saying: I must have you — how is the way to you? The young man said:

That you surrender the outer fortress to us and the inner fortress to our Lord. She sent to him and gave orders for the fortress to be opened. She said: The outer fortress — here it is, I have opened it to you; and the inner fortress, what is it? He said to her: You say, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and you surrender your heart to Allah. She said: Yes, but I am a great queen, and I would like, if I am to enter Islam, to submit before the greatest of you. You are a young lad; it is not fitting that you should be my guide. He said: Yes — ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, he is the commander of the army, he is our greatest. So she came to ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar, and when she stood before him she said: I would like one greater than you. Is there among the Muslims one greater than you? I shall not enter Islam save at the hands of the greatest of the Muslims. ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar said to her:

Yes — the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, is in Medina. So she set out for him, and the army with her, and they travelled until they reached Medina. When they stood before ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb she said to him: I shall not enter Islam save at the hands of the greatest of the Muslims. Is there one greater than you? ʿUmar said: Yes — this is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he is in his grave as though alive.
