She said to ʿUmar: Take me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; I shall not enter Islam save before him. So she stood before the Messenger ﷺ and said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. And she placed her hand on the threshold of the door of the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have entered Islam, and I would like not to

besmirch my Islam with anything of the transgressions hereafter. If Allah accepts my Islam, let Him take my spirit to Him now. And she died before ʿUmar, and ʿUmar wept a great weeping; so she was washed and shrouded, and he buried her at al-Baqīʿ!
At first she attached herself to an aim of the
(the soul), and that aim led her, by the loftiness of her
(spiritual resolve), until she reached what she reached.
«And He is their protector for what they used to do»
«O company of jinn, you have taken many of mankind»
«among mankind: Our Lord, we profited from one another»
— that is, mankind profited by the jinn's making the appetites alluring to them, and the jinn profited by mankind's obedience to them —
«and we have reached our term which You appointed for us»
— which is the Day of Resurrection; and this is an expression of regret from them —
— Exalted, upon the tongue of the angels —
⟨of the times in which they come out of it to drink the boiling water, for that is outside it, as He said:⟩
«Then indeed their return is to the Hellfire»
(Q. 37:68). And from Ibn ʿAbbās: that it concerns those of whom Allah knew that they would believe; so

(whoever) — that is, abiding therein except whom Allah wills, of those of the unbelievers who believed afterwards. This is the commentator's words, and the answer is not very satisfying. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, mentioned that the people of the Garden abide forever in the Garden and the people of the Fire abide forever in the Fire. What His name
(the First) entails is that He is before everything; and what His name
(the Last) entails is that He is after everything, without fail. And this name, with the attribute it comprises, must be manifested;
must be manifested. So if we are abiding forever, how is

manifested? And the people of the Garden continue in the Garden: whoever enters it never goes out of it, and the people of the Fire likewise never go out of it, as the Qurʾan has told. And the Qurʾan is true, and

must be manifested also. So what is the answer? The answer is that the people of the Garden continue in the bliss and rise higher in the bliss until they become absent in the bliss, until no sensation remains to them, and they return to the state they were in in pre-eternity. And the people of the Fire continue in the Fire after a severe punishment

and successive afflictions, ages upon ages. They must come to feel no pain, growing used to it, until they become absent in that, and return to the state they were in in pre-eternity. So pre-eternity must be manifested in post-eternity, and they will be in post-eternity as they were in pre-eternity. And this does not contradict the everlasting abiding (

) of the people of the Garden in the Garden, nor the everlasting abiding of the people of the Fire in the Fire. And it is thus: the states before their return to the state of pre-eternity are trials from

, Blessed and Exalted. The people of the Garden — He tries them with bliss until they return to a post-eternity like the pre-eternity; and the people of the Fire — painful trials and a severe punishment, all of it affliction, and it must come to an end one day, and so they return to the post-eternity which is the mirror of pre-eternity. This is what is possible.
— as We gave the disobedient of mankind and the jinn to enjoy one another —
«some of the wrongdoers of others, for what they used to earn»
«O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you»
— from your totality, which holds true of mankind; and the messengers of the jinn are their warners, who hear the speech of the messengers and convey it to their people —
«recounting to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this your day? They said: We bear witness against ourselves»
— they have indeed conveyed to us —
«And the life of this world deluded them»
«and they bore witness against themselves that they were unbelievers»
«is because your Lord would not destroy the towns for wrongdoing»
(Q. 6:131) — the sending of the messengers is necessary, as a proof against them.
«and your Lord is not unaware of what they do»
(Q. 6:132). People are of degrees: ulama, who are the heirs of the prophets; and rich men, who are
the trustees of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and ascetics

who are the leaders; and warriors who are the ones who wage jihad, the swords of Allah; and kings who are the shadows of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. If these five are upright, the conditions of the world are all upright. And if the ulama covet this world, and the ascetics desire it, and the warriors are ones who make a show of their deeds (

) is as nothing — and the rich, the merchants, are treacherous, and the kings are unjust: if the ulama covet this world, then who is to be followed, and by whom is one to be guided? And if the ascetics desire this world, then by whom is [Allah] to be pointed to? And if the merchants are traitors, then in whom is trust to be placed? And if the warriors make a show of their deeds,

then who will overcome the enemy? And if the kings are tyrants, then who is to shepherd [the people]? These are the ones who have corrupted this world and corrupted the world. Had they been sound, everything would have been sound; but they were corrupt and corrupted everything.
«And your Lord is not heedless of what they do»
— free of need of His creation and of their acts of worship —
«If He wills He can take you away»
— O people of Mecca, by destruction —
«and leave in succession after you whatever He wills»
«as He produced you from the seed of another people»

(Q. 6:133). He took them away, but He has kept you in being as a mercy to you. Had Allah willed, He would have destroyed the people, all of them, and brought others. This is His constant practice; there is no doubt in it, because we witness it constantly. If we reflect now upon fifty years ago, we find our fathers standing, governing this world; and here we are now, and nothing has remained of our fathers. And from here to fifty years hence you will not see one of us; our children will remain. So it is always.
«as He produced you from the seed of another people»
«Indeed what you are promised is surely coming»
— this is a proof that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it —
«Say: O my people, act according to your station»
«so you shall know for whom will be the end of the Abode»
— the praiseworthy end in the abode of the hereafter: is it we or you? —
«to Allah, of what He has produced»

— which they spend upon guests and the poor, and to their associate-gods a share which they spend upon their keepers. The unbelievers of Mecca used to divide their wealth into two portions: a thing of which they said that it belonged to Allah, Blessed and Exalted — if they found a guest they would entertain him, and they would give alms to the poor from something of it; and they assigned a thing to their gods as well, spent upon their keepers, for the service of the associate-gods.
«And they said: this is for Allah, by their claim»
— by their claim they said: this is Allah's share —

— and they would put it in a single store. If something fell from Allah's share over to the share of their gods, they would say: leave it, leave it, Allah is free of need. And if something fell from the share of their gods over to the side of Allah's share, they would say: give it back, give it back — and they would give it back. It is Allah who provided them the beasts and provided them the crops, and they assigned

to Him an associate. They divided between Him and His associate, and they were not just in the division. Since nothing remained but that they assign Him a share and another a share, it was their due to give Him His share in full; but
«what is for their associate-gods does not reach Allah»
— to His side: everything that fell from the side of their associate-gods to the side of Allah they gave back; they do not accept this —
«and what is for Allah, that does reach their associate-gods»
— and what was for Allah, if it fell upon the share of the associate-gods, they would say: leave it, Allah is free of need —
— as there was made alluring to them what has been
«there has been made alluring to many of the associators the killing of their children»
— likewise, out of the folly of the Jāhiliyya they used to kill their children by burying them alive —
«by their associate-gods, that they might destroy them»
«for them their religion. And had Allah willed they would not have done it. So leave them and what they fabricate»

(Q. 6:137). One of the unbelievers accepted Islam at the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and whenever he sat in the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ he sat downcast and grieving, always with his head covered. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke to him: what ails you, always grieving, after Allah has guided you to Islam? He said: I did a sin in the Jāhiliyya which I think Allah will not forgive me. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: and what is it? He said that he was ashamed to mention that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him and said to him: your sin is a paltry thing beside the pardon of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. He said to him: I was a man in the Jāhiliyya among those who hate daughters; whenever a daughter was born to me I killed her. Then a daughter was born to me, and her mother asked of me that I not kill her, and asked of me covenants and pledges, and I gave her covenants and pledges that I would not kill her — until she grew up and reached the age of women and became the most beautiful of the women of the world, and the men sought her in marriage. Satan entered into me, so that I was too proud that my daughter should be a wife to a man. So I asked her mother that she travel with me to visit some of the kin, and her mother rejoiced at that, and prepared for her every ornament and gown, and adorned her, and sent her with me. When we had gone to the middle of the road I turned aside with her to a well there, and I wanted to throw her into the well. She grew aware of that and said: O my father, do not kill me, do not kill me; and beware of betraying my mother after you made a covenant with her

and gave her covenants and pledges that you would not kill me. When I looked at her I had mercy on her, and when I looked to the fact that the men were seeking her in marriage I resolved upon killing her — until my

(the soul) overcame me, and I pushed her into the well, and she fell and cried out: you have killed me, O my father. I heard her weeping, and I sat around the well for days, until she grew cold and her voice was stilled and I knew that she had died; and I went away. When he reached this point the Prophet ﷺ wept and said: by Allah, were I to punish anyone for a sin he committed in the Jāhiliyya, I would punish you for this deed! The people of the Jāhiliyya used to do this.
These [verses] exposed the Jāhiliyya and described what they were upon of ignorance and folly.
«And they said: these are cattle and tilth that are forbidden»
«none may eat them save whom we will»
— of the keepers of the idols and others —
— they have no proof for it —
«and cattle whose backs have been forbidden»
— so they are not ridden, like the camels set loose by pagan vow (
) and the camels with slit ears dedicated to the idols (
«and cattle over which they do not mention the name of Allah»
— at their slaughter; rather they mention the name of their idols, and they ascribed that to Allah —
«as a fabrication against Him. He will requite them for what they used to fabricate»
«And they said: what is in the bellies of these cattle»
— the forbidden ones, and they are the camels set loose by vow and the camels with slit ears —
— it is permitted for the male to eat of the cattle of our gods —
— but it is forbidden for women to eat of the cattle of the gods —
— unless it dies of itself; if it is carrion, then carrion is lawful for the males and the females —
«then they are partners in it. He will requite them»
— that, by the declaring lawful and the declaring forbidden —
«Lost indeed are those who killed their children»
«without knowledge, and forbade what Allah provided them»
«fabricating against Allah. They have gone astray and they were not guided»
— spread out upon the ground, like melons and other such things —

— in that they rise upon a trunk, like the date palm. Allah produced for us orchards by which we live: among them what spreads out upon the ground, and among them what has a trunk, like the date palm.
— and He produced the date palm —
— its fruit and its grain, in form and in taste —
«and the olive and the pomegranate, alike»
«Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit»
and the zakat is a tenth or half of it.
— by giving the whole of it, so that nothing remains for your dependants —
«indeed He does not love the extravagant»
(Q. 6:141) — those who exceed what has been bounded for them. And He produced —
«and of the cattle [some] for carrying burdens»
— Allah created for us, of the kind of
cattle, beasts for carrying burdens, fit to be loaded upon, such as the large camels —
— not fit for it, such as the small camels and the sheep. The correct view is that
are such as the camels and the oxen, which are the ones fit for carrying, and
is what is not fit for carrying, such as the sheep.
«Eat of what Allah has provided you, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan»
— his ways in forbidding and permitting —
«indeed he is to you a manifest enemy»
— Allah produced for you eight kinds
— two mates, a male and a female; and of the goats, two mates —
— O Muhammad, to those who forbade the males of the cattle at one time and their females at another and ascribed that to Allah —
— of the sheep and the goats —
«or what the wombs of the two females contain»
— be it male or female? Which of these classes did He forbid: the males, or the females, or the offspring? —
— about how that forbidding came to be —

(Q. 6:143) — in it. The meaning is: whence did the prohibition come? If it was on account of maleness, then all males are forbidden; or of femaleness, then all females are forbidden; or of the womb's containing, then both of the pair are forbidden. So whence the restriction?
«And of camels two, and of oxen two. Say: is it the two males that He has forbidden, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses»
— the prohibition, so that you relied upon it? No; rather you are liars.
«than he who invents a lie against Allah»
«in order to lead people astray without knowledge? Indeed Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people»
«I do not find in what has been revealed to me»
— there is nothing in the Book of Allah forbidden save four things —
unlike what is other than it, such as the liver and the spleen —
«or the flesh of swine, for that is an abomination»
«or an ungodliness over which a name other than Allah's has been invoked»

— or a thing slaughtered for other than the name of Allah. There is nothing forbidden save these four. The verse of al-Baqara confirmed this, and it specified these four as well; and the verse of al-Māʾida confirmed it, and it enumerated the kinds of carrion:
«and the strangled, and the beaten to death, and the fallen, and the gored, and what a wild beast has eaten»
(Q. 5:3) — all of this falls under carrion.
— to something of what has been mentioned, and eats it —
«not desiring it nor transgressing, then your Lord is forgiving»
— to him for what he ate —
(Q. 6:145) — toward him. There is joined to what has been mentioned, by the sunna, every fanged beast of prey and every taloned bird.
— whatever does not have its toes parted, such as the camel and others —
«and of oxen and sheep We forbade them their fat»
— the caul-fat and the fat of the kidneys —
— that is, what clings to them of it —
— the intestines, the plural of ḥāwin or ḥāwiya —
— and that is the fat of the tail, for it was made lawful to them.
— on account of their wrongdoing, in what has preceded in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ —
(Q. 6:146) — in Our reports and Our promises.
«your Lord is possessed of a vast mercy»
— in that He has not hastened the punishment upon you; and in it is a gentleness in calling them to faith (
«and His might will not be turned back»
«Those who associated partners will say: Had»
«Allah willed, we would not have associated [partners with Allah]»
— the unbelievers say that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the one who willed their
(associating partners with Allah); this is true. We —
«nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything»

(Q. 6:148) — likewise our fathers, and likewise our forbidding: had Allah not willed that, it would not have been. This is true. And upon it they built a lie: that He is therefore content with it — since He is the one who willed it, He is content with it. This is a lie. They measured al-Ḥaqq, Blessed and Exalted, against the created being; for the created being wills nothing unless he is content with it, because he wills nothing except a thing in which there is a benefit for him. If he has a benefit in a thing, he wills that it should be. So his will and his contentment are joined together, because he is a seeker of benefit. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted — nothing comes to be except by His will; yet He wills a thing and is content with it, and He wills a thing and is not content with it.
«Had Allah willed, we would not have associated [partners with Allah]»
is by Allah's will, and disobedience is by Allah's will; but He was not content with this
«And He is not content with unbelief for His servants; and if you are grateful, He is content with it for you»
(Q. 39:7) — He willed it and was not content with it. So He has two addresses: the address of will and the address of wisdom (

). The address of will: nothing comes to be except a thing Allah has willed; and unbelief and the forbidden things and the acts of disobedience, all of these are by Allah's will — but He is not content with unbelief for His servants. And faith is by His will and obedience is by His will, and He is content with that. So they spoke a word (
) of truth and built a falsehood upon it.
«Had Allah willed, we would not have associated [partners with Allah], nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything»
— this is true; but that our
and our forbidding are by His will and that He is therefore content with it — this is a lie.
— that Allah is content with that —
«that you can bring it forth for us?»
«but conjecture, and you do nothing but guess»
«then to Allah belongs the conclusive argument»
(Q. 6:149). Had Allah willed, He would have guided all people; but He did not will it.

The people of faith and the people of guidance are fewer than others. And what is the wisdom in this? Faith is precious, and a thing, when it is scarce, is precious; and when it grows abundant with everyone it is not precious in people's eyes. So when Allah willed that there should be

faith precious and the believer precious, He made the believers fewer than the unbelievers. And also, so that His self-sufficiency and His freedom from need of anyone might appear. Allah is self-sufficient; were He in need of anything, He would have been in need of a multitude of Muslims and a multitude of believers. But since He is self-sufficient, a few of the people being Muslims suffices Him. Were the people unbelievers altogether, that would not harm Him; so He made few the Muslims, the people of faith, that He might show His freedom, in Himself, from need of anyone. And thirdly, that He might show His power: for the people of faith, who are the fewer — fewer in number (

) — and with that He is able to preserve them, so that the unbelievers do not harm them, many though they are. The unbelievers are more, and greater in number and in weapons and in knowledge and in stratagems; and the Muslims are few among them, weak; most of them are poor, most of them unlearned. And with this Allah preserved them, so that the unbelievers had no power over them in anything. Rather you find the unbelievers always fearing the Muslims, while the Muslims pay them no heed. If it be said that this contradicts what was mentioned yesterday,

(Q. 6:12) — if His mercy outstripped His wrath, and the unbelievers are more than the Muslims, then how does mercy prevail over wrath? Yes: the fewness of the Muslims is in relation to mankind and the jinn only. Otherwise the angels, all of them, and the wide-eyed maidens of Paradise (

) and the highest assembly are far more than mankind and the jinn, and they are all people of faith. In view of that, the people of mercy are more than the people of wrath; but the people of wrath are more among mankind and the jinn.
«your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden this»
«and if they testify, do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who have denied Our signs and those who do not believe in the hereafter, and they ascribe equals to their Lord»
. This which the unbelievers of Quraysh forbade, of the camels with slit ears dedicated to idols (
) and the camels set loose by pagan vow (
), is a lie and a fabrication. Now: come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you — He mentioned ten things —
. What Allah has made obligatory upon us is faith in Him alone, and that we associate nothing with Him.
(associating partners with Allah) is the greatest of the grave sins. The Messenger ﷺ was asked about the greatest
of the grave sins, and he said:
⟨That you associate anything with Allah when He created you, and that you be undutiful to your parents, and that you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife.⟩
Shirk is the greatest of the grave sins and the greatest of the ruinous sins.

— that is, be good to your parents with goodness. After shirk comes undutifulness to parents. So grave is undutifulness that He did not mention it: do not associate anything with Him — He did not say, and do not be undutiful, but rather, and be good to your parents with goodness. He so abhorred undutifulness that He did not even name it.
— on account of poverty. Likewise what the unbelievers used to commit, of killing the child for fear of poverty: do not do this, for Allah is the Provider.
«We provide for you and for them. And do not come near indecencies»
— the grave sins, such as fornication —
«what is outward of them and what is inward»
. Likewise, do not come near indecencies is more emphatic than do not commit them, because it is a grave sin and forbidden, and all that leads up to it is forbidden. The Messenger ﷺ says:

⟨The adultery of the two eyes is looking; and the adultery of the tongue is speech; and the adultery of the nose is the kiss; and the adultery of the two hands is touching; and the adultery of the heart is the soul's musing; and the adultery of the two feet is walking; and all of this the genitals either confirm or deny.⟩
If the genitals enter in, all these limbs have committed adultery; and if
they do not enter in, these limbs are safe — for Allah forgives the lesser sins through the avoidance of the grave sins.
«And do not come near indecencies, what is outward of them and what is inward»
«And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, save by right»

), the prescribed penalty for apostasy, and the stoning of one who has been married. Associating partners with Allah, undutifulness to parents, the killing of children, fornication, and the killing of the soul which Allah has forbidden save by right — these are five.
«He has enjoined upon you, that you may reason»

(Q. 6:151) — that you may ponder. And if you look into the things forbidden, all of them, you find them going back to killing; for if man were not forbidden the killing of the soul, killing would become frequent, as He said:
«And in retaliation there is life for you»
(Q. 2:179). And were fornication not forbidden, men would fight one another over women as the beasts and the cattle do; and man is stronger and greater in stratagem, so killing would occur in plenty.

And theft: whoever lays hands on a person's property exposes himself to being killed, for he may himself be killed. And since the Law has made amputation obligatory in theft, one whose hand has been cut off — that may well lead to his death. And the drinking of wine: whoever drinks wine becomes drunk and loses his reason, and perhaps he kills or
is killed without being aware. All the things forbidden go back to killing, and Allah does not love
killing, because He loves the continuance of the world, save what He wills.
«And do not come near the property of the orphan save in the way that is best»
— that is, what holds his welfare —

— by reaching puberty. Allah has forbidden guardians to consume the property of their orphans; let them keep it for them, and when they reach puberty and reach sound judgement let them hand over to them their property. There was one of the righteous who had memorised the Book of Allah and was always writing out the written codex (

). He said that he had written forty codices. He would see the fly perhaps drinking from the ink upon the writing — except from this word: he never saw a fly drink from it, out of fear of the orphan's property. And learning from an orphan's books is permitted in the view of most of the ulama, though some of them have forbidden it.
«And give full measure and weight with equity»
— when you measure for people, or weigh for them, be just, and do not short people in their things —
«and We do not charge a soul save with its capacity»
— its ability. For if he errs in the measure and the weight, and Allah knows the soundness of his intention, then there is no

reckoning against him, as has come in the hadith. And a man, if he reflects on the manner of weighing, finds within himself an admonisher that restrains him from short measure and deficiency. The manner of weighing is thus: the weigher commonly folds these two fingers and extends the three — and this is “Allah” — as though the weigher's hand were always addressing him: Allah, Allah, Allah, Allah. And the severest thing with which the servant is punished in his grave is short measure and deficiency in the measure. There was a man who was always occupied with measuring and weighing; and when his death drew near they prompted him with the two testimonies of faith (

), and he began to say: Two mountains of fire, two mountains of fire. Two mountains of fire upon his tongue kept him from pronouncing the two testimonies — and that was the tongue of the balance with which he used to weigh. And whoever recites the Qurʾan much and accustoms himself to the remembrance of Allah may well merit a good end. There was a man who used to recite the Qurʾan much; and when death came to him, whenever he was told, there is no god but Allah, he would say:
«Ṭā Hā. We have not sent down the Qurʾan upon you that you should be distressed»
«Allah — there is no god but He; to Him belong the most beautiful names»

(Q. 20:8). He kept repeating this until he died. And there was one who used to sell the foul weed, and who was always saying: A bundle for a fals, a bundle for a fals, a bundle for a fals. And when death came to him, whenever he was told, say: there is no god but Allah, he said: A bundle for a fals, a bundle for a fals — and he died upon that. And there was a devout young man in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. When death came to him they prompted him with the word of the testimony, and he was unable to
pronounce it. So the Prophet ﷺ came and prompted him, and he was not able to pronounce it. He said to the Companions:
⟨What do you know of his deeds?⟩
They said: We know nothing but good — and they praised him well. The Prophet ﷺ pondered and said:
They said: Yes, his mother is living. So he called for his mother:
⟨Are you pleased with this son of yours?⟩
She said: No; may Allah not pardon him, and may Allah not forgive him. The Messenger ﷺ said to her:
⟨If you pardon him he will pronounce the word and enter the Garden; and if you do not pardon him, this is the cause of his wretchedness.⟩
She said: I will never pardon him.
So the Messenger ﷺ called for firewood and kindled a fire and said:
⟨Carry him and put him into the fire.⟩

And when they carried him and were about to put him into the fire, she said: I have pardoned him, I have pardoned him. And he pronounced the two testimonies. The right of parents! The Messenger ﷺ knew that she would not be content to see her son devoured by the fire.
— in a judgement or in other than it —
— the one spoken for or against —
«And fulfil the covenant of Allah. That He has enjoined upon you, that perhaps you may remember»
— which I have enjoined upon you —
— this is the straight path of Allah —
«so follow it, and do not follow the [other] ways»
— the roads that differ from it —
«That He has enjoined upon you, that perhaps you may guard against evil»
(Q. 6:153). The Prophet ﷺ drew a line with his hand and then said:
⟨This is the path of Allah, straight.⟩
And he drew lines to its right and to its left and then said:
⟨These are the ways; there is not one of them but upon it is a devil calling to it.⟩
«And that this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow the [other] ways, lest they scatter you from His way»
(Q. 6:153). And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, forbade the community to split apart in matters of belief, because the way of truth is one, and the ways
that branch off it are all of them the ways of Satan.

⟨The Jews split into seventy-one sects, all of them in the Fire; and the Christians split into seventy-two sects, all of them in the Fire; and my community will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire save one: that which I and my Companions are upon.⟩
That is, the Sunna and the Community (
(then) is for the ordering of the telling, not of the events —
«and a guidance and a mercy, that perhaps they»
«is a Book We have sent down, blessed»
— abundant in good, abundant in benefits in this world and in religion —
— O people of Mecca, follow this Book by acting upon what is in it —
«that perhaps you may be shown mercy»

(Q. 6:155). And of its blessing is that the endurance of this world is by the endurance of the Qurʾan. So long as the Qurʾan is recited, the rains and the plants and the offspring are not cut off. And when the Qurʾan is raised up, until none remains who has memorised it, and it is effaced from the written codices (
), the world remains without good until the Hour rises upon them. And guard against unbelief, that perhaps you may be shown mercy.
«was the Book sent down upon two parties»
— their reading, that is, their tongue —

(Q. 6:156). Had the Qurʾan not been sent down, this community would have had an argument, and they would have said: the Books were sent down upon the Jews and the Christians, and we do not know how to read them. This argument was voided by the sending down of the Qurʾan in their own tongue.
«Or lest you say: had the Book been sent down upon us, we would have been better guided than they»

— had the Qurʾan not been sent down, the Arabs would have said that they are keener of mind than the non-Arabs, and that had a Book come to them they would have been granted of guidance what the others were not granted —
«For a clear proof has come to you»
«from your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy»
— and now this Qurʾan is before you in your own tongue. So what do you say? —
«than he who denies the signs of Allah and turns away from them»
«We shall requite those who turn away from Our signs with an evil punishment»
(Q. 6:157) — they turn away from the Qurʾan.
— do the deniers of the Qurʾan await anything —
«but that the angels should come to them»
— that is, His command, that is, His punishment —
«or that some of the signs of your Lord should come»
— that is, His marks that point to the Hour —
«on the day some of the signs of your Lord come»
— and it is the rising of the sun from its place of setting, as in the hadith of the two Ṣaḥīḥs —
«no soul will be benefited by its faith that had not believed before»
(Q. 6:158). They await, in their persistence in error and misguidance, the coming of the Hour. The Messenger ﷺ says:
⟨The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the smoke⟩
— and it is this smoke with which the states are now occupied. The Hour will not come until you see the smoke. All the states now are occupied with smoke, a smoke that annihilates the world —
⟨and the beast of the earth, and a sinking⟩

⟨in the east and a sinking in the west, and Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj, and the Dajjāl, and the descent of ʿĪsā b. Maryam, and the rising of the sun from its place of setting, and a fire that comes forth from Aden.⟩

These are the signs of the rising of the Hour. Some of them have appeared and some of them have not yet appeared. As for the smoke, it is this smoke with which the states are now occupied. And a sinking in the east and a sinking in the west — all this has occurred time and again. And Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj are two great non-Arab states, by which the destruction of the state of the Arabs comes about, and the destruction of the states will be at their hands as well. Now their remnants are from China and Indochina; these are of the remnants of Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj, and the destruction of Europe will inevitably be at the hand of these. These states in time past are the ones that destroyed the state of the Arabs in the time of the Abbasids. The Tatars are of them, and their remnants are these states that have been named to you, and they will destroy Europe before anything else. And Yaʾjūj

and Maʾjūj are the greatest trial for the Muslims; likewise the Dajjāl, and the descent of ʿĪsā, and the coming forth of the Beast, and the rising of the sun from the west. And they mentioned the Mahdī in some of the hadiths

And the signs such that, if anything of them appears, we know that the great change in the world has occurred, are the descent of ʿĪsā, and the appearance of the Dajjāl, and the rising of the sun from the west. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, accepts the repentance of the servant so long as he has not come to the death-rattle, so long as the door of repentance has not been shut. ʿUmar said:
⟨Yes — a door the length of whose two leaves is a distance of forty years.⟩
No one knows what the meaning of this
the things, or when they will come to pass.
«or earned good in its faith. Say: Wait; indeed we are waiting»
— by their disagreeing over it, so that they took part of it and left part —
— parties in that; they left their religion which they had been commanded to follow, and they are the Jews and the Christians; or they split apart and became party upon party —
«you are not of them in anything»
— so do not concern yourself with them —
(Q. 6:159) — and so He will requite them for it. And this is abrogated by the verse of the sword.
«for him is tenfold the like of it»
(Q. 6:160), for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, writes ten for him. This is the Jalāl's
(Qurʾanic commentary), and what is correct is that it remain upon its apparent sense: every good deed enters into this, on the evidence of the hadith. The Messenger ﷺ said:

⟨Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has prescribed mercy upon Himself. So whoever among you intends a good deed and does not do it, a good deed is written for him as though he had done it; and whoever intends an evil deed and does not do it, it is not written against him; and whoever does one evil deed⟩
«And the requital of an evil is an evil like it»
⟨and whoever does a good deed, for him is tenfold the like of it, or up to seven hundredfold, or up to more than that.⟩
That is because the soul that incites to evil — Allah has so described it — and the soul is like foul ground while the heart is like good ground. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says:
«And the good land — its vegetation comes forth by the leave of its Lord; and that which is foul brings forth only scantily»
(Q. 7:58). For this reason the doing of good issues from the heart, and its vegetation comes forth by the leave of its Lord multiplied; and the deed of
the soul that incites to evil comes forth from foul ground; it brings forth only scantily. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down this verse,
«Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is tenfold the like of it»
«The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is as the likeness of a grain that brings forth seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains»
(Q. 2:261) — this is seven hundred. The Messenger ﷺ said:
«Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan, that He may multiply it for him many times over»
(Q. 2:245) — many times over, more than seven hundred. The Messenger ﷺ said:
«The steadfast will be paid their reward without reckoning»
(Q. 39:10) — without limit of number. So he said:

And that is a great hope for the community. The wisdom in that is that the person of a human being is soul, heart, spirit and innermost secret, just as the ranks of numbers among the people of arithmetic are four ranks: the place of units, the place of tens, the place of hundreds and the place of thousands. If you multiply one in the position of units, it is one only; and if you put it in the position of tens, it becomes ten; and if you put it in the position of hundreds, it becomes a hundred; and if you put it in the position of thousands, it becomes a thousand. So whoever does an evil deed, this is from the place of the soul, which is the place of units: an evil like it,
«the requital of an evil is an evil like it»

(Q. 42:40), only that. And whoever comes with a good deed, this is from the place of the heart, so for him is tenfold the like of it, because he has multiplied one in the place of tens. And if he multiplies in the place of the spirit, his requital is hundreds, because that is the place of hundreds. And if it is in the place of the innermost secret, his requital is thousands, because this is the place of thousands. So it is upon us to do good, and Allah will requite us manifold over. And in truth,
«comes with a good deed, for him is tenfold the like of it»

(Q. 6:160). The servant, when he offers a single good deed, has from Allah tenfold the like of it before he offers one. Allah has offered us the good deed of bringing into being — He brought us into existence out of nothing; and the good deed of readiness — He made us ready for work; and the good deed of upbringing — when we were born He entrusted our fathers with our rearing until we came to reason; and the good deed of sending the messengers; and the good deed of sending down the books; and the good deed of making clear the good deed and the evil deed; and the good deed of sincerity (
); and the good deed of guidance; and the good deed of enabling grace; and the good deed of acceptance. He did ten before we did one.
«Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is tenfold the like of it»
— He offered us ten before we offered one.
«And whoever comes with an evil deed is not requited save with the like of it»
«And the requital of an evil is an evil like it»
(Q. 6:160) — they will not be diminished anything of their requital. The Messenger ﷺ says:
⟨Woe to him whose units overcome his tens.⟩

When he does an evil deed it is written once, and when he does a good deed it is written ten times or more. Moreover, the one who is on the servant's right and takes charge of writing the good deeds is the commander over the one who is on the servant's left. So when he does a good deed, he orders it written on the spot; and when he does an evil deed, he tells him to delay writing it for six hours, perhaps he will repent, or seek forgiveness, or one of Allah's righteous servants will intercede for him, or he will do some good, another good deed:
«Indeed good deeds drive away evil deeds»

(Q. 11:114). So if anything of that occurs within the span of six hours, his evil deed is not written; but if he is heedless of everything until six hours have passed, it is written once — the generosity of Allah. And when the servant is heedless until the units
of which some part is not recorded are more than the tens, then this one is heedless indeed.
«Say: Indeed my Lord has guided me to a straight path»
— say, O Muhammad: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has guided you to a straight path, which is Islam —
— it is the religion of Ibrāhīm —
«inclining to the truth, and he was not of those who associate partners»

gave his whole self to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and Allah said that he was not of those who associate partners. Ibrāhīm surrendered his wealth to the guests, and surrendered his children to the sacrifice, and surrendered himself to the flames, and the fire was coolness and peace upon him; it found no way to him.
«Say: Indeed my prayer and my rite of sacrifice»
— my worship, of hajj and other than it —
«are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner»
«I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit»
«Say: Shall I seek a lord other than Allah»
— a deity; I shall never seek other than Him —
«when He is the Lord of everything»
«save against itself; and shall not bear»
(Q. 6:164). The soul bears only its own burden. In this, if there is in it a semblance of contradiction between His word
«And they shall surely bear their own burdens, and burdens along with their burdens»
(Q. 29:13) and his word, upon him be blessings and peace,
⟨Whoever institutes an evil practice bears its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection⟩

— then how are these two to be brought together? A man, when he has not done a sinful deed, nor commanded it, nor been a cause of its being done, it is not written against him. As for His word, Exalted,
«And they shall surely bear their own burdens, and burdens along with their burdens»
— that is because they led these others astray and drove them to committing what is forbidden, and for this reason it was written
⟨whoever institutes an evil practice bears its burden and the burden of whoever acts by it until the Day of Resurrection⟩
, because they point the way to this. And whoever does not point the way, and does not command it, and is not a cause of its being done — he is the one of whom His word holds true:
«And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of that wherein you used to differ»
«And it is He who has made you»
(vicegerent); each of you succeeds another therein —
«and has raised some of you above others in degrees»
— some of them find wealth, and some of them find rank, and some of them find nothing of that —
— so that the obedient among you and the disobedient may be made manifest —
«indeed your Lord is swift in punishment»

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made plain that He made the children of Ādam vicegerents in the earth. Every human being is a vicegerent on behalf of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, upon the face of the earth, over a portion of this world. Ādam was made a vicegerent in the earth, and he is the father of mankind: Allah created him and made him a vicegerent. The Qurʾan has made explicit mention of the vicegerency (

) of no servant among the servants of Allah except the vicegerency of Ādam and the vicegerency of Dāwūd. Both of them took fright at the vicegerency, so that the letters of the name of each were separated.

: no letter touches the next. This is because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made explicit mention of the vicegerency of them both. And every human being is a vicegerent, because Allah is the Lord of [all] things, and every one of us is lord of something, though it be little and though it be small. For this reason Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said
«And We have certainly honoured the children of Ādam»

(Q. 17:70) — He honoured them by making them vicegerents in the world. All created things are the possession of the children of Ādam, and they are the vicegerents of Allah upon this wide earth. So you find that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has addressed none but human beings, and has laid obligation upon none but them, and has promised none but them, and has threatened none but them, and has sent the messengers to none but them, and has sent down the books to none but them. When He is pleased with them He honours them with an honouring beyond which there is no increase, and when He is angry with them He makes war upon them and punishes them with a severe punishment.
Since every one of the children of Ādam is a vicegerent in the earth, the believers are so all the more.
«Allah has promised those of you who believe»
«and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them vicegerents in the earth, as He made vicegerents of those who were before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion»
«which He has approved for them, and that He will surely exchange for them, after their fear, security»
(Q. 24:55). He promised us this and He fulfilled it for us. The community of Muhammad

ﷺ — Allah made this come true among them, until they ruled all the lands. They had no geometry, and they had no arithmetic, and they had no science of medicine. Among them was the man who had suras of the Qurʾan, or verses, which he kept in memory — but he believed in it truly, and complied with its commands, and avoided its prohibitions. Today the Muslims have entered into every science: they have taken up the science of arithmetic, and they have taken up the science of geometry, and they have taken up the science of history, they have taken up the science of everything — and they have abandoned their Book, a small part of which, were they to memorize it and act by it, would guarantee them the return to their ancient glory and their former might. They have abandoned the matter where it stands and have sought it in other than its place. The way back to what we aspire to is to hold fast to this Book and to act by it, as our forebears did, the Companions of the Messenger ﷺ, ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb and those who followed him. Today the Muslims are more in number and greater in learning, and the signs of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that appear in this age are more than in any age. Sulaymān — Allah subjected the wind to him:
«its morning course was a month and its evening course a month»

(Q. 34:12). And now Allah has subjected the air to the community of Muhammad entire: all of them fly and go wherever they wish. Faith had a right to increase by this, but it did not increase. And Dāwūd — iron was made pliant for him; and for the community of Muhammad everything has been made pliant: iron, and fire, and the sea, and the air, and everything — they dispose of it as they please now. But faith has not risen; it has not increased. They have ridden the seas, and they have ridden the air, and they have ridden the land,
and they have found the good things, and the treasuries of the earth have been opened to them. All of this had a right to call them to guidance

and to an increase of faith; but this has not come about. Matter has done away with spirit. I call for a return to the Book of Allah and for holding fast to it — that we seek to understand it, and comply with its command, and avoid its prohibition, so that we may be like those who went before us among the Companions of the Messenger ﷺ.
